    <section class="intro">
    
This page documents production updates to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). You can
periodically check this page for announcements about new or updated features,
bug fixes, known issues, and deprecated functionality.</p>

<p>This page includes release notes for all
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/release-channels">channels</a>
and releases.</p>

<h2 id="current_versions" data-text="Current versions" tabindex="-1">Current versions</h2>

<p>The following table lists the current versions for each <a href="/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/release-channels">release
channel</a>. To learn more about
the designations in this table, see <a href="/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/release-channels#what_versions_are_available_in_a_channel">What versions are available in a
channel</a>.
For general information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE
versioning and support</a> and <a href="/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About
GKE cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

<table class="">
  <thead>
  <tr>
    <th>GKE Release Channel</th>
    <th>Rapid</th>
    <th>Regular</th>
    <th>Stable</th>
    <th>Extended</th>
    <th>No Channel (Static)</th>
  </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>Available minor versions</td>
    <td>1.32 to 1.36</td>
    <td>1.32 to 1.35</td>
    <td>1.32 to 1.35</td>
    <td>1.30 to 1.35</td>
    <td>1.32 to 1.35</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Recommended auto-upgrade target</td>
    <td>1.35.3-gke.1522000</td>
    <td>1.35.3-gke.1234000</td>
    <td>1.33.9-gke.1060000</td>
    <td>1.30.14-gke.2320000</td>
    <td>1.33.9-gke.1060000</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Auto-upgrade targets</td>
    <td><ul><li>1.32.13-gke.1362000</li><li>1.33.11-gke.1013000</li><li>1.34.6-gke.1307000</li><li>1.35.3-gke.1522000</li><li>1.36.0-gke.1379000</li></ul></td>
    <td><ul><li>1.32.13-gke.1258000</li><li>1.33.10-gke.1115000</li><li>1.34.6-gke.1154000</li><li>1.35.3-gke.1234000</li></ul></td>
    <td><ul><li>1.32.13-gke.1059000</li><li>1.33.9-gke.1060000</li><li>1.34.5-gke.1076000</li><li>1.35.2-gke.1269001</li></ul></td>
    <td><ul><li>1.30.14-gke.2320000</li><li>1.31.14-gke.1723000</li><li>1.32.13-gke.1258000</li><li>1.33.10-gke.1115000</li><li>1.34.6-gke.1154000</li><li>1.35.3-gke.1234000</li></ul></td>
    <td><ul><li>1.32.13-gke.1258000</li><li>1.33.9-gke.1060000</li><li>1.34.6-gke.1154000</li><li>1.35.3-gke.1234000</li></ul></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Default patch version for cluster creation</td>
    <td>1.35.3-gke.1522000</td>
    <td>1.35.3-gke.1234000</td>
    <td>1.33.9-gke.1060000</td>
    <td>1.35.3-gke.1234000</td>
    <td>1.35.3-gke.1234000</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>COS version of default patch version</td>
    <td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125#cos-125-19216-220-130_">cos-125-19216-220-130</a></td>
    <td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125#cos-125-19216-220-72_">cos-125-19216-220-72</a></td>
    <td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m121#cos-121-18867-381-14_">cos-121-18867-381-14</a></td>
    <td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125#cos-125-19216-220-72_">cos-125-19216-220-72</a></td>
    <td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125#cos-125-19216-220-72_">cos-125-19216-220-72</a></td>
  </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<p>For information on the current minor versions rollout and support schedule, see
the <a href="/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-schedule">GKE release
schedule</a>. To find all the patch
versions available in a channel, <a href="/kubernetes-engine/versioning#available_versions">check available and default
versions</a>.</p>

<p>This table also lists the Container-Optimized OS version that corresponds
to the channel&#39;s default patch version. To upgrade a cluster to a specific image
version, see <a href="/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/node-images#map-gke-cos">Map Container-Optimized OS node image versions to
GKE patch
versions</a>.</p>

<h2 id="other_resources" data-text="Other resources" tabindex="-1">Other resources</h2>

<p>For more detailed information about security-related known issues, see the
<a href="/kubernetes-engine/docs/security-bulletins">security bulletin</a> page.</p>

<p>To view release notes for versions prior to 2020, see the
<a href="/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes-archive">Release notes archive</a>.</p>

<h2 id="April_29_2026" data-text="April 29, 2026" tabindex="-1">April 29, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r17-version-updates" data-text="(2026-R17) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R17) Version updates</h4>



<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

<div>
<devsite-selector>
<section>
  <h3 id="rapid-channel" data-text="Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Rapid channel</h3>
  <aside class="note"><strong>Note</strong>: Your clusters might not have these versions available.
Rollouts are already in progress when we publish the release notes, and can take
multiple days to complete across all Google Cloud zones.</aside>
  

<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.35.md#v1353">1.35.3-gke.1522000</a> is now the default version for cluster creation in the Rapid channel.</li>
<li>The following versions are now available in the Rapid channel:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.32.md#v13213">1.32.13-gke.1407000</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.33.md#v13311">1.33.11-gke.1074000</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.34.md#v1347">1.34.7-gke.1055000</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.35.md#v1353">1.35.3-gke.1737000</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.36.md#v1360">1.36.0-gke.1379000</a></li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following versions are no longer available in the Rapid channel:
<ul>
<li>1.32.13-gke.1090000 is <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning#patch-version-support">deprecated</a> in the Rapid channel. This version will be removed in 90 days, or at the end of support, if sooner.</li>
<li>1.32.13-gke.1147000 is <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning#patch-version-support">deprecated</a> in the Rapid channel. This version will be removed in 90 days, or at the end of support, if sooner.</li>
<li>1.32.13-gke.1205000</li>
<li>1.32.13-gke.1258000</li>
<li>1.32.13-gke.1318000</li>
<li>1.33.9-gke.1117000 is <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning#patch-version-support">deprecated</a> in the Rapid channel. This version will be removed in 90 days, or at the end of support, if sooner.</li>
<li>1.33.9-gke.1166000 is <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning#patch-version-support">deprecated</a> in the Rapid channel. This version will be removed in 90 days, or at the end of support, if sooner.</li>
<li>1.33.10-gke.1067000</li>
<li>1.33.10-gke.1115000</li>
<li>1.33.10-gke.1176000</li>
<li>1.34.5-gke.1153000 is <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning#patch-version-support">deprecated</a> in the Rapid channel. This version will be removed in 90 days, or at the end of support, if sooner.</li>
<li>1.34.5-gke.1208000 is <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning#patch-version-support">deprecated</a> in the Rapid channel. This version will be removed in 90 days, or at the end of support, if sooner.</li>
<li>1.34.6-gke.1068000</li>
<li>1.34.6-gke.1154000</li>
<li>1.34.6-gke.1237000</li>
<li>1.35.2-gke.1485000</li>
<li>1.35.2-gke.1842000 is <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning#patch-version-support">deprecated</a> in the Rapid channel. This version will be removed in 90 days, or at the end of support, if sooner.</li>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r17-security-updates" data-text="(2026-R17) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R17) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

<p>

<table>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>Container-Optimized OS version</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.31.14-gke.1823000</td>
<td>cos-117-18613-534-80</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m117#cos-117-18613-534-80_">cos-117-18613-534-80 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.36.0-gke.1379000</td>
<td>cos-125-19216-220-130</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125#cos-125-19216-220-130_">cos-125-19216-220-130 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>In GKE versions earlier than 1.34.6-gke.1154000 and
1.35.2-gke.1691000, mounting Cloud Storage buckets by using the
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cloud-storage-fuse-csi-driver">Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver</a>
can experience significant delays. This issue typically manifests as a
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">CreateContainer error</code> that states the following message:
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">failed to reserve container name</code>. This error is self-healing and resolves
automatically after the underlying mount operation completes and the container
runtime releases the reservation.</p>

<p>The delay is caused by an inefficient bucket access check performed by the
CSI driver sidecar by using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ListObjects</code> API method, which can take
several hours to complete on buckets that contain millions of empty folders.</p>

<p>The error occurs because the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubelet</code> enforces a strict two-minute timeout
for the container creation request. If the FUSE mount process exceeds this
time limit while the sidecar is performing the initial bucket access check,
then the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubelet</code> cancels the operation and retries. However, the container
runtime remains blocked on the first attempt and retains the reservation for
the container name.</p>

<p>The new GKE releases fix this issue by replacing the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">ListObjects</code> check with the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">GetStorageLayout</code> API method, which performs
the same validation but returns almost instantly in most cases.</p>

<p>To resolve this issue, upgrade your cluster to one of the following versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.34.6-gke.1154000 or later</li>
<li>1.35.2-gke.1691000 or later</li>
</ul>

<p>For GKE version 1.33 clusters running version 1.33.5-gke.2435000
or later, you can mitigate this issue by setting the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">skipCSIBucketAccessCheck: &quot;true&quot;</code> volume attribute to bypass the check.</p>

<p>There is no supported fix for this issue in cluster versions
1.33.5-gke.2435000 and earlier.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="April_21_2026" data-text="April 21, 2026" tabindex="-1">April 21, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>For clusters running GKE version 1.35.3-gke.1389000 or later,
you can now use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">c4a-highmem-96-metal</code>
(<a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>) machine
type from the C4A machine series with the following features:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/autopilot-overview">Autopilot</a> mode</li>
<li><a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/node-auto-provisioning#cluster-level-enablement">Node auto-provisioning</a></li>
<li><a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-compute-classes">ComputeClasses</a>
that auto-create node pools</li>
<li><a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-autoscaler">Cluster autoscaling</a></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Starting in GKE version 1.35.2-gke.1842000, you can install
the Slurm Operator add-on for GKE (<a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>).
This managed installation of the Slurm Operator allows you to enable Slurm
scheduling capabilities on any GKE cluster. The add-on provides
the foundation to build customized AI and HPC platforms, including CPU, GPU,
and TPU machines (covering specific scenarios). For more information, see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/slurm-on-gke/concepts/overview">About Slurm on GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_20_2026" data-text="April 20, 2026" tabindex="-1">April 20, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Accelerator network profile is Generally Available (GA), simplifying your
AI/ML node pool setup. Accelerator network profile automates networking
configuration, including the creation of necessary VPCs and subnets, removing
the need for complex, manual steps previously required for configuring
GPU and TPU workloads. For details, see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/config-auto-net-for-accelerators">Configure automated networking for accelerator VMs</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="April_13_2026" data-text="April 13, 2026" tabindex="-1">April 13, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The validation of the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">HealthCheckPolicy</code> custom resource from the
GKE Gateway API is more rigorous in GKE
version 1.34 and later. Existing <code translate="no" dir="ltr">HealthCheckPolicy</code> resources that already
contain mismatched type fields in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">config</code> are exempted and continue to
function. However, updates to any existing policy must not introduce a
mismatched type field in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">config</code> or change currently mismatched
fields to new invalid values.</p>

<p>When the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">HealthCheckPolicy</code> custom resource is validated, the type field
is now verified against the specified health check. For example, if
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">type: TCP</code> is specified but <code translate="no" dir="ltr">httpHealthCheck</code> is configured, then the fields
are mismatched and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl</code> rejects the policy. However, for this same example,
if <code translate="no" dir="ltr">type: TCP</code> is specified and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">tcpHealthCheck</code> is configured, then the
fields are valid.</p>

<p>Earlier versions of GKE accept custom resources that don&#39;t have matching fields. If you use an earlier version, the type field is used
and the configuration in the health check field is ignored.</p>

<p>For more details, see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-gateway-resources#configure_health_check">Configure health checks</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="April_08_2026" data-text="April 08, 2026" tabindex="-1">April 08, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p><span id="logging-agent-change-20260408"></span></p>

<p>The feature announced on <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#November_07_2025">November 7, 2025</a>,
providing faster log processing, has been rolled back. The rollback is due
to an issue in an underlying dependency. The described performance
improvements are not currently in effect.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/tag/v1.5.0">Gateway API v1.5</a>
is supported in GKE version 1.35.2-gke.1842000 and later.
The GKE Gateway controller passes core conformance tests for
this version of the Gateway API.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE managed DRANET is now Generally Available (GA)
for GKE version 1.35.2-gke.1842000 or later.</p>

<p>GKE DRANET is a managed feature that implements the
Kubernetes Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) API for high-performance
networking. The GA release expands support beyond the preview phase to
include the following hardware:</p>

<ul>
<li>NVIDIA GPU Instances: Support for instances starting from A3 Ultra, including A4, A4X, and A4X Max.</li>
<li>Cloud TPU Instances: Support for TPU v6e and TPU v7x.</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/allocate-network-resources-dra">Allocate network resources by using GKE managed DRANET</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r13-security-updates" data-text="(2026-R13) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R13) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

<p>

<table>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>Container-Optimized OS version</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.30.14-gke.2286000</td>
<td>cos-117-18613-534-44</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m117#cos-117-18613-534-44_">cos-117-18613-534-44 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.31.14-gke.1681000</td>
<td>cos-117-18613-534-44</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m117#cos-117-18613-534-44_">cos-117-18613-534-44 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.32.13-gke.1205000</td>
<td>cos-117-18613-534-44</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m117#cos-117-18613-534-44_">cos-117-18613-534-44 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.33.10-gke.1067000</td>
<td>cos-121-18867-381-45</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m121#cos-121-18867-381-45_">cos-121-18867-381-45 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.34.6-gke.1068000</td>
<td>cos-125-19216-220-72</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125#cos-125-19216-220-72_">cos-125-19216-220-72 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

</p></div>

      <div><h4 id="2026-r12-version-updates" data-text="(2026-R12) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R12) Version updates</h4>



<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r12-security-updates" data-text="(2026-R12) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R12) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

<p>

<table>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>Container-Optimized OS version</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.30.14-gke.2250000</td>
<td>cos-117-18613-534-36</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m117#cos-117-18613-534-36_">cos-117-18613-534-36 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.31.14-gke.1634000</td>
<td>cos-117-18613-534-36</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m117#cos-117-18613-534-36_">cos-117-18613-534-36 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.32.13-gke.1147000</td>
<td>cos-117-18613-534-24</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m117#cos-117-18613-534-24_">cos-117-18613-534-24 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.33.9-gke.1166000</td>
<td>cos-121-18867-381-24</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m121#cos-121-18867-381-24_">cos-121-18867-381-24 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>To provide more controls over the control plane version upgrade, you can now do
the following:</p>

<ul>
<li>Configure a frequency of disruption from auto-upgrades by using the cluster
disruption budget. For more information, see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cluster-disruption-budget">Control the frequency of disruption from auto-upgrades</a>.</li>
<li>Continue using an existing control plane patch for a longer period, which
facilitates large-scale upgrade and downgrade operations. For more
information, see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning#patch-version-support">Patch version support</a>.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_18_2026" data-text="March 18, 2026" tabindex="-1">March 18, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r11-version-updates" data-text="(2026-R11) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R11) Version updates</h4>



<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r11-security-updates" data-text="(2026-R11) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R11) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

<p>

<table>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>Container-Optimized OS version</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.34.5-gke.1153000</td>
<td>cos-125-19216-220-57</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125#cos-125-19216-220-57_">cos-125-19216-220-57 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.35.2-gke.1485000</td>
<td>cos-125-19216-220-57</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125#cos-125-19216-220-57_">cos-125-19216-220-57 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_13_2026" data-text="March 13, 2026" tabindex="-1">March 13, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.35 and later, all organization and cluster
 administrators can granularly control which privileged Autopilot
 partner workloads can run in GKE clusters. Additionally,
 approved customers can authorize and run their own privileged workloads in
 Autopilot mode by using custom allowlists.</p>

<p>For more information, see
 <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-autopilot-privileged-workloads">About Autopilot privileged  workloads</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_12_2026" data-text="March 12, 2026" tabindex="-1">March 12, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r10-version-updates" data-text="(2026-R10) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R10) Version updates</h4>



<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r10-security-updates" data-text="(2026-R10) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R10) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

<p>

<table>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>Container-Optimized OS version</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.30.14-gke.2192000</td>
<td>cos-117-18613-534-15</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m117#cos-117-18613-534-15_">cos-117-18613-534-15 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m117#cos-117-18613-534-15_">cos-117-18613-534-15 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m117#cos-117-18613-534-15_">cos-117-18613-534-15 release notes</a></td>

</p></div>

<h2 id="March_10_2026" data-text="March 10, 2026" tabindex="-1">March 10, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Managed OpenTelemetry for GKE is available in Preview for
clusters running version 1.34.1-gke.2178000 or later. Managed OpenTelemetry for
GKE provides a fully managed and simplified experience for
collecting OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) traces, metrics, and logs on
GKE. This feature includes the following characteristics:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Managed collection:</strong> an in-cluster OTLP endpoint that automatically routes
telemetry to the Cloud Telemetry API.</li>
<li><strong>Automatic configuration:</strong> a new Instrumentation custom resource that
automatically injects environment variables into your workloads to simplify
OTLP ingestion.</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/managed-otel-gke">Managed OpenTelemetry for GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Inference Quickstart (GIQ) now offers
recommendations for distributed AI inference. This enables you to deploy
optimized, full configurations for advanced models, such as the Qwen and gpt-oss
model families, on NVIDIA GPUs and Cloud TPUs.</p>

<p>This release introduces GKE Inference Gateway by integrating
llm-d inference scheduling. You can select optimized configurations for
workloads like Advanced Customer Support, Code Completion, and Deep Research.
This tunes your infrastructure to meet the specific latency and throughput
requirements of these applications.</p>

<p>For more information, see <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/machine-learning/inference/inference-quickstart">Analyze model serving performance and costs with Inference Quickstart</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can use automated disk type selection for Hyperdisk volumes on
GKE. This feature allows GKE to automatically
select the most appropriate disk type based on the machine type of the node
where your workload is scheduled.</p>

<p>With this feature, you can create a single StorageClass that supports clusters
with mixed VM generations. For example, GKE can provision
Hyperdisk on compatible instances (such as C3 or C4) while automatically falling
back to Persistent Disk on other generations.</p>

<p>For more information, see <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/hyperdisk#automated_disk_type_selection">Automated disk type selection</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/compute-optimized-machines#h4d_series">H4D machine series</a>,
designed for high performance computing (HPC) workloads, is generally available
for GKE clusters. Based on 5th generation AMD EPYC Turin with
Cloud RDMA 200 Gbps networking, H4D VMs offer 192 cores (SMT disabled), up to
1,488 GB of memory, and 3,750 GiB of Local SSD. H4D is optimized for
tightly-coupled applications that scale across multiple nodes and offers
RDMA-enabled 200 Gbps networking.</p>

<p>You can use H4D with GKE clusters in Standard, or with
the Performance compute class in Autopilot. For more information, see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/run-hpc-workloads">Run high performance computing (HPC) workloads with H4D</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_25_2026" data-text="February 25, 2026" tabindex="-1">February 25, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r8-version-updates" data-text="(2026-R8) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R8) Version updates</h4>



<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="February_24_2026" data-text="February 24, 2026" tabindex="-1">February 24, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The release note for <a href="/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#November_11_2025">November 11, 2025</a> has been updated to correct the version requirements for using N4D machine types. Cluster autoscaler was incorrectly included in the list of features requiring GKE version 1.34.1-gke.2037000 or later. You can use any available GKE version to use N4D and Cluster autoscaler.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Expanded coverage for compute flexible committed use discounts (CUDs) is
available to all Cloud Billing accounts. All Cloud Billing accounts have
been automatically migrated to the
<a href="/docs/cuds-multiprice">new spend-based CUD model</a> and you no longer need to opt
in to benefit from the expanded coverage. For the full list of eligible SKUs
across Compute Engine, GKE, and Cloud Run,
see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/skus/sku-groups/compute-flexible-cud-eligible-skus">SKU Groups - Compute Flexible CUD Eligible SKUs</a>.</p>

<p>To learn more about compute flexible CUDs and how they apply to your GKE usage, see
the <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/cud">GKE CUDs documentation</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can create a bare metal instance from the <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/general-purpose-machines#c4a_series">C4A machine series</a> with the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">c4a-highmem-96-metal</code> machine type. This machine type is available in Public Preview for Standard clusters running GKE version 1.35.0-gke.2232000 or later. You can select this machine type by using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--machine-type</code> flag when creating a cluster or node pool. For more information about the requirements and limitations of this machine type, see the <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/arm-on-gke#arm-requirements-limitations">Requirements and limitations</a> section of the &quot;Arm workloads on GKE&quot; document.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_19_2026" data-text="February 19, 2026" tabindex="-1">February 19, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r7-version-updates" data-text="(2026-R7) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R7) Version updates</h4>



<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

<div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r7-security-updates" data-text="(2026-R7) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R7) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

<p>

<table>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>Container-Optimized OS version</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.30.14-gke.2071000</td>
<td>cos-113-18244-582-2</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m113#cos-113-18244-582-2_">cos-113-18244-582-2 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.31.14-gke.1423000</td>
<td>cos-117-18613-439-120</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m117#cos-117-18613-439-120_">cos-117-18613-439-120 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_18_2026" data-text="February 18, 2026" tabindex="-1">February 18, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>Multiple security vulnerabilities have been identified in the OpenSSL library.
The most significant finding is CVE-2025-15467, a critical vulnerability that
might allow for remote code execution (RCE) or denial of service (DoS) attacks
via network-based vectors.
For more information, see the
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/security-bulletins#gcp-2026-006-gke">GCP-2026-006 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_17_2026" data-text="February 17, 2026" tabindex="-1">February 17, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>After March 17, 2026, when you enable GKE, the GKE
MCP server is automatically enabled.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>Control of MCP use with organization policies is deprecated. After March 17,
2026, organization policies that use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcp.managed.allowedMCPServices</code>
constraint won&#39;t work, and you can control MCP use with IAM deny policies. For
more information about controlling MCP use, see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/control-mcp-use-iam">Control MCP use with IAM</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_13_2026" data-text="February 13, 2026" tabindex="-1">February 13, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now determine the status and health of a TPU slice and partition by monitoring these new beta system metrics:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/accelerator/slice/state</code>: Indicates the current status of the slice.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/accelerator/partition/state</code>: Indicates the health of the partition.</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/metrics_kubernetes#kubernetes-kubernetes">GKE system metrics</a> documentation.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_11_2026" data-text="February 11, 2026" tabindex="-1">February 11, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r6-version-updates" data-text="(2026-R6) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R6) Version updates</h4>



<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r6-security-updates" data-text="(2026-R6) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R6) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and

<h2 id="February_03_2026" data-text="February 03, 2026" tabindex="-1">February 03, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Image streaming and secondary boot disks are now generally available (GA) for
nodes using the Ubuntu with containerd (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">UBUNTU_CONTAINERD</code>) image type. These
features improve workload startup performance on GKE Standard and Autopilot clusters
through image data streaming and preloaded disk data. To use these features on
Ubuntu nodes, your cluster must be running GKE version 1.35.0-gke.1403000 or later.</p>

<p>For more information, see the documentation for
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/image-streaming">Image Streaming</a>
and <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/data-container-image-preloading">Using Secondary Boot Disks</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_29_2026" data-text="January 29, 2026" tabindex="-1">January 29, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r4-version-updates" data-text="(2026-R4) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R4) Version updates</h4>



<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r4-security-updates" data-text="(2026-R4) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R4) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

<p>

<table>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>Container-Optimized OS version</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.29.15-gke.2725000</td>
<td>cos-113-18244-521-74</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m113#cos-113-18244-521-74_">cos-113-18244-521-74 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.30.14-gke.1973000</td>
<td>cos-113-18244-521-74</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m113#cos-113-18244-521-74_">cos-113-18244-521-74 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.31.14-gke.1319000</td>
<td>cos-117-18613-439-92</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m117#cos-117-18613-439-92_">cos-117-18613-439-92 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>

</tbody>
</table>

</p></div>

<h2 id="January_27_2026" data-text="January 27, 2026" tabindex="-1">January 27, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) support on GKE Dataplane V2 is now
generally available (GA). You can now deploy workloads that use SCTP on
GKE Standard clusters. This feature enables direct SCTP
communication for Pod-to-Pod and Pod-to-Service traffic.</p>

<p>SCTP support requires clusters to use GKE Dataplane V2 and Ubuntu node images.
This feature is available in GKE version 1.32.2-gke.1297000 or
later.</p>

<p>For more information, see <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/deploy-workloads-with-sctp">Deploy workloads with
SCTP</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_26_2026" data-text="January 26, 2026" tabindex="-1">January 26, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/general-purpose-machines#n4a_series">N4A machine
series</a>
is generally available for GKE clusters in Autopilot and
Standard modes. For more information, see <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/arm-on-gke">Arm workloads on
GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_21_2026" data-text="January 21, 2026" tabindex="-1">January 21, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r3-version-updates" data-text="(2026-R3) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R3) Version updates</h4>



<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r3-security-updates" data-text="(2026-R3) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R3) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

<p>

<table>

<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>Container-Optimized OS version</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>

</tr>

</p></div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now determine which Kubernetes JobSets are scheduled on which
GKE node pools and nodes by monitoring the new generally
available system metrics:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/jobset/assigned_node_pools</code>: GKE node pools
where a Kubernetes JobSet has scheduled Pods.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/jobset/assigned_nodes</code>: GKE nodes where a
Kubernetes JobSet has scheduled Pods.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/node_pool/assigned_jobsets</code>: Kubernetes JobSets that have
scheduled Pods on a GKE node pool.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/node/assigned_jobsets</code>: Kubernetes JobSets that have
scheduled Pods on a GKE node.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_20_2026" data-text="January 20, 2026" tabindex="-1">January 20, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">asia-southeast3</code> region in Bangkok, Thailand is available. For more
information, see the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/about/locations/">Global Locations</a>.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>In some GKE versions earlier than 1.34.0-gke.2011000, using the
Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver with streaming writes enabled might cause file
writes to fail with an Input/Output error on the application side accompanied by
503 errors in the gke-gcsfuse-sidecar logs. This issue occurs when streaming
writes are enabled, and is caused by stalls during write operations. Streaming
writes are enabled by default in GKE versions 1.33.2-gke.4655000
and later.</p>

<p>To work around this limitation, you can perform one of the following actions:</p>

<ul>
<li>Upgrade your cluster to GKE version 1.34.1-gke.3849001 or
later.</li>
<li>If you can&#39;t upgrade your cluster, disable streaming writes by passing the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">--enable-streaming-writes=false</code> or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">write:enable-streaming-writes:false</code>
flags when you <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cloud-storage-fuse-csi-driver-perf#mount-options">configure mount
options</a>
for Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver. These flags only prevent error reliably
when staging writes use fast media types such as SSD or tmpfs. tmpfs is
specified using <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--temp-dir</code> or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">file-system:temp-dir</code> flags when you
configure mount options.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_15_2026" data-text="January 15, 2026" tabindex="-1">January 15, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r2-security-updates" data-text="(2026-R2) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R2) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

<p>

<table>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>Container-Optimized OS version</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.35.0-gke.1624000</td>
<td>cos-125-19216-104-45</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125#cos-125-19216-104-45_">cos-125-19216-104-45 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_07_2026" data-text="January 07, 2026" tabindex="-1">January 07, 2026</h2>

      <div><h4 id="2026-r1-version-updates" data-text="(2026-R1) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R1) Version updates</h4>



<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2026-r1-security-updates" data-text="(2026-R1) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2026-R1) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

<p>

<table>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>Container-Optimized OS version</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.35.0-gke.1403000</td>
<td>cos-125-19216-104-45</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125#cos-125-19216-104-45_">cos-125-19216-104-45 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>NodeLocal DNSCache is enabled by default on new Standard
GKE clusters which are created running version 1.34.1-gke.3720000
or later. NodeLocal DNSCache is a GKE add-on that improves DNS
performance by running a DNS cache directly on each cluster node as a DaemonSet.
To learn more, see <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/nodelocal-dns-cache">Set up NodeLocal
DNSCache</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_06_2026" data-text="January 06, 2026" tabindex="-1">January 06, 2026</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>A fix is available for the <a href="#December_16_2025">December 16, 2025</a> issue in which
Autopilot nodes enter into a state where new system Pods and user Pods are
unable to run due to NRI RunPodSandbox failures. For more details, including
instructions on how to confirm if you&#39;re affected by this, see <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/troubleshooting/autopilot-clusters#nri-runpodsandbox-error">Pods unable to
run on a Node due to NRI RunPodSandbox failed</a>.</p>

<p>The fix is available with GKE version 1.34.1-gke.3899000 and
later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_05_2026" data-text="January 05, 2026" tabindex="-1">January 05, 2026</h2>

cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><h4 id="kubernetes_135_is_now_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="Kubernetes 1.35 is now available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Kubernetes 1.35 is now available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.35 is now available in the Rapid channel. For more information about the content of Kubernetes 1.35, read the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.35.md#changelog-since-v1340">Kubernetes 1.35 Release Notes</a> and Kubernetes <a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/12/17/kubernetes-v1-35-release/">1.35 Release Blog</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_in_135" data-text="Deprecated in 1.35" tabindex="-1">Deprecated in 1.35</h4>

<ul>
<li>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">PreferClose</code> value for a <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/">Kubernetes Service&#39;s</a> <code translate="no" dir="ltr">trafficDistribution</code> field is now deprecated in favor of the more explicit <code translate="no" dir="ltr">PreferSameZone</code>.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="removed_in_135" data-text="Removed in 1.35" tabindex="-1">Removed in 1.35</h4>

<ul>
<li>Kubernetes has <a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/11/26/kubernetes-v1-35-sneak-peek/#cgroup-v1-support">deprecated cgroup v1</a> support.</li>
<li>GKE is removing cgroup v1 support in 1.35. If you have specifically configured your node pools to use cgroup v1 then upgrades will be blocked until you configure cgroup v2. To migrate to cgroup v2, see <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/migrate-cgroupv2#migrate">Migrate to cgroup v2</a>.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><h4 id="new_features_in_135" data-text="New features in 1.35" tabindex="-1">New features in 1.35</h4>

<ul>
<li><strong>In-place Pod Resize:</strong> <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/resize-container-resources/">In-place Pod Resize</a> is now GA. This feature allows Pod CPU and memory requests and limits to be modified in-place without Pod or container restart.</li>
<li><strong>Writable cgroups:</strong> GKE <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/writable-cgroups">Writable cgroups</a> for containers is now GA. This feature allows workloads to manage resources for child processes using the Linux cgroups API, improving reliability for applications like <a href="https://www.ray.io/">Ray</a>.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="other_changes_in_135" data-text="Other changes in 1.35" tabindex="-1">Other changes in 1.35</h4>

<ul>
<li><strong>Windows containerd 2.1:</strong> GKE Windows nodes will use containerd 2.1 in 1.35, upgraded from containerd 1.7 in GKE 1.34. Clusters containing Windows nodes will have auto-upgrades to 1.35 delayed until 1.34 EOL due to possible compatibility issues introduced in containerd 2.0. Check if you&#39;re using deprecated containerd features removed in 2.0 and migrate off of them, see <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/migrate-containerd-2#migrate">Migrate nodes to containerd 2</a>. After all deprecated features are removed, manually upgrade your cluster to 1.35.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_19_2025" data-text="December 19, 2025" tabindex="-1">December 19, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Rollout sequencing with custom stages is now available in Preview. This feature
offers granular control over upgrading groups of clusters within a fleet,
allowing you to progressively roll out GKE versions across environments. For
more information see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/rollout-sequencing-custom-stages/about-rollout-sequencing">About rollout sequencing with custom stages</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_18_2025" data-text="December 18, 2025" tabindex="-1">December 18, 2025</h2>

support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2025-r52-security-updates" data-text="(2025-R52) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2025-R52) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

<p>

<table>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>Container-Optimized OS version</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.34.1-gke.3759000</td>
<td>cos-125-19216-104-45</td>
<td><a href="/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125#cos-125-19216-104-45_">cos-125-19216-104-45 release notes</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>GKE Standard clusters enrolled in the Regular channel now
support Autopilot features. Autopilot features include the container-optimized
compute platform and fully managed nodes, letting you use Autopilot&#39;s
advantages without migrating to a dedicated Autopilot cluster.</p>

<p>To use Autopilot features in Standard clusters, use either of the
following configurations:</p>

<ul>
<li>Enroll a cluster in the Regular channel with GKE version 1.34.1-gke.1829001
or later.</li>
<li>Enroll a cluster in the Rapid channel with GKE version 1.33.1-gke.1107000
or later.</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-classes-standard-clusters">Run workloads in Autopilot mode in Standard clusters</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_16_2025" data-text="December 16, 2025" tabindex="-1">December 16, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>In rare cases, a cluster control plane upgrade can cause an Autopilot node to
enter into a state in which new system and user Pods are unable to run, which
then causes issues such as broken Pod networking. GKE is
regularly detecting this issue, and when possible GKE
is mitigating new occurrences of this issue. For more details, see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/troubleshooting/autopilot-clusters#nri-runpodsandbox-error">Pods unable to run on a Node due to NRI RunPodSandbox failed</a>,
and to mitigate this issue yourself, follow the procedure in the section
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/troubleshooting/autopilot-clusters#unreliable-workloads-specific-node">Consistently unreliable workload performance on a specific node</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_15_2025" data-text="December 15, 2025" tabindex="-1">December 15, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Autopilot now supports N4A machine types in
Public Preview, available on clusters running
version 1.34.1-gke.3403001 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_10_2025" data-text="December 10, 2025" tabindex="-1">December 10, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><h4 id="2025-r51-security-updates" data-text="(2025-R51) Security updates" tabindex="-1">(2025-R51) Security updates</h4>

<p>This release includes new GKE versions that use updated
Container-Optimized OS images. These updated images are cumulative,
incorporating security fixes from all Container-Optimized OS
versions released since the previous GKE release.</p>

<p>To identify the specific vulnerabilities that were resolved in each updated
Container-Optimized OS image, see the <strong>Security</strong> release notes
for that image. The following table includes links to the release notes for
each updated Container-Optimized OS image:</p>

<p>

<table>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>Container-Optimized OS version</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.34.1-gke.2541000 and later, you can specify
secure tags for firewalls in the
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/reference/crds/computeclass#resourceManagerTags"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">spec.nodePoolConfig.resourceManagerTags</code> field</a>
in ComputeClasses. GKE adds those secure tags to the nodes that
GKE creates for that ComputeClass, so that you can target
nodes by using these tags in firewall policies. For more information, see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/tags-firewall-policies">Selectively enforce firewall policies in GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_08_2025" data-text="December 08, 2025" tabindex="-1">December 08, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#October_14_2025">October 14, 2025</a>
issue in which MountVolume calls for network file system (NFS) volumes might
fail is fixed for GKE versions 1.34.1-gke.2877000 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_05_2025" data-text="December 05, 2025" tabindex="-1">December 05, 2025</h2>

information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="December_03_2025" data-text="December 03, 2025" tabindex="-1">December 03, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Inference Gateway is generally available (GA) and ready for production
workloads. This release introduces major performance, security, and usability
enhancements since the Public Preview.</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Stable v1 API</strong>: The API has graduated to v1. The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">InferenceModel</code> resource
is replaced by the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">InferenceObjective</code> resource for a clearer definition of
serving goals. A zero-downtime migration path is available.</li>
<li><strong>Prefix-Aware Routing</strong>: A new, intelligent routing feature inspects request
context and routes requests with shared prefixes (like in conversational AI)
to the same model replica. This can maximize KV cache hits and improve
Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) latency by up to 96%.</li>
<li><strong>API Key Authentication</strong>: Secure your endpoints by enforcing API key
validation through a new integration with Apigee.</li>
<li><strong>Body-Based Routing</strong>: The gateway can route requests using the model
field directly from the HTTP request body, which enables native
compatibility with the OpenAI API specification.</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information see
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-gke-inference-gateway">About GKE Inference Gateway</a>
and <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/deploy-gke-inference-gateway">Deploy GKE Inference Gateway</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Starting with version 1.33.2-gke.4655000, the GCSFuse CSI Driver automatically
applies performance-tuning defaults for Cloud Storage FUSE volumes used on nodes
with <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/cloud-storage-fuse/automated-configurations">high-performance machine types</a>.
However, in GKE versions 1.34.1-gke.1431000 to 1.34.1-gke.3403001, these
defaults are not being applied. This is due to an issue where GCSFuse fails
to recognize the machine type from the configuration file provided by the
GCSFuse CSI Driver.</p>

<p>To apply the performance defaults, explicitly set the machine-type as a
gcsfuse mount option. Use the command-line flag format, with the key and
value separated by an equals sign (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">=</code>).</p>

<p>For example: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">machine-type=n2-standard-4</code></p>

<p>Ensure the Pod using the GCSFuse volume is scheduled on a node that matches
the specified machine type. These settings are optimized for high-performance
machine types and might not be suitable for other node types. For more
information on scheduling, see the Kubernetes documentation on
<a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/">assigning Pods to Nodes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_28_2025" data-text="November 28, 2025" tabindex="-1">November 28, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2025-r49-version-updates" data-text="(2025-R49) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2025-R49) Version updates</h4>



<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for
manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information about versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and
support</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">About GKE
cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="November_27_2025" data-text="November 27, 2025" tabindex="-1">November 27, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>TPU7x (Ironwood), Google&#39;s seventh-generation TPU for large-scale AI workloads,
is available in <a href="/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a> in GKE
Standard clusters that run version 1.34.0-gke.2201000 and later, and in
Autopilot clusters that run version 1.34.1-gke.3084001 and later.
TPU7x offers a significant performance increase compared to previous
generations, with 2307 TFLOPs of BF16 performance and 192&nbsp;GB of
high-bandwidth memory (HBM) per chip. For more information, see
<a href="/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/tpus#ironwood-benefits">Get started with Ironwood (TPU7x)</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_24_2025" data-text="November 24, 2025" tabindex="-1">November 24, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Fast-starting nodes are now generally available. GKE provisions
fast-starting nodes on a best-effort basis in Autopilot when workloads
use compatible configurations. For more information, see
<a href="/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/fast-starting-nodes">About quicker workload startup with fast-starting nodes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_21_2025" data-text="November 21, 2025" tabindex="-1">November 21, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>In GKE versions 1.34.1-gke.2037001 and 1.34.1-gke.2541000, Arm
nodes that use an Ubuntu node image might incorrectly use an image with a
64&nbsp;KB page size instead of the default 4&nbsp;KB page size. Avoid using
version 1.34.1-gke.2037001 and 1.34.1-gke.2541000 for your Ubuntu Arm nodes.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>GKE versions earlier than 1.32 don&#39;t support
<a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes/#nfs">direct NFS volume mounts</a>
to NFS volumes that exclusively use an NFS protocol greater than <code translate="no" dir="ltr">NFSv4.0</code>.</p>

<p>When using direct NFS volume mounts, Pods on GKE node versions
earlier than 1.32 might fail to mount NFS volumes that are configured to only
support protocols greater than <code translate="no" dir="ltr">NFSv4.0</code> (such as <code translate="no" dir="ltr">NFSv4.1</code> or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">NFSv4.2</code>). This
issue occurs because the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">containerized_mounter</code> on these earlier
GKE versions uses version <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.2.8</code> of the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">nfs-utils</code> package,
which doesn&#39;t support <code translate="no" dir="ltr">NFSv4</code> minor versions. As a result, the mount process
fails with the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">mount.nfs: access denied by server</code> error message.</p>

<p>This issue doesn&#39;t affect GKE version 1.32 and later, which
include an updated version of the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">nfs-utils</code> package. To resolve this issue,
try one of the following options:</p>

<ul>
<li>Upgrade clusters to GKE version 1.32 or later.</li>
<li>Configure the NFS volume to support both the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">NFSv3</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">NFSv4</code> protocols,
which allows the mount to succeed by falling back to a compatible version.</li>
<li>Use a PersistentVolume and PersistentVolumeClaim to mount the NFS volume,
which allows for explicit NFS version specification.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_20_2025" data-text="November 20, 2025" tabindex="-1">November 20, 2025</h2>

cluster upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="November_17_2025" data-text="November 17, 2025" tabindex="-1">November 17, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>NVIDIA recommends that Kubernetes clusters enable Coherent Driver-Based Memory
Management (CDMM) to resolve memory over-reporting. CDMM is enabled by default
on A4X nodes running the R580 GPU driver in GKE clusters with the
following versions:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>1.33 or later</strong>: 1.33.4-gke.1036000 or later</li>
<li><strong>1.32</strong>: 1.32.8-gke.1108000 or later</li>
</ul>

<p>CDMM allows GPU memory to be managed through the driver instead of the operating
system (OS), avoiding OS onlining of GPU memory, and exposing the GPU memory as
a Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) node to the OS.</p>

<p>For more information about CDMM, see
<a href="https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/tesla/tesla-release-notes-580-65-06/index.html#hardware-software-support">Hardware and Software Support</a>.
To create GKE clusters with A4X, see the following documents:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="/ai-hypercomputer/docs/create/gke-ai-hypercompute">Create an AI-optimized GKE cluster with default configuration</a></li>
<li><a href="/ai-hypercomputer/docs/create/gke-ai-hypercompute-custom-a4x">Create a custom AI-optimized GKE cluster which uses A4X</a></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
