<h2 id="May_13_2025" data-text="May 13, 2025" tabindex="-1">May 13, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>GKE Autopilot clusters fail to update the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">cgroup_mode</code> field and display the following error:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded><code translate="no" dir="ltr">ERROR: (gcloud.container.clusters.update)
    ResponseError: code=400,
    message=INVALID_ARGUMENT: invalid node_pool_auto_config.linux_node_config.
    Allowed fields are: [&#34;cgroup_mode&#34;]
</code></pre></devsite-code>
<p>This issue occurs in all GKE versions. A fix for this issue is in progress. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/migrate-cgroupv2">Migrate nodes to Linux cgroupv2</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE now provides insights and recommendations that help you to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/crd-with-invalid-caBundle">identify and troubleshoot</a> clusters with Custom Resource Definitions that contain an invalid or malformed Certificate Authority bundle, which might disrupt cluster operations. Implementing the recommendation helps you to keep your clusters stable and performant.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_12_2025" data-text="May 12, 2025" tabindex="-1">May 12, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.33 and later, the Compute Engine persistent disk CSI Driver supports provisioning Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability volumes in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ReadWriteOnce</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ReadWriteOncePod</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ReadWriteMany</code> access modes. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/regional-pd#balanced_high_availability">Provisioning Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability volumes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><h4 id="133_is_now_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="1.33 is now available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">1.33 is now available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.33 is now available in the Rapid channel. For more information about the content of Kubernetes 1.33, read the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.33.md#changelog-since-v1320">Kubernetes 1.33 Release Notes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><h4 id="new_features_in_133" data-text="New features in 1.33" tabindex="-1">New features in 1.33</h4>

<ul>
<li>New v1beta2 versions of the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/dynamic-resource-allocation/#api">Kubernetes Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) APIs</a> will be available (because this is a beta API, using it in GKE clusters requires <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/use-beta-apis">opt-in</a>). For more information about using DRA in GKE, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-dynamic-resource-allocation">About dynamic resource allocation in GKE</a>.</li>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/04/23/kubernetes-v1-33-release/#beta-in-place-resource-resize-for-vertical-scaling-of-pods">In-Place Pod Resize</a> (Public Preview) allows you to change the CPU and memory requests and limits assigned to containers within a <em>running</em> Pod (limitations apply) through the new <code translate="no" dir="ltr">resize</code> pod subresource (on-by-default), often without requiring a container restart significantly decreasing service disruptions. For more information, see <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/resize-container-resources/">Resize CPU and Memory Resources assigned to Containers</a>.</li>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/04/23/kubernetes-v1-33-release/#stable-sidecar-containers">Sidecar Containers</a> graduated to stable, enabling the &quot;sidecar pattern&quot;. initContainers with  <code translate="no" dir="ltr">restartPolicy: Always</code> will start before application containers and remain running throughout the pod&#39;s lifecycle, terminating after the main containers exit.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5116">Streaming List Response Encoding</a> enables efficient handling of requests for large object collections, improving API server reliability and performance.</li>
<li><p><a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/04/23/kubernetes-v1-33-release/#multiple-service-cidrs">Multiple Service CIDRs</a> is now generally available, allowing cluster administrators to <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/network/extend-service-ip-ranges/">dynamically increase the number of IP addresses available</a> for <code translate="no" dir="ltr">type: ClusterIP</code> Services (by creating new ServiceCIDR objects).</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> To ensure network stability during this initial phase, Service CIDRs can only be created within the 34.118.224.0/20 reserved IP address range in Compute Engine. Future releases will remove this limitation.</span></aside></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_in_133" data-text="Deprecated in 1.33" tabindex="-1">Deprecated in 1.33</h4>

<p>The gitRepo volume driver is deprecated and disabled for security reasons. For more information, see <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5040">KEP-5040</a>.</p>

<h4 id="removed_in_133" data-text="Removed in 1.33" tabindex="-1">Removed in 1.33</h4>

<p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion</code> field in the Node API object is no longer populated in 1.33 and later. This field actually reported the kubelet version, not the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kube-proxy</code> version. You can use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion</code> to get the kubelet version. For more information, see <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-network/4004-deprecate-kube-proxy-version">KEP-4004</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="other_changes_in_133" data-text="Other changes in 1.33" tabindex="-1">Other changes in 1.33</h4>

<p><a href="https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/docs/containerd-2.0.md">containerd 2.0</a> is supported. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/migrate-containerd-2">Migrate nodes to containerd 2</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_08_2025" data-text="May 08, 2025" tabindex="-1">May 08, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.32 and later, GKE Sandbox (gVisor) can now be configured with SYS_ADMIN privileges in GKE Autopilot. This lets you use <a href="https://gvisor.dev/docs/tutorials/docker-in-gke-sandbox/">Docker-in-Docker with gVisor</a> in GKE Autopilot.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>ClusterProfile sync is now available to generate a cluster inventory for an existing fleet. A cluster inventory lets you work with open source and third party integrations that use the <a href="https://multicluster.sigs.k8s.io/concepts/cluster-profile-api/">ClusterProfile</a> specification.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_02_2025" data-text="May 02, 2025" tabindex="-1">May 02, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="April_24_2025" data-text="April 24, 2025" tabindex="-1">April 24, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>Saxml on GKE is de-prioritized beginning April 24, 2025. This means the project won&#39;t get further updates. Existing Saxml deployments will continue to function as is without disruption. We <em>strongly suggest</em> that you migrate to <a href="https://github.com/google/JetStream">JetStream</a>, Google&#39;s up to date open source inference framework for high-performance LLM serving on TPUs and GPUs. JetStream offers continuous batching and quantization for better throughput and memory efficiency. For a migration example, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/tutorials/serve-gemma-tpu-jetstream">Serve Gemma using TPUs on GKE with JetStream</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="April_17_2025" data-text="April 17, 2025" tabindex="-1">April 17, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Inference Gateway is now available to significantly improve the performance, efficiency, and observability of generative AI workloads on GKE.</p>

<p>GKE Inference Gateway provides:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Improved performance</strong>: AI serving tail latency is reduced, and AI serving throughput is increased through inference-optimized load balancing.</li>
<li><strong>Efficient resource utilization</strong>: Enables dense multi-workload serving of multiple LoRA fine-tuned models on a shared accelerator, leading to higher GPU/TPU utilization.</li>
<li><strong>Simplified operations</strong>: Features include model-aware routing, model-specific serving priority, and integrated AI Safety.</li>
<li><strong>Enhanced observability</strong>: Golden signals of observability are provided for inference requests.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_08_2025" data-text="April 08, 2025" tabindex="-1">April 08, 2025</h2>

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2025-r14_version_updates" data-text="(2025-R14) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2025-R14) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="April_03_2025" data-text="April 03, 2025" tabindex="-1">April 03, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE now provides insights and recommendations that help you <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/vertical-pod-autoscaling#identify-workloads">identify workloads without resource requests or limits</a> so that you can specify the resource needs for these workloads. Configuring CPU and memory requests and limits for containers is the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/architecture/best-practices-for-running-cost-effective-kubernetes-applications-on-gke#set_appropriate_resource_requests_and_limits">best practice</a> for improving reliability and performance, and is a necessary prerequisite for understanding and optimizing resource utilization by your workloads and their cost.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Automatic application monitoring is now generally available in GKE versions 1.28 and later. When configured on GKE clusters, this feature automatically collects key metrics with Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus and provides out-of-the-box dashboards for monitoring the supported workloads. Automatic application monitoring supports six new AI model servers (NVIDIA Triton, vLLM, TGI, JetStream, TorchServe and TensorFlow Serving). For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-automatic-application-monitoring">Configure automatic application monitoring</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_28_2025" data-text="March 28, 2025" tabindex="-1">March 28, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In version 1.32.1-gke.1729000 and later, you can customize specific kubelet and Linux kernel parameters like sysctls and huge pages by using the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-custom-compute-classes#customize-node-system-config"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">nodeSystemConfig</code></a> field in your GKE compute classes. Additionally, you can now specify default values for fields that are omitted in individual rules in a compute class by using the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/reference/crds/computeclass#priorityDefaults"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">priorityDefaults</code></a> field. For details, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-custom-compute-classes#autoprovisioning-and-compute-classes">About custom compute classes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="March_21_2025" data-text="March 21, 2025" tabindex="-1">March 21, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.32.2-gke.1652000 and later, new external LoadBalancer Services use zonal Network Endpoint Group (NEG) backends by default. This applies only to new backend service-based external LoadBalancer Services. Existing LoadBalancer Services are not affected. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/backend-service-based-external-load-balancer">Create a backend service-based external load balancer</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Starting in GKE version 1.32.1-gke.1729000, Autopilot clusters will automatically use the new <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/horizontal-pod-autoscaling#hpa-profile">Performance HPA Profile</a>. This new profile enables faster autoscaling on CPU and Memory metrics for up to 1,000 <code translate="no" dir="ltr">HorizontalPodAutoscaler</code> objects by routing autoscaling metrics through the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gke-metrics-agent</code> Daemonset. If desired, users can revert to the old autoscaling profile by <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/horizontal-pod-autoscaling#disable_performance_hpa_profile">disabling the Peformance HPA Profile</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>All GKE clusters now export four new rollup metrics by default at no additional charge. These new metrics are for monitoring GKE TPU NodePools and JobSets:</p>

<ul>
<li><p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/node_pool/accelerator/times_to_recover</code>: Distribution of recovery period durations. Each sample indicates a single recovery operation for the NodePool to recover from a downtime period. The data is sampled within 60s after the completion of NodePool recovery, and emitted within 24h. This metric does not include a sample for downtime period longer than 7 days. This metric is only applicable for GKE multi-host TPU node pools.</p></li>
<li><p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/jobset/times_between_interruptions</code>: Distribution of times between the end of last interruption and beginning of current interruption for a JobSet. Each sample indicates a single duration between last and current interruption. The data is sampled within 60s after the current interruption starts, and emitted within 24h. The metric does not include a sample for duration between interruptions longer than 7 days. This metric is only applicable for JobSets running on nodes with GPU/TPU and having a single replicated job.</p></li>
<li><p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/jobset/times_to_recover</code>: Distribution of recovery period durations. Each sample indicates a single recovery operation for the JobSet to recover from a downtime period. The data is sampled within 60s after the completion of JobSet recovery, and emitted within 24h. This metric does not include samples for downtime periods longer than 7 days. This metric is only applicable for JobSets running on nodes with GPU/TPU and having a single replicated job.</p></li>
<li><p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/jobset/uptime</code>: Total time the JobSet has been available. The data is sampled every 60s and emitted within 24h after sampling. This metric is only applicable for JobSets running on nodes with GPU/TPU and having a single replicated job.</p></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="March_18_2025" data-text="March 18, 2025" tabindex="-1">March 18, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>On GKE clusters running versions 1.32.2-gke.1182000 to 1.32.2-gke.1297000, Pods using Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver volumes (persistent or CSI ephemeral) fail to schedule when both of the following are true:</p>

<ul>
<li>The Pods run on the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/workload-resources/pod-v1/#hosts-namespaces">host network</a> (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">hostNetwork: true</code>)</li>
<li>You use a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cloud-storage-fuse-csi-driver-sidecar#configure-a-private-image">custom sidecar image</a> built with a Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver version earlier than <a href="https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/gcs-fuse-csi-driver/tree/v1.12.2">v1.12.2</a>.</li>
</ul>

<p>The fix is available on GKE cluster version 1.32.2-gke.1297001 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_14_2025" data-text="March 14, 2025" tabindex="-1">March 14, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>JobSet metrics are automatically available on new GKE Standard and Autopilot clusters starting from version 1.32.1-gke.1357001 or later. For existing clusters, you can upgrade your clusters and manually enable the JobSet metrics package. For more details on the list of JobSet metrics, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/kube-state-metrics#ksm-jobset-metrics">JobSet metrics</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_12_2025" data-text="March 12, 2025" tabindex="-1">March 12, 2025</h2>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="March_07_2025" data-text="March 07, 2025" tabindex="-1">March 07, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/monitor-startup-latency-metrics">monitor startup latency</a> of Kubernetes workloads and nodes using the new <strong>Startup Latency</strong> dashboard available in the Observability tab on the Deployment details and Cluster details pages in the GKE Console. The dashboard is useful for tracking, troubleshooting and optimizing startup latency of your GKE workloads.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE now allows you to enable logging of Horizontal Pod Autoscaler decisions starting from GKE version 1.31.5-gke.1090000 or later, or version 1.32.1-gke.1260000 or later. These logs include <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/view-horizontalpodautoscaling-events#atomic_recommendation">atomic recommendations</a> (based on individual metrics) and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/view-horizontalpodautoscaling-events#final_recommendation">final recommendations</a> (consolidated HPA decisions). The logs are stored in Cloud Logging and offer insights into the decision-making process of the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler.</p></div>
    </div>

information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

      <div><p>The Envoy project recently announced several new security vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-53269, CVE-2024-53270, and CVE-2024-53271) that could allow an attacker to crash Envoy.</p>

<h2 id="March_04_2025" data-text="March 04, 2025" tabindex="-1">March 04, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">europe-north2</code></a> region in Stockholm, Sweden is now available. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/about/locations">Global Locations</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_28_2025" data-text="February 28, 2025" tabindex="-1">February 28, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>New recommendations of <code translate="no" dir="ltr">NODE_SA_MISSING_PERMISSIONS</code> subtype are added to the portfolio of <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/optimize-with-recommenders">GKE Recommendations</a>. Use the new recommendations to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/troubleshooting/logging#identify-fix-permissions-logs-in-all-clusters">identify clusters</a> with node service accounts missing IAM permissions that are critical for normal cluster operations.</p>

<p>If your organization has a policy to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/organization-policy/restricting-service-accounts#disable_service_account_default_grants">disable automatic role grants to default service accounts</a>, the created <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/service-accounts#default-gke-service-agent">default GKE node service account</a> will not get the necessary permissions. Missing critical permissions can degrade your essential cluster operations, such as logging and monitoring.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_27_2025" data-text="February 27, 2025" tabindex="-1">February 27, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The GKE Autopilot partner program now lets partners create and manage allowlists that correspond to specific partner workloads. In GKE version 1.32.1-gke.1729000 and later, you can explicitly install allowlists in your clusters to run only the partner solutions that you need. </p>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/run-autopilot-partner-workloads">Run privileged workloads from GKE Autopilot partners</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="February_25_2025" data-text="February 25, 2025" tabindex="-1">February 25, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Three new metrics are added for checking node and node pool status:</p>

<ul>
<li><p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/node/status_condition</code>: The condition of a node from the node status condition field. The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Ready</code> field has <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Unknown</code> status if the node controller has not heard from the node in the last <code translate="no" dir="ltr">node-monitor-grace-period</code> period. This metric is available for clusters with GKE version 1.32.1-gke.1260000 and later.</p></li>
<li><p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/node_pool/multi_host/available</code>: The multi-host NodePool availability. When <em>all</em> the nodes in the node pool are available, the value is <code translate="no" dir="ltr">True</code>. If any of the nodes in the node pool are unavailable, the value is <code translate="no" dir="ltr">False</code>. This metric is available for Multi-host TPU node pools only.</p></li>
<li><p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/node_pool/status</code>: The current status of the node pool from the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">NodePool</code> instance. Status updates happen after GKE API operations complete. This metric is available for Multi-host TPU node pools only.</p></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_21_2025" data-text="February 21, 2025" tabindex="-1">February 21, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.33 and later, if you omit the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">whenUnsatisfiable</code> field in a new GKE compute class specification, the default value is <code translate="no" dir="ltr">DoNotScaleUp</code>.</p>

<p>In GKE versions earlier than 1.33, the default value is <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ScaleUpAnyway</code>. Ensure that your compute class specifications explicitly set a value in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">whenUnsatisfiable</code> field after you upgrade to version 1.33. This change only affects new <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ComputeClass</code> objects that you create that omit the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">whenUnsatisfiable</code> field. Any existing compute classes that omit the field continue to use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ScaleUpAnyway</code> as the default value even after you upgrade the cluster to version 1.33 or later.</p>

<p>To learn more about the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">whenUnsatisfiable</code> field, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-custom-compute-classes#define-scaling-no-rules">Define scaling behavior when no priority rules apply</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_20_2025" data-text="February 20, 2025" tabindex="-1">February 20, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>New GKE 1.27 patch versions starting with version 1.27.16-gke.2440000 are built with COS 109, because COS 105 is near the end of support. GKE makes new 1.27 patch versions available using COS 109. However, GKE won&#39;t auto-upgrade nodes across the COS milestone boundary, from a patch version using COS 105 to a patch version using COS 109.</p>

<p>If you manually upgrade your nodes to 1.27.16-gke.2440000 or later, GKE continues node auto-upgrades as normal. Control plane upgrades are unaffected, and cluster auto-upgrades to the next minor version towards the end of extended support proceed as normal.</p>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning#cos-extended">Container-Optimized OS updates during the extended support period</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE automatically adds the following resource labels to node pools:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">goog-gke-accelerator-type</code>: The accelerator type used in the node pool.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">goog-gke-tpu-node-pool-type</code>: The TPU node pool type, which can be single-host or multi-host.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">goog-gke-node-pool-provisioning-model</code>: The provisioning model of the node pool. The nodes can be on demand, by reservation, or Spot VMs. </li>
</ul>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/creating-managing-labels#automatically-applied-labels">Automatically applied labels</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Managed NVIDIA Data Center GPU Manager (DCGM) Metrics Package is now generally available for both GKE Standard and Autopilot clusters running version 1.32.0-gke.1764000 and later. You can enable the feature via the Console, gcloud, or Terraform. Starting with cluster version 1.32.1-gke.1357000, GKE Managed NVIDIA DCGM will be default-on for new clusters. </p>

<p>GKE Managed DCGM provides a curated set of metrics for monitoring the utilization, performance, and health of NVIDIA GPUs. These metrics are collected by Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus and you can view the metric charts in the Observability Tab on the Kubernetes Clusters page or in Cloud Monitoring. For more information, see Collect and view DCGM metrics.</p>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/dcgm-metrics">Collect and view DCGM metrics</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_19_2025" data-text="February 19, 2025" tabindex="-1">February 19, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Starting on July 1, 2025, new organizations will no longer be able to create GKE clusters with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/oidc">Identity Service for GKE</a>. You can continue to use Identity Service for GKE in existing organizations, but we encourage you to migrate to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workforce-identity-federation">Workforce Identity Federation</a>.</p>

<p>Workforce Identity Federation is the recommended method for configuring access to your GKE clusters from external identity providers. Workforce Identity Federation provides a single hosted solution for managing external IdPs across Google Cloud products. Unlike Identity Service for GKE, Workforce Identity Federation doesn&#39;t install components in your cluster.</p>

<p>For details and migration instructions, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/oidc">Use external identity providers to authenticate to GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2025-r06_version_updates" data-text="(2025-R06) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2025-R06) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Weighted load balancing for GKE External LoadBalancer Services is now generally available on GKE clusters running version  1.31.0-gke.1506000 or later. Weighted load balancing is a more efficient way to distribute traffic to nodes based on the number of serving Pods they have backing the Service. </p>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/service-load-balancer#weighted-lb">Weighted load balancing</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_04_2025" data-text="February 04, 2025" tabindex="-1">February 04, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>A bug in the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/image-streaming">image streaming</a> feature caused authentication-related failures in specific scenarios when the workload tried to access container image data. This bug has been fixed in the following GKE versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.32.0-gke.1448000 and above.</li>
<li>1.31.4-gke.1183000 and above.</li>
<li>1.30.8-gke.1261000 and above.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A security vulnerability was discovered in the Google Secret Manager Provider for Secret Store CSI Driver. This vulnerability could allow an attacker to gain access to the Kubernetes service account token of the CSI driver.</p>

<p>For more details, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/security-bulletins#gcp-2025-006">GCP-2025-006 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE cluster notifications have the following new capabilities:</p>

<ul>
<li>You can now receive cluster notifications through Cloud Logging. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-notifications#viewing-logging">Viewing cluster notifications in Cloud Logging (Preview)</a>.</li>
<li>GKE now sends a cluster notification to notify you when your cluster is running a minor version that is at or near the end of support. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-notifications#end-of-standard-support-notification">Minor version at or near the end of support</a>.</li>
<li>GKE now sends a cluster notification to notify you when your cluster has completed an upgrade operation. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-notifications#upgrade-operation-complete-notification">Upgrade operation is complete</a>.</li>
</ul>

<p>For more details about the different types of cluster notifications GKE sends and how you can receive them, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-notifications">Cluster notifications</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_03_2025" data-text="February 03, 2025" tabindex="-1">February 03, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Starting on February 3, 2025, GKE will create a new service agent named <code translate="no" dir="ltr">service-{PROJECT_
NUMBER}@gcp-sa-gkenode.iam.gserviceaccount.com</code> that the GKE system workloads that run on your worker nodes can use. This service agent will only have the minimum permissions that GKE needs to operate these nodes by default, and will help to isolate the requirements of GKE-managed workloads from the requirements of your workloads. GKE-managed system workloads will begin using this service agent in an upcoming GKE version, which we&#39;ll announce in a separate release note.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_30_2025" data-text="January 30, 2025" tabindex="-1">January 30, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>Starting on January 28, 2025, the following Preview features are deprecated:</p>

<ul>
<li>GKE threat detection</li>
<li>Supply chain concerns - Binary Authorization</li>
<li>GKE Compliance dashboard</li>
</ul>

<p>For deprecation and removal dates, and for information about alternatives, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/posture-management-deprecation">Posture management deprecations</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_29_2025" data-text="January 29, 2025" tabindex="-1">January 29, 2025</h2>

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2025-r04_version_updates" data-text="(2025-R04) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2025-R04) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="January_23_2025" data-text="January 23, 2025" tabindex="-1">January 23, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2025-r03_version_updates" data-text="(2025-R03) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2025-R03) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="rapid-channel_66" data-text="Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Rapid channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts are already in progress
when we publish the release notes, and can take multiple days to complete across all Google Cloud
zones.</span></aside>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>User-managed firewall rules for GKE LoadBalancer Services is now generally available on GKE clusters running version 1.31.3-gke.1056000 or later. By allowing user-managed firewall rules for GKE LoadBalancer Services, advanced firewall policies can now be configured to control ingress traffic to your GKE Services exposed with passthrough network load balancers. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/user-managed-firewall-rules">User-managed firewall rules for GKE LoadBalancer Services</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-system-config#kubelet-options">customize a node system configuration</a> with the following new kubelet and sysctl configuration options:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>Kubelet</p>

<ul>
<li>containerLogMaxSize</li>
<li>containerLogMaxFiles</li>
<li>imageGcLowThresholdPercent</li>
<li>imageGcHighThresholdPercent</li>
<li>imageMinimumGcAge</li>
<li>imageMaximumGcAge (1.30.7-gke.1076000 and later, 1.31.3-gke.1023000 and later)</li>
<li>allowedUnsafeSysctls (1.32.0-gke.1448000 and later)</li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>Sysctl</p>

<ul>
<li>kernel.shmmni</li>
<li>kernel.shmmax</li>
<li>kernel.shmall</li>
<li>net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_acct (1.32.0-gke.1448000 and later)</li>
<li>net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max (1.32.0-gke.1448000 and later)</li>
<li>net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_buckets (1.32.0-gke.1448000 and later)</li>
<li>net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_close_wait (1.32.0-gke.1448000 and later)</li>
<li>net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established (1.32.0-gke.1448000 and later)</li>
<li>net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait (1.32.0-gke.1448000 and later)</li>
</ul></li>
</ul>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-system-config#kubelet-options">Kubelet configuration options</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-system-config#sysctl-options">Sysctl configuration options</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Starting with GKE version 1.32.1-gke.1002000, the default OS image for Ubuntu is updated from Ubuntu 22.04 to Ubuntu 24.04.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_21_2025" data-text="January 21, 2025" tabindex="-1">January 21, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now use A3 Ultra VM powered by NVIDIA H200 Tensor Core GPUs with our new Titanium ML network adapter, which delivers non-blocking 3.2 Tbps of GPU-to-GPU traffic with RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE). </p>

<p>A3 Ultra VMs are generally available in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">a3-ultragpu-8g</code> machine type and can be used through both the modes of operation in Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE):</p>

<ul>
<li>GKE Standard supports A3 Ultra with GPUDirect RDMA on GKE version 1.31.4-gke.1183000 or higher. To get started, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/ai-hypercomputer/docs/create/gke-ai-hypercompute">Create a Hypercompute Cluster with GKE with default configuration</a>.</li>
<li>GKE Autopilot supports A3 Ultra without GPUDirect RDMA on GKE version 1.31.4-gke.1183000 or higher. To get started, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-gpus">Deploy GPU workloads in Autopilot</a>. A3 Ultra with GPUDirect RDMA is not yet supported on GKE Autopilot.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_16_2025" data-text="January 16, 2025" tabindex="-1">January 16, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>With minor version 1.33, GKE nodes use containerd 2.0, which removes support for Docker Schema 1 images and the CRI v1alpha2 API. GKE pauses automatic upgrades to 1.33 when it detects that a cluster uses the deprecated features. To prepare for this change, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/migrate-containerd-2">Migrate nodes to containerd 2</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_14_2025" data-text="January 14, 2025" tabindex="-1">January 14, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2025-r02_version_updates" data-text="(2025-R02) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2025-R02) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="January_09_2025" data-text="January 09, 2025" tabindex="-1">January 09, 2025</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A security issue impacted resources in VPCs with GKE Multi-Cluster Gateway (MCG) configured. MCG is an optional feature that is used by a small subset of GKE customers. We are individually notifying customers who had the feature enabled during that time period.</p>

<p>For more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/security-bulletins#gcp-2025-001">GCP-2025-001 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_07_2025" data-text="January 07, 2025" tabindex="-1">January 07, 2025</h2>

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2025-r01_version_updates" data-text="(2025-R01) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2025-R01) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<li>The following node versions are now available:
<ul>

<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#v12815">1.28.15-gke.1435000</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.29.md#v12912">1.29.12-gke.1055000</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.30.md#v1308">1.30.8-gke.1051000</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.31.md#v1314">1.31.4-gke.1072000</a></li>
</ul></li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_17_2024" data-text="December 17, 2024" tabindex="-1">December 17, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><p><strong>1.32 is now available in the Rapid channel</strong></p>

<p>Kubernetes 1.32 is now available in the Rapid channel. For more information about the content of Kubernetes 1.32, read the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.32.md#changelog-since-v1310">Kubernetes 1.32 Release Notes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p><strong>Deprecated in Kubernetes 1.32</strong></p>

<ul>
<li><p>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs were <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-32">deprecated in 1.29 and removed in 1.32</a> in favor of newer versions:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3 FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration</code>
<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.29, will no longer be served in 1.32,</li>
<li>instead, use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1</code>, available since 1.29.</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion</code> field in the Node API is deprecated and will not be populated starting in v1.33. The field is currently populated with the kubelet version, not the kube-proxy version, and might not accurately reflect the kube-proxy version in use. For more information, see <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-network/4004-deprecate-kube-proxy-version">KEP-4004</a>.</p></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><strong>New features</strong></p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/dynamic-resource-allocation/">Dynamic Resource Allocation</a> graduated to beta, and enables efficient scheduling of advanced device driver resources (because this is a beta API, using it in GKE clusters requires <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/use-beta-apis">opt-in</a>).</li>
<li>Support for <a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2024/12/17/kube-apiserver-api-streaming/">more efficient API streaming</a> graduated to beta and is enabled by default in the API server. Clients can <a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2024/12/17/kube-apiserver-api-streaming/#enabling-api-streaming-for-your-component">opt into use of this more efficient mechanism</a>.</li>
<li>Support for <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/#recovering-from-failure-when-expanding-volumes">recovery from volume expansion failure</a> graduated to beta and is enabled by default.</li>
<li>Support in the Job API for <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/job/#delegation-of-managing-a-job-object-to-external-controller">management by external controllers</a> graduated to beta and is enabled by default. This enables integrations with external controllers like <a href="https://kueue.sigs.k8s.io/docs/concepts/multikueue/">MultiKueue</a>.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_16_2024" data-text="December 16, 2024" tabindex="-1">December 16, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Trillium, our sixth-generation TPU, is now generally available. Support is available for GKE Standard clusters in version <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.31.1-gke.1846000</code> or later, and Autopilot clusters in version <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.31.2-gke.1384000</code> or later. You can use TPU Trillium in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">us-east5-b</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">europe-west4-a</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">us-east1-d</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">asia-northeast1-b</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">us-south1-a</code> zones. </p>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/tpus#trillium-benefits">Benefits of using TPU Trillium</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Cloud DNS additive VPC scope is now generally available on GKE clusters running version <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.28.3-gke.1430000</code> or later. You can now configure your GKE clusters to add GKE headless service entries to your Cloud DNS private zone visible from your VPC networks, on top of using Cloud DNS (cluster scope) as your GKE DNS provider.</p>

<p>To learn more, read <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cloud-dns#dns-scopes">Cloud DNS scopes for GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_13_2024" data-text="December 13, 2024" tabindex="-1">December 13, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The C4A machine family is generally available in the following versions:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>Standard clusters in version <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.28.13-gke.1024000</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.29.8-gke.1057000</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.30.4-gke.1213000</code> or later. To use this family in GKE Standard, you can use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--machine-type</code> flag when creating a cluster or node pool.</p></li>
<li><p>Autopilot clusters in <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.28.15-gke.1344000</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.29.11-gke.1012000</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.30.7-gke.1136000</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.31.3-gke.1056000</code> or later. To use this family in GKE Autopilot, schedule your workloads along with the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/machine-family: c4a</code> node selector. In versions <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.31</code> or above, the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/arch: arm64</code> node selector would default to C4A machine family.</p></li>
</ul>

<p>Cluster autoscaler and node auto-provisioning are supported in <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.28.15-gke.1344000</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.29.11-gke.1012000</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.30.7-gke.1136000</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.31.3-gke.1056000</code> or later.</p>

<p>Local SSD support is available for Public <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products/?_gl=1*jq03lo*_ga*MTE4MTA1MzEyMS4xNzMzOTQ1MTU0*_ga_4LYFWVHBEB*MTczNDAxMzM2OS40LjEuMTczNDAxMzk2NS4wLjAuMA..#product-launch-stages">Preview</a> from <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.31.1-gke.2008000</code>. Contact your Account Team to participate in the preview.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE now provides insights and recommendations that help you identify and amend clusters running a minor version that reached <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning#recommender-end-of-support">end of standard support</a>, clusters with nodes in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning#recommender-version-skew">violation of version skew policy</a>, and clusters <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/maintenance-windows-and-exclusions#recommender-maintenance-window">without a maintenance window</a> to achieve reliable operations, up-to-date security posture and supportability.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_12_2024" data-text="December 12, 2024" tabindex="-1">December 12, 2024</h2>

information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>

<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded from version 1.30 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.30.md#v1305">1.30.5-gke.1443001</a> with this release.</li>

<h2 id="December_02_2024" data-text="December 02, 2024" tabindex="-1">December 02, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.31.1-gke.2105000 or later, you can now configure custom compute classes to consume Compute Engine reservations. Workloads that use those custom compute classes automatically trigger reservation consumption during node creation. This lets you manage reservation consumption more centrally. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-custom-compute-classes#reservations">About custom compute classes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

      <div><p>Cloud TPU Trillium (v6e) machine types are now in public preview for Autopilot clusters running version 1.31.2-gke.1384000 or later. These TPUs are available in the following zones: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">us-east5-b</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">europe-west4-a</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">us-east1-d</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">asia-northeast1-b</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">us-south1-a</code>. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/plan-tpus">Plan TPUs in GKE</a>.</p></div>

<h2 id="November_26_2024" data-text="November 26, 2024" tabindex="-1">November 26, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Cluster autoscaler and node auto-provisioning support the C4 machine family in GKE version 1.28.15-gke.1159000, 1.29.10-gke.1227000 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_21_2024" data-text="November 21, 2024" tabindex="-1">November 21, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>If your GKE cluster was created before version 1.26, you can now <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/migrate-cgroupv2">migrate it to cgroupv2</a>. This migration enables the use of <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/pod-bursting-gke#availability-in-gke">Pod bursting</a> in Autopilot mode.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_20_2024" data-text="November 20, 2024" tabindex="-1">November 20, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now specify a custom resource policy as a compact placement policy with node auto-provisioning in clusters running GKE version 1.31.1-gke.2010000 or later. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/compact-placement#compact-placement-node-autoprovision">Use compact placement for node auto-provisioning</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

      <div><p>GKE version 1.31 introduces increased scalability, allowing users to create clusters with up to 65,000 nodes. For clusters exceeding 5,000 nodes, a quota increase is required. Contact Google Cloud support to request this increase.</p></div>

<h2 id="November_18_2024" data-text="November 18, 2024" tabindex="-1">November 18, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Performance horizontal Pod autoscaling (HPA) profile is now available in Preview for new and existing GKE clusters running version 1.31.2-gke.1138000 or later. This feature speeds up HPA reaction time and enables quick recalculation of up to 1,000 HPA objects. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/horizontal-pod-autoscaling#hpa-profile">Configuring Performance HPA profile</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="November_11_2024" data-text="November 11, 2024" tabindex="-1">November 11, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Clusters now have unified and flexible configuration, allowing you to modify control plane access and cluster node settings at any time, without the need to recreate the cluster. This eliminates the previous distinction between private and public clusters.  All clusters support this flexibility and utilize DNS-based endpoints for secure and direct control plane access from any network, removing the need for bastion hosts or proxies.  You can still enhance security with measures like VPC Service Controls.</p>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/network-isolation">About network isolation in GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>DNS-based access for GKE clusters control plane is now generally available. This capability provides each cluster with a unique domain name system (DNS) name or fully-qualified domain name (FQDN). Access to clusters is controlled through IAM policies, eliminating the need for bastion hosts or proxy nodes. Authorized users can connect to the control plane from different cloud networks, on-prem deployments, or from remote locations, without relying on proxies.</p>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/network-isolation">About network isolation in GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_08_2024" data-text="November 08, 2024" tabindex="-1">November 08, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The machine family of N1 custom machine types (like <code translate="no" dir="ltr">custom-1-1024</code>) is now accurately labeled as &quot;N1&quot; for all node versions later than 1.31.2-gke.1115000.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_07_2024" data-text="November 07, 2024" tabindex="-1">November 07, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE clusters running version 1.28 or later now support automatic application monitoring in public preview. Enabling this feature automatically deploys <code translate="no" dir="ltr">PodMonitoring</code> configurations to capture key metrics for supported workloads like Apache Airflow, Istio, and RabbitMQ. These metrics are integrated with Cloud Monitoring dashboards for observability. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-automatic-application-monitoring">Configure automatic application monitoring for workloads</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_06_2024" data-text="November 06, 2024" tabindex="-1">November 06, 2024</h2>

information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The GKE Volume Populator is generally available on GKE clusters running version 1.31.1-gke.1729000 or later. This feature provides a way to automate data transfer from a Google Cloud Storage bucket source storage to a destination PersistentVolumeClaim backed by a Parallelstore instance. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/volume-populator">Transfer data from Cloud Storage during dynamic provisioning using GKE Volume Populator</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_05_2024" data-text="November 05, 2024" tabindex="-1">November 05, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Cloud TPU v6e machine types are now in public preview for GKE clusters running version 1.30.4-gke.1167000 or later. These TPU VMs (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">ct6e-standard</code>) are available in the following zones: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">us-east5-b</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">europe-west4-a</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">us-east1-d</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">asia-northeast1-b</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">us-south1-a</code>. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/plan-tpus">Plan TPUs in GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><strong>Generally available</strong>: In GKE version 1.26 and later, Hyperdisk Balanced volumes can be created in Confidential mode for <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/confidential-gke-nodes#confidential-mode-for-hyperdisk-balanced">custom boot disks</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/confidential-gke-nodes#creating_chd_pv">persistent volumes</a> and attached to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/confidential-gke-nodes">Confidential GKE Nodes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_31_2024" data-text="October 31, 2024" tabindex="-1">October 31, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>Clusters that are experiencing stale endpoint resources and stale kube-dns entries are likely affected by <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126578">Kubernetes issue #126578</a>. Your cluster is most likely affected if endpoint resources consistently have incorrect Pod IPs. This issue has been fixed in the following GKE versions or later:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.28.14-gke.1115000</li>
<li>1.29.9-gke.1207000</li>
<li>1.30.5-gke.1171000</li>
<li>1.31.1-gke.1414000</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE control plane authority is now generally available with version 1.31.1-gke.1846000 or later. GKE control plane authority provides enhanced visibility, security controls, and customization of the GKE control plane. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-control-plane-authority">About GKE control plane authority</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>For GKE clusters running version 1.31.1-gke.1146000 or later, Cloud Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) v3 machine types are generally available. These TPU VMs (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">ct3-hightpu-4t</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ct3p-hightpu-4t</code>) are currently available in us-east1-d, europe-west4-a, us-central1-a, us-central1-b, and us-central1-f. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/tpus">TPUs in GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Weighted load balancing for GKE External LoadBalancer Services is now available in Preview. Weighted load balancing is a more efficient way to distribute traffic to nodes based on the number of serving Pods they have backing the Service. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/service-load-balancer">About LoadBalancer Services</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_29_2024" data-text="October 29, 2024" tabindex="-1">October 29, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Instance Group Managers for node pools created with version 1.30.5-gke.1523000 or later and 1.31.1-gke.1869000 or later will now have <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instance-groups/update-on-repair"><em>update on repair</em></a> enabled by default. This will allow labels to persist upon Spot VM preemption.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Three new metrics are added for measuring node and workload startup latency:</p>

<ul>
<li><p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/node/latencies/startup</code>: The total startup latency of a node, from the GCE instance&#39;s <code translate="no" dir="ltr">CreationTimestamp</code> to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Kubernetes Node Ready</code> for the first time.</p></li>
<li><p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/pod/latencies/pod_first_ready</code>: The Pod end-to-end startup latency (from Pod <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Created</code> to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Ready</code>), including image pulls. This metric is available for clusters with GKE version 1.31.1-gke.1678000 or later.</p></li>
<li><p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/autoscaler/latencies/per_hpa_recommendation_scale_latency_seconds</code>: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA) scaling recommendation latency (the time between metrics being created and the corresponding scaling recommendation being applied to the API server) for the HPA target. This metric is available for clusters running the following versions or later:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.30.4-gke.1348001</li>
<li>1.31.0-gke.1324000</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_28_2024" data-text="October 28, 2024" tabindex="-1">October 28, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The A3 Edge (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">a3-edgegpu-8g</code>) machine type with H100 80GB GPUs attached is now available on GKE Standard clusters. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus/about-gpus">About GPUs</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_25_2024" data-text="October 25, 2024" tabindex="-1">October 25, 2024</h2>

and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The new release of the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/gateway-api#gateway_controller">GKE Gateway controller</a> (2024-R2) is now generally available. With this release, the GKE Gateway controller provides the following new capabilities:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/api-types/referencegrant/">ReferenceGrant</a> support</li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-gateway-resources#configure_cloud_armor">Cloud Armor backend security policy support for internal Gateways</a></li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-gateway-resources#configure-region">Regional selection for regional multi-cluster Gateways</a></li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-gateway-resources#configure_service_capacity">Traffic-based autoscaling for single cluster Gateways</a></li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Conformance:</strong></p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/implementations/#google-kubernetes-engine">GKE Gateway is now conformant to Gateway APIs v1.1.0</a></li>
</ul>

<p>To learn more about our GKE Gateway controller capabilities, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gatewayclass-capabilities">supported capabilities per GatewayClass</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now use NVIDIA H100 80GB GPUs on GKE in the following smaller machine types: </p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">a3-highgpu-1g</code> (1 GPU)</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">a3-highgpu-2g</code> (2 GPUs)</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">a3-highgpu-4g</code> (4 GPUs)</li>
</ul>

<p>These machine types are available through <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/provisioningrequest">Dynamic Workload Scheduler Flex Start mode</a>, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/spot-vms">Spot VMs</a> in GKE Standard mode clusters, or <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-spot-pods">Spot Pods</a> in GKE Autopilot mode clusters. You can only provision these machine types if there&#39;s available capacity in your region.</p>

<p>GKE continues to support the 8 GPU H100 80GB machine types: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">a3-highgpu-8g</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">a3-megagpu-8g</code>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE clusters with the control plane running version 1.29.1-gke.1425000 or later, TPU slice nodes support <code translate="no" dir="ltr">SIGTERM</code> signals that alert the node of an imminent shutdown. The imminent shutdown notification is configurable up to five minutes in TPU nodes. To configure GKE to terminate your workloads gracefully within this notification timeframe, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/handle-disruption-gpu-tpu">Manage GKE node disruption for GPUs and TPUs</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_16_2024" data-text="October 16, 2024" tabindex="-1">October 16, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.31.1-gke.1621000 and later, the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kube_pod_resource_request</code> metric and the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kube_pod_resource_limit</code> metric are exported as part of the the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/control-plane-metrics#scheduler">scheduler metrics package</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_15_2024" data-text="October 15, 2024" tabindex="-1">October 15, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>On GKE Autopilot clusters running version 1.30 and later, partner workloads that set AppArmor profiles might unexpectedly be rejected at admission. This might include installations of Prisma Defender, Wiz Runtime Sensor, Sentinel One Agent, Checkpoint CloudGuard, Aqua Security Enforcer and Splunk OTEL Collector.</p>

<p>The following GKE versions contain a fix for this issue:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.30.5-gke.1355000 and later</li>
<li>1.31.1-gke.1621000 and later</li>
</ul>

<p>Clusters in any release channel can be created on or upgraded to these versions. For details, see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/upgrading-a-cluster#upgrade_cp">Manually upgrading the control plane</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>For newly-created VPC Peering-based clusters running version 1.27 or later, traffic from the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kube-apiserver</code> to nodes routes through <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/control-plane-node-communication/#konnectivity-service">the Konnectivity service</a>. For existing VPC Peering-based clusters, GKE gradually migrates your cluster to use the Konnectivity service.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now create workloads with multiple network interfaces in GKE Autopilot clusters running version 1.29.5-gke.1091000 and later or version 1.30.1-gke.1280000 and later. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/setup-multinetwork-support-for-pods">Setup multi-network support for Pods</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_11_2024" data-text="October 11, 2024" tabindex="-1">October 11, 2024</h2>

<h2 id="October_04_2024" data-text="October 04, 2024" tabindex="-1">October 04, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>CVE-2024-45016 was discovered in the Linux kernel, which can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes.</p>

<p>For more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-057">GCP-2024-057 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Ray Operator on GKE is now generally available on 1.29 and later. Ray Operator is a GKE add-on that lets you manage and scale <a href="https://docs.ray.io/">Ray</a> applications. To learn more, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/ray-on-gke/concepts/overview">Ray Operator documentation</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The following beta APIs were added in Kubernetes 1.31 and are available in GKE version 1.31.1-gke.1361000 and later:</p>

<ul>
<li>networking.k8s.io/v1beta1/ipaddresses</li>
<li>networking.k8s.io/v1beta1/servicecidrs</li>
</ul>

<p>Enabling both APIs at the same time enables the Multiple Service CIDRs Kubernetes feature in a GKE cluster. For more information, see the following resources:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/1880-multiple-service-cidrs/README.md">KEP-1880 - Multiple Service CIDRs</a></li>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/network/extend-service-ip-ranges/">Extended Service IP ranges</a></li>
</ul>

<p>During the beta phase, you can only create Service CIDRs in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">34.118.224.0/20</code> reserved IP address range to avoid possible issues with overlapping IP address ranges.</p></div>
    </div>

<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded from version 1.27 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v12716">1.27.16-gke.1342000</a> with this release.</li>

<h2 id="October_01_2024" data-text="October 01, 2024" tabindex="-1">October 01, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE now supports the Parallelstore CSI driver in allowlisted general availability (GA), which means that you can reach out to your Google support team to use the service under <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">GA terms</a>.</p>

<p>Parallelstore accelerates AI/ML training and excels at saturating individual compute clients, ensuring that expensive compute resources are efficiently used. The product demonstrated a 3.9x training time improvement and 3.7x better throughput improvement compared to native ML framework data loaders and saturates single clients NIC bandwidth at 90%+.</p>

<p>For details, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/parallelstore-for-gke">About the GKE Parallelstore CSI driver</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.30.3-gke.1639000 and later and 1.31.0-gke.1058000 and later, GKE can handle GPU and TPU node disruptions by notifying you in advance of a shutdown and by gracefully terminating your workloads. This feature is generally available. For details, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/handle-disruption-gpu-tpu">Manage GKE node disruption for GPUs and TPUs</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
