<h2 id="September_24_2024" data-text="September 24, 2024" tabindex="-1">September 24, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>GKE clusters using <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/network-policy">the Network Policy feature</a> and Pods specifying a <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.30/#container-v1-core">hostPort</a> might have experienced networking connectivity issues after control plane upgrades. As a precaution, GKE disabled auto-upgrades for potentially impacted clusters.</p>

<p>The following GKE versions contain a fix for this issue and are safe to manually upgrade to:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.27.16-gke.1342000 or later</li>
<li>1.28.13-gke.1078000 or later</li>
<li>1.29.8-gke.1157000 or later</li>
<li>1.30.4-gke.1282000 or later</li>
<li>1.31 or later</li>
</ul>

<p>GKE control plane upgrades are now resumed and clusters will be auto-upgraded when the patch version becomes an auto-upgrade target for your clusters, honoring maintenance windows and exclusions.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_23_2024" data-text="September 23, 2024" tabindex="-1">September 23, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes clusters with Windows nodes where <code translate="no" dir="ltr">BUILTIN\Users</code> may be able to read container logs and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">AUTHORITY\Authenticated</code> Users may be able to modify container logs. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-054">GCP-2024-054 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>For GPU node pools created in GKE Standard clusters running version 1.30.1-gke.115600 or later, GKE automatically installs the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">default</code> NVIDIA GPU driver version corresponding to the GKE version if you don&#39;t specify the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gpu-driver-version</code> flag.</p></div>

<h2 id="September_10_2024" data-text="September 10, 2024" tabindex="-1">September 10, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>We previously identified a potential issue that could cause downtime for traffic directed to your GKE-managed internal passthrough Network Load Balancers after certain cluster operations, like node upgrades. This issue specifically affected clusters with GKE subsetting and Services configured with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">externalTrafficPolicy=Cluster</code>. See the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#August_14_2024">Aug 14, 2024 release note</a> for details.</p>

<p>A fix for this issue is now available. We recommend upgrading your GKE cluster&#39;s control plane to the following patch versions or later:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.27.16-gke.1258000</li>
<li>1.28.13-gke.1024000</li>
<li>1.29.8-gke.1057000</li>
<li>1.30.4-gke.1129000</li>
<li>1.31.0-gke.1506000</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_06_2024" data-text="September 06, 2024" tabindex="-1">September 06, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2024-r34_version_updates" data-text="(2024-R34) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2024-R34) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="rapid-channel_85" data-text="Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Rapid channel</h3><p>There are no new releases in the Rapid channel.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="regular-channel_85" data-text="Regular channel" tabindex="-1">Regular channel</h3><p>There are no new releases in the Regular channel.</p></section>

</div></div>

<h2 id="September_04_2024" data-text="September 04, 2024" tabindex="-1">September 04, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>For GKE versions 1.29 and later, the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gke-metrics-agent</code> Pod runs with the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">prometheus-metrics-collector</code> container in addition to the existing <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gke-metrics-agent</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">core-metrics-exporter</code> containers. This change might result in an increase in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Service time series ingestion requests per minute</code> quota; however, there is no additional cost.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="August_27_2024" data-text="August 27, 2024" tabindex="-1">August 27, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Starting from version 1.30.3-gke.1451000, new and upgraded GKE clusters support the GKE Metrics Server updates where the addon-resizer runs in the cluster&#39;s control plane instead of worker nodes.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_26_2024" data-text="August 26, 2024" tabindex="-1">August 26, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2024-36978</li>
</ul>

<p>For more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-049">GCP-2024-049 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2024-41009</li>
</ul>

<p>For more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-048">GCP-2024-048 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_21_2024" data-text="August 21, 2024" tabindex="-1">August 21, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE support for <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/hyperdisk-ml">Hyperdisk ML</a> as an attached persistent disk option is now generally available. Support is available for both Autopilot and Standard clusters running GKE versions 1.30.2-gke.1394000 and later.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_apis_in_131" data-text="Deprecated APIs in 1.31" tabindex="-1">Deprecated APIs in 1.31</h4>

<ul>
<li>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs were <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-29">deprecated in 1.29</a> in favor of newer versions:
<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3 FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration</code>
<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.29, will no longer be served in 1.32</li>
<li>instead, use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1</code>, available since 1.29</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
<li>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion</code> field in the Node API is deprecated and will not be populated starting in v1.33. The field is currently populated with the kubelet version, not the kube-proxy version, and might not accurately reflect the kube-proxy version in use. For more information, see <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-network/4004-deprecate-kube-proxy-version">KEP-4004</a>.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><h4 id="131_is_now_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="1.31 is now available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">1.31 is now available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.31 is now available in the Rapid channel. For more information about the content of Kubernetes 1.31, read the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.31.md#changelog-since-v1300">Kubernetes 1.31 Release Notes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_in-tree_volume_support" data-text="Deprecated in-tree volume support" tabindex="-1">Deprecated in-tree volume support</h4>

<ul>
<li>The Ceph CephFS (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/cephfs</code>) and RBD (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/rbd</code>) volume plugins are <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#urgent-upgrade-notes">deprecated since 1.28</a> and are removed in 1.31.</li>
<li><p>To determine if you have volumes/pods using RBD or Ceph volumes, run the following commands. If either of them print output, then you are using a deprecated volume type.</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl describe pv | egrep \-i &#39;Type: \*(RBD|CephFS)&#39;</code></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl describe pod \-A | egrep \-i &#39;Type: \*(RBD|CephFS)&#39;</code></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>Switch to use an RBD or CephFS CSI driver (like the CSI drivers provided at <a href="https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/">https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/</a>), or a Google Cloud-managed solution like <a href="https://cloud.google.com/filestore/docs/csi-driver">Filestore</a>.</p></li>
<li><p>For more information, refer to the <a href="https://groups.google.com/a/kubernetes.io/g/dev/c/U0--uNBae0Q/m/yhmcWHi3AAAJ?utm_medium=email&amp;utm_source=footer">OSS Kubernetes announcement</a> and <a href="https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/">https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/</a></p></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><h4 id="new_features" data-text="New features" tabindex="-1">New features</h4>

<p>The following features are new in Kubernetes 1.31:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/extend-kubernetes/api-extension/custom-resources/#custom-resource-field-selectors">Field selectors for custom resources</a> is beta and enabled by default.</li>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#matchlabelkeys">matchLabelKeys</a> and <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#mismatchlabelkeys">mismatchLabelKeys</a> for Pod Affinity and Pod Anti Affinity are beta and enabled by default.</li>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#traffic-distribution">Traffic distribution for Services</a> is beta and enabled by default.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/4006-transition-spdy-to-websockets">Transition kubectl from SPDY to WebSockets</a> is beta and enabled by default.</li>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes/#read-only-mounts">Recursive Read-only (RRO) mounts</a> is beta and enabled by default.</li>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/job/#success-policy">Job success/completion policy</a> is beta and enabled by default.</li>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/#persistentvolume-deletion-protection-finalizer">Always Honor PersistentVolume Reclaim Policy</a> is beta and enabled by default.</li>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/#proc-access">procMount security context option</a> is beta and enabled by default.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2024-39503</li>
</ul>

<p>For more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-047">GCP-2024-047 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The C4 machine family is generally available in the following versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>Standard clusters in version 1.29.2-gke.1521000 and later. To use this family in GKE Standard, you can use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--machine-type</code> flag when creating a cluster or node pool.</li>
<li>Autopilot clusters in 1.30.3-gke.1225000 and later. To use this family in GKE Autopilot, you can use the Performance compute class when scheduling your workloads.</li>
<li>Cluster autoscaler and node auto-provisioning are supported in 1.30.3-gke.1225000 and later.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_16_2024" data-text="August 16, 2024" tabindex="-1">August 16, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.29.7-gke.1238000-1.30, and 1.30.3-gke.1571000 or later, node pools use regional instance templates instead of global instance templates. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instance-templates#regional_and_global_instance_templates">Regional and global instance templates</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>We&#39;ve identified a potential issue that may cause downtime for traffic coming to your <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balancing">GKE managed Internal passthrough Network Load Balancers</a>, after certain cluster operations like node upgrades. This issue specifically affects clusters with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balancing#subsetting">GKE Subsetting</a> and Services with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">externalTrafficPolicy=Cluster</code>.</p>

<p>This issue is more likely to occur in clusters with more than 25 nodes. To prevent this issue altogether, we recommend updating your Service configuration to use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">externalTrafficPolicy=Local</code>. If you&#39;re already experiencing downtime, scale up the number of pods backing your LoadBalancer to provide immediate relief. A fix for this issue will be available in upcoming GKE releases.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_13_2024" data-text="August 13, 2024" tabindex="-1">August 13, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.30 and later, there is a <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gcp-compute-persistent-disk-csi-driver/pull/1658">workaround in the PDCSI driver</a> for privileged workloads that access container namespaces with hostpath. The workaround delays NodeUnstage until attached filesystems are no longer in use. Under certain conditions, the privileged hostpath workloads may cause a container&#39;s mount namespace to be retained longer than the container&#39;s lifecycle. The workaround addresses an issue where the driver could proceed with detaching a GCE persistent disk even if the block device filesystem is still in use.</p>

<p>With this fix, the PDCSI driver will validate that an attached block device is no longer in use prior to unmounting it from a GKE node.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Custom compute classes are a new set of capabilities in GKE that provide an API for fine-grained control over fallback compute priorities, autoscaling configuration, obtainability and node consolidation. Custom compute classes offer enhanced flexibility and control over your GKE compute infrastructure so that you can ensure optimal resource allocation for your workloads. You can use custom compute classes in GKE version 1.30.3-gke.1451000 and later. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-custom-compute-classes">About custom compute classes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="August_06_2024" data-text="August 06, 2024" tabindex="-1">August 06, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now keep a GKE Standard cluster on a minor version for longer with the Extended release channel. Clusters running 1.27 or later can be enrolled in the Extended channel, and automatically receive security patches during the extended support period after the end of standard support. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/release-channels#extended">Get long-term support with the Extended channel</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_02_2024" data-text="August 02, 2024" tabindex="-1">August 02, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/gpu-operator/latest/overview.html">NVIDIA GPU Operator</a> can now be <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gpu-operator">used as an alternative</a> to fully managed GKE for both Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu node images. Choose this <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/gpus#manage-gpu-stack">option to manage your GPU stack</a> if you&#39;re looking for a consistent multi-cloud experience, already using the NVIDIA GPU Operator, or have software reliant on it.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_01_2024" data-text="August 01, 2024" tabindex="-1">August 01, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Autopilot nodes use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/using-gvnic">Google Virtual NIC (gVNIC)</a> for 1.30.2-gke.1023000 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now enable NCCL Fast Socket on your multi-GPU Autopilot workloads. <a href="https://github.com/google/nccl-fastsocket">NCCL Fast Socket</a> is a transport layer plugin designed to improve NVIDIA Collective Communication Library (NCCL) performance on Google Cloud. To enable NCCL Fast Socket on GKE Autopilot, you must use a GKE Autopilot cluster with control plane version 1.30.2-gke.1023000 or later. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/nccl-fast-socket#nccl-fastsocket-autopilot">Improve workload efficiency using NCCL Fast Socket</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>GKE Autopilot versions 1.28.6-gke.1317000 and later fixes a known issue for ephemeral storage requests.  If the combined ephemeral storage requests across all containers in your workload exceed 10 GiB, your workload will be rejected with an error message. This differs from earlier versions, which admitted the workload if it requested more than 10 GiB while only actually provisioning 10 GiB, which would result in workload eviction when the workload used more than 10 GiB.</p>

<p>To ensure uninterrupted operation with GKE Autopilot versions 1.28.6-gke.1317000 and later, do the following:</p>

<ul>
<li>Verify that containers injected by webhooks don&#39;t cause Pods to exceed the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/autopilot-resource-requests#hardware-min-max">maximum Autopilot resource limits</a>.</li>
<li>Adjust workload resource requests to account for any containers that may be injected by webhooks.</li>
<li>If any Pods are rejected after updating, reduce their ephemeral storage requests to meet the limit for your workload configuration.</li>
</ul>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/autopilot-resource-requests#autopilot-resource-management">Automatic resource management in Autopilot</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now keep a GKE Standard cluster on a minor version for longer with the Extended release channel. Clusters running 1.27 or later can be enrolled in the Extended channel, and automatically receive security patches during the extended support period after the end of standard support. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/release-channels#extended">Get long-term support with the Extended channel</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_26_2024" data-text="July 26, 2024" tabindex="-1">July 26, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>With GKE patch version 1.30.1-gke.115600 and later, if you don&#39;t specify the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gpu-driver-version</code> flag when creating new GPU node pools, then GKE automatically installs the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">default</code> GPU driver version that corresponds to the GKE version. If you prefer to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gpus#installing_drivers">manually install the GPU driver</a>, set <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gpu-driver-version=disabled</code>. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gpus#create-gpu-pool-auto-drivers">Create a GPU node pool</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_25_2024" data-text="July 25, 2024" tabindex="-1">July 25, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.30.2-gke.1100 and later, the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">_CMDLINE</code> field is removed from kubelet log entries to reduce log volumes.</p>

<p>If you need to access <code translate="no" dir="ltr">_CMDLINE</code> information, you have two options:</p>

<ol>
<li><p><strong>SSH into the node</strong>:</p>

<ul>
<li>SSH into the relevant node.</li>
<li>Run the following command: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ps aux | grep kubelet</code>.</li>
</ul></li>
<li><p><strong>Search cloud logging</strong>:</p>

<ul>
<li>Use the Cloud Logging interface or API.</li>
<li><p>Apply the following filter to search kubelet startup logs:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Carbon" syntax-guessed><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">resource</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-k">type</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"k8s_node"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-nx">log_name</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"projects/{PROJECT_ID}/logs/kubelet"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-nx">resource</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">labels</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">cluster_name</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"{CLUSTER_NAME}"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-nx">SEARCH</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"`FLAG:`"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></li>
</ul>

<p>Remember to replace <code translate="no" dir="ltr">{PROJECT_ID}</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">{CLUSTER_NAME}</code> with the appropriate values for your environment.</p></li>
</ol></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_24_2024" data-text="July 24, 2024" tabindex="-1">July 24, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>In GKE versions starting from 1.29.4-gke.1542000 and earlier than 1.29.7-gke.1008000, while Anthos Service Mesh is enabled, Pods that utilize Google Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver volumes might encounter scheduling issues, with this error message:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Transact-SQL" syntax-guessed><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-n">Pod</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-ss">"your-pod-name"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-k">is</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nl">invalid</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">spec.volumes[x</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">]</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nl">name</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">Duplicate</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-k">value</span><span class="devsite-syntax-err">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-ss">"gke-gcsfuse-tmp"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">spec</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">initContainers</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">x</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">]</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nl">name</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">Duplicate</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-k">value</span><span class="devsite-syntax-err">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-ss">"gke-gcsfuse-sidecar"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-err">]</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
<p>This issue has been resolved in GKE version 1.29.7-gke.1008000.</p></div>
    </div>

      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<p>For more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-045">GCP-2024-045 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>

      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2024-36972</li>
</ul>

<p>For more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-044">GCP-2024-044 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/committed-use-discounts-overview#spend_based">Compute flexible committed use discounts</a> (CUDs), previously known as Compute Engine Flexible CUDs, have been <a href="https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/containers-kubernetes/compute-flexible-cud-expands-to-gke-autopilot-and-cloud-run">expanded</a> to include several GKE Autopilot and Cloud Run SKUs (see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/cud">GKE CUD documentation</a> for details). The legacy GKE Autopilot CUD will be removed from sale on October 15, 2024. GKE Autopilot CUDs purchased before this date will continue to apply through their term.</p></div>
    </div>

      <div><p>Ray Operator on GKE is now generally available in the Rapid channel. Ray Operator is a GKE add-on that allows you to manage and scale <a href="https://docs.ray.io/">Ray</a> applications. To learn more, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/ray-on-gke/concepts/overview">Ray Operator documentation</a>.</p></div>

<h2 id="July_03_2024" data-text="July 03, 2024" tabindex="-1">July 03, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h3 id="2024-r22_version_updates" data-text="(2024-R22) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2024-R22) Version updates</h3>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A remote code execution vulnerability, <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2024-6387">CVE-2024-6387</a>, was recently discovered in OpenSSH. The vulnerability exploits a race condition that can be used to obtain access to a remote shell, enabling attackers to gain root access. This vulnerability has a Critical severity for GKE. An expedited rollout is in progress to make patch versions available.</p>

<p>For patch versions and mitigation steps, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-040">GCP-2024-040 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now preload data or container images in new nodes on GKE, enabling faster workload deployment and autoscaling. This feature is Generally Available and production-ready, with support for Autopilot and Terraform. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/data-container-image-preloading">Use secondary boot disks to preload data or container images</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Managed DCGM Metrics Package is now available in Preview for both GKE Standard and Autopilot clusters running version 1.30.1-gke.1204000 and later. </p>

<p>You can now configure Autopilot and Standard clusters to export a predefined list of DCGM metrics emitted by GKE Managed DCGM exporter including metrics for GPU performance, utilization, and I/Os in the GPU node pools with GKE-managed NVIDIA drivers. These metrics are collected by Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus. You can view the curated DCGM metrics in the Observability Tab on the Kubernetes Clusters page or in Cloud Monitoring. </p>

<p>For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/dcgm-metrics">Collect and view DCGM metrics</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_02_2024" data-text="July 02, 2024" tabindex="-1">July 02, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>A faulty component in the Persistent Disk CSI (PDCSI) driver may cause mount failures for NVMe block devices on specific GKE clusters. This issue affects machine types that exclusively use the NVMe interface for attached Persistent Disks, such as third-generation machine types, T2A instances, and Confidential VMs. For more details, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/persistent-disks#choose_an_interface">About persistent disks</a>.</p>

<p>Impacted GKE versions include:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.30.2-gke.1023000</li>
<li>1.27.15-gke.1012000</li>
<li>1.27.14-gke.1100000</li>
</ul>

<p>Mount failures will log errors indicating difficulties verifying and re-linking the GCE Persistent Disk. You will see log errors like this:</p>

<p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;Error when getting device path: rpc error: code = Internal desc = error verifying GCE PD (&quot;$PVC&quot;) is attached: failed to find and re-link disk $PVC with udevadm after retrying for 3s: couldn&#39;t get serial number for disk $PVC at device path /dev/$NVME_PATH: google_nvme_id failed for device &quot;/dev/$NVME_PATH&quot; with output [**numbers**]: exit status 1&quot;</code></p>

<p>This issue will be resolved in the next GKE releases. In the meantime, if you are experiencing mount failures, upgrade your cluster to the default version 1.30.1-gke.1329000 for the 1.30 release channel or 1.27.14-gke.1059000 for the 1.27 release channel.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_28_2024" data-text="June 28, 2024" tabindex="-1">June 28, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2024-26923</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-039">GCP-2024-039 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Resource requests for <code translate="no" dir="ltr">anetd</code> Pods have been increased from 200mil CPU and 110m memory to 205mil CPU and 230m memory. In some cases, if the CPU and memory budgets on the nodes are limited, GKE might evict workloads to facilitate <code translate="no" dir="ltr">anetd</code> during control plane upgrades. This can occur if your clusters are being upgraded from earlier versions to one of the following versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.28.5-gke.1217000 and later</li>
<li>1.29 and later</li>
<li>1.30 and later</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="June_14_2024" data-text="June 14, 2024" tabindex="-1">June 14, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>For GKE clusters running versions later than 1.28.10-gke.1141000, the NEG, Ingress, L4 internal load balancer, and L4 RBS controllers skip processing nodes that are missing the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">thetopology.kubernetes.io/zone</code> label until the zone information is ready. The load balancer controllers no longer block sync operations when a node is introduced without the label.</p></div>
    </div>

      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2024-26584</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-035">GCP-2024-035 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>

<h2 id="May_27_2024" data-text="May 27, 2024" tabindex="-1">May 27, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A new vulnerability (CVE-2024-4323) has been discovered in Fluent Bit that could result in remote code execution. Fluent Bit versions 2.0.7 through 3.0.3 are affected.</p>

<p>GKE doesn&#39;t use a vulnerable version of Fluent Bit and is <strong>unaffected</strong>.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-031">GCP-2024-031 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_24_2024" data-text="May 24, 2024" tabindex="-1">May 24, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE now provides insights and recommendations to create a backup plan for unprotected clusters that have existed for more than 7 days. These insights and recommendations are currently available in <code translate="no" dir="ltr">us-central1-a</code>. See <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/backup-for-gke/concepts/backup-for-gke">Backup for GKE</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/backup-for-gke/how-to/data-protection-recommendations">protect clusters with Backup for GKE</a> documents for details.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_22_2024" data-text="May 22, 2024" tabindex="-1">May 22, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The GKE Container Security API is now enabled automatically when GKE Enterprise is enabled on a project.  This change ensures the security and compliance features are ready for use as part of GKE Enterprise activation.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The C4 machine family is available in Public Preview for Standard clusters running GKE version 1.29.2-gke.1521000 and later. You can select this family by using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--machine-type</code> flag when creating a cluster or node pool. The following limitations apply:</p>

<ul>
<li>GKE versions prior to 1.29.2-gke.1521000 might encounter a volume device path mounting error which can cause Pods to be stuck in a Pending state. If you encounter this issue, try deleting and re-creating the Pod, to trigger re-processing of the volume mount.</li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/confidential-gke-nodes">Confidential GKE nodes</a> are not supported in Public Preview.</li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/local-ssd">Local SSD</a> is not supported.</li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/nested-virtualization">Nested virtualization</a> is not supported in Public Preview.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_21_2024" data-text="May 21, 2024" tabindex="-1">May 21, 2024</h2>

<h2 id="May_15_2024" data-text="May 15, 2024" tabindex="-1">May 15, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Added a release note to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#May_16_2023">May 16, 2023</a> for 1.27 available in the Rapid channel. This release note was previously only added to the Release notes (Rapid channel only) page by mistake.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A vulnerability (CVE-2023-52620) was discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-030">GCP-2024-030 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_14_2024" data-text="May 14, 2024" tabindex="-1">May 14, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A vulnerability (CVE-2024-26642) was discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-029">GCP-2024-029 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_13_2024" data-text="May 13, 2024" tabindex="-1">May 13, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A vulnerability (CVE-2024-26581) was discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-028">GCP-2024-028 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_10_2024" data-text="May 10, 2024" tabindex="-1">May 10, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Container Threat Detection (KTD) fails to deploy on Autopilot clusters running the following GKE versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.28.6-gke.1095000 to 1.28.7-gke.1025000</li>
<li>1.29.1-gke.1016000 to 1.29.1-gke.1781000</li>
</ul>

<p>To mitigate this issue, upgrade the cluster to version 1.28.7-gke.1026000 or later, or to 1.29.2-gke.1060000 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In new Standard clusters running GKE version 1.29 and later, GKE assigns IP addresses for GKE Services from a Google-managed range: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">34.118.224.0/20</code> by default. With this feature, you don&#39;t need to specify your own IP address range for Services. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/alias-ips#cluster_sizing_secondary_range_svcs">Subnet secondary IP address range for Services</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A vulnerability (CVE-2024-26643) was discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-026">GCP-2024-026 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The 2024-R13 release notes were updated on June 7th, 2024 with the following:</p>

<p><strong>Regular channel</strong></p>

<p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Regular channel were <strong>not</strong> upgraded from version 1.28 to version 1.29.1-gke.1589018. That release note was published by mistake</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_02_2024" data-text="May 02, 2024" tabindex="-1">May 02, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Starting in GKE 1.30, the metric <code translate="no" dir="ltr">scheduler_pod_scheduling_duration_seconds</code> in <a href="http://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/control-plane-metrics#scheduler">control plane metrics package</a> will no longer be available, as a result of <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119049">deprecation in the upstream OSS</a>. The replacement metric <code translate="no" dir="ltr">scheduler_pod_scheduling_sli_duration_seconds</code> will be exported as part of the the control plane metrics package instead.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The new release of the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/gateway-api#gateway_controller">GKE Gateway controller</a> (2024-R1) is now <strong>generally available</strong>. With this release, the GKE Gateway controller will provide the following new capabilities and fixes:</p>

<p><strong>New capabilities:</strong></p>

<ul>
<li>Gateway API CRDs v1.0.0</li>
<li>Cloud Armor backend security policy support for Regional external Gateways</li>
<li>Self-managed certificates with Certificate Manager on Regional internal &amp; external Gateways</li>
<li>Google-managed certificates with Certificate Manager on Regional internal &amp; external Gateways [<strong>Preview</strong>]</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Bug fixes:</strong></p>

<ul>
<li>Fixed missing permissions to MCI service agent role for regional SSL policy</li>
</ul>

<p>To learn more about our GKE Gateway controller capabilities, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gatewayclass-capabilities">supported capabilities per GatewayClass</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><h4 id="new_apis_in_130" data-text="New APIs in 1.30" tabindex="-1">New APIs in 1.30</h4>

<p>The following APIs are new in Kubernetes 1.30:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1</code> <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ValidatingAdmissionPolicy</code></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_features_in_130" data-text="Deprecated features in 1.30" tabindex="-1">Deprecated features in 1.30</h4>

<p>The Ceph CephFS (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/cephfs</code>) and RBD (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/rbd</code>) volume plugins are deprecated since 1.28 and will be removed in a future release.</p>

<p>To determine if you have volumes/pods using RBD or Ceph volumes, run the following commands. If either of them print output, then you are using a deprecated volume type:</p>

<ul>
  <li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl describe pv | egrep -i 'Type: *(RBD|CephFS)'</code></li>
  <li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl describe pod -A | egrep -i 'Type: *(RBD|CephFS)'</code></li>
</ul>

<p>Switch to use an RBD or CephFS CSI driver (like the CSI drivers provided in the <a href="https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/">Ceph CSI driver project</a>), or a Google Cloud-managed solution like <a href="https://cloud.google.com/filestore/docs/csi-driver">Filestore</a>. For more information, refer to the OSS Kubernetes announcement and to the <a href="https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/">Ceph CSI driver project</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><h4 id="130_is_now_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="1.30 is now available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">1.30 is now available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.30 is now available in the Rapid channel. For more information about the content of Kubernetes 1.30, read the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.30.md#changelog-since-v1290">Kubernetes 1.30 Release Notes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><h4 id="new_features_in_130" data-text="New features in 1.30" tabindex="-1">New features in 1.30</h4>

<p>The following features are new in Kubernetes 1.30:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/validating-admission-policy/">ValidatingAdmissionPolicy</a> is GA and now enabled by default.</li>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/custom-resources/custom-resource-definitions/#validation-ratcheting">Validation Ratcheting</a> is beta and enabled by default, and makes CustomResourceDefinitions even safer and easier to manage.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_apis_in_130" data-text="Deprecated APIs in 1.30" tabindex="-1">Deprecated APIs in 1.30</h4>

<p>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs were previously deprecated in 1.29 in favor of newer versions:</p>

<ul>
  <li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3 FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration</code>: Deprecated since 1.29, will no longer be served in 1.32. Instead, use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1</code>, which is available since Kubernetes 1.29</li>
  <li>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion</code> field in the Node API is deprecated and will
    not be populated starting in v1.33. The field is currently populated with the kubelet version,
    not the kube-proxy version, and might not accurately reflect the kube-proxy version in use.
    For more information, see <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-network/4004-deprecate-kube-proxy-version">KEP-4004</a>.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_30_2024" data-text="April 30, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 30, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now configure access to private image registries that use private certificates using a containerd configuration file. For details, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/customize-containerd-configuration">Customize containerd configuration in GKE nodes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE 1.29.2-gke.1355000 and later, GPU workloads using the Accelerator compute class in GKE Autopilot support scheduling multiple GPU pods on a single node. To schedule multiple GPU Pods on the same node, specify the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gke-accelerator-count</code> node selector with a value that&#39;s higher than the Pod GPU request. For details, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-gpus#request-gpus">Deploy GPU workloads in GKE Autopilot</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>A <a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/marketplace/product/google/rag-on-gke">Quick Start Solution</a> and <a href="https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/ai-on-gke/tree/main/applications/rag#rag-on-gke-application">Reference Architecture</a> are now available for developing and deploying Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) applications on GKE. RAG improves the quality of Large Language Model (LLM) responses for a specific application. For example, RAG can enable a customer service chatbot to access help center articles, a shopping assistant to tap into product catalogs and customer reviews, or a travel booking agent to access up-to-date flight and hotel information.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_29_2024" data-text="April 29, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 29, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Cloud DNS additive VPC scope is now available in Preview. You can now configure your GKE clusters to add GKE headless Service entries to your Cloud DNS private zone visible from your VPC networks, on top of using Cloud DNS (cluster scope) as your GKE DNS provider.</p>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cloud-dns#dns_scopes">Cloud DNS scopes for GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Dual-stack LoadBalancer Services are now generally available with GKE. You can now create a dual-stack GKE cluster and expose GKE Services using either IPv4, IPv6 ,or a combination of both, depending on your <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ipFamilyPolicy</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ipFamilies</code> specs.</p>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/service-load-balancer-parameters#ipv4ipv6_dual-stack_loadbalancer_service">GKE LoadBalancer Service parameters</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_26_2024" data-text="April 26, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 26, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now use the node system configuration file in GKE to enable and use Linux huge pages in your Pods. For instructions, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-system-config#huge-page-options">Linux huge page configuration options</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Sandbox supports the use of NVIDIA GPUs (H100, A100, L4, and T4) in Public Preview in GKE version 1.29.2-gke.1108000 and later on both Standard and Autopilot clusters. GKE Sandbox provides an extra layer of security to prevent untrusted code from affecting the host kernel on your cluster nodes. For GPUs, while GKE Sandbox doesn&#39;t mitigate all NVIDIA driver vulnerabilities, it helps protect against Linux kernel vulnerabilities. For details, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/sandbox-pods#gpus">GPUs in GKE Sandbox</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Standard clusters now support nested virtualization. For details, including requirements and limitations, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/nested-virtualization">Use nested VMs with GKE Standard clusters</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_25_2024" data-text="April 25, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 25, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A vulnerability (CVE-2024-26585) was discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-024">GCP-2024-024 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_24_2024" data-text="April 24, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 24, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>A known issue causes a subset of Pods in GKE Autopilot clusters to occasionally become stuck during termination or creation. As a result, we temporarily disabled bursting in Autopilot clusters that were created or upgraded to version 1.29.2-gke.1060000 and later on or after April 24, 2024. Clusters that enabled bursting prior to April 24, 2024 continue to support bursting.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_19_2024" data-text="April 19, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 19, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>A bug in the Image streaming feature might cause containers to fail because of missing files.</p>

<p>Containers running on a node with image streaming enabled on specific GKE versions might fail to be created with the following error:</p>

<p>&quot;CreateContainer in sandbox from runtime service failed&quot; err=&quot;rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create containerd container: failed to mount [PATH]: too many levels of symbolic links&quot;</p>

<p>The following GKE versions are impacted:</p>

<ul>
<li>All 1.28 versions</li>
<li>All 1.29 versions</li>
</ul>

<p>We&#39;re working on fixing this issue. In the meantime, if you&#39;re impacted by this issue, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/image-streaming#disable">disable Image streaming</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_18_2024" data-text="April 18, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 18, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

<h2 id="April_16_2024" data-text="April 16, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 16, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The Z3 machine family is generally available in Standard clusters running for GKE 1.25 and later. You can select this family by using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--machine-type</code> flag when creating a cluster or node pool. The following limitations apply:</p>

<ul>
<li>Node auto-provisioning for Z3 is supported in 1.29 and later.</li>
<li>GKE Autopilot is supported in 1.29 and later.</li>
<li>Z3 machines are gracefully terminated during host maintenance.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_12_2024" data-text="April 12, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 12, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GPUDirect-TCPX is now supported on GKE version 1.27 and later and requires the following patch versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>For GKE version 1.27, use GKE patch version 1.27.7-gke.1121000 or later.</li>
<li>For GKE version 1.28, use GKE patch version 1.28.8-gke.1095000 or later.</li>
<li>For GKE version 1.29, use GKE patch version 1.29.3-gke.1093000 or later.</li>
</ul>

<p>To use GPUDirect-TCPX, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gpu-bandwidth-gpudirect-tcpx">Maximize GPU network bandwidth with GPUDirect-TCPX and multi-networking</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_10_2024" data-text="April 10, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 10, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>This note was updated on June 3, 2024. The GKE version required for N4 machine type support has been updated.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The N4 machine family is generally available in GKE Standard clusters running on GKE 1.29.3-gke.1121000 and later. You can select this family by using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--machine-type</code> flag when creating a cluster or node pool. The following limitations apply:</p>

<ul>
<li>Confidential GKE nodes is not supported.</li>
<li>Local SSD is not supported.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">hyperdisk-balanced</code> is the only supported boot disk type.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>This note was updated on June 3, 2024. The GKE version required for N4 machine type support has been updated.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_09_2024" data-text="April 09, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 09, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Cloud Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) are now available in GKE Autopilot clusters running version 1.29.2-gke.1521000 or later. To learn more, visit <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/tpus-autopilot">Deploy TPU workloads on GKE Autopilot</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_08_2024" data-text="April 08, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 08, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

<h2 id="April_05_2024" data-text="April 05, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 05, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GPU NVIDIA Multi-Process Service (MPS) is available in version 1.27.7-gke.1088000 and later, which allows multiple workloads to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/nvidia-mps-gpus">share a single NVIDIA GPU hardware accelerator with NVIDIA MPS</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_04_2024" data-text="April 04, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 04, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A Denial-of-Service (DoS) vulnerability (CVE-2023-45288) was recently discovered in multiple implementations of the HTTP/2 protocol, including the golang HTTP server used by Kubernetes. The vulnerability could lead to a DoS of the Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) control plane.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-022">GCP-2024-022 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_03_2024" data-text="April 03, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 03, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The GKE compliance dashboard now offers compliance evaluation for CIS Kubernetes Benchmark 1.5, Pod Security Standards (PSS) Baseline, and PSS Restricted standards in Preview. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/fleet-management/docs/about-compliance-dashboard">About the compliance dashboard</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE threat detection is now available in Preview. Threats against the Kubernetes control plane impacting your GKE Enterprise clusters are now visible in the GKE security posture dashboard. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-gke-threat-detection">About GKE threat detection</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_02_2024" data-text="April 02, 2024" tabindex="-1">April 02, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Observability for Google Kubernetes Engine: Added a dashboard for Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) metrics on the Observability tab of both the cluster listing and cluster details pages for GKE clusters. The charts on this dashboard are populated with data only if the cluster <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/tpus">has TPU nodes</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-metrics#system-metrics">GKE system metrics</a> is enabled. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/view-observability-metrics">View observability metrics</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.27 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#v1287">1.28.7-gke.1026000</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.28 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#v1287">1.28.7-gke.1026000</a> with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_19_2024" data-text="March 19, 2024" tabindex="-1">March 19, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Workloads running on GKE clusters with COS-based nodes may experience DNS resolution issues. The likelihood of impact is low and not all clusters are impacted. The issue is resolved on the following minimal GKE node versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>For 1.27: 1.27.11-gke.1118000</li>
<li>For 1.28: 1.28.7-gke.1100000</li>
<li>For 1.29: 1.29.2-gke.1217000</li>
</ul>

<p>Clusters with a node version that is lower than 1.27.3-gke.1200 are not affected.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Cilium cluster-wide network policies are now generally available with the following GKE versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.28.6-gke.1095000 or later</li>
<li>1.29.1-gke.1016000 or later</li>
</ul>

<p>You can now control your GKE workloads&#39; ingress and egress traffic cluster-wide, without being bound to a namespace for your network policies. This new capability is intended to streamline network policies for GKE platform administrators looking for a uniform way to apply policies across namespaces or application teams.</p>

<p>Cilium cluster-wide network policy is available in all <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/docs/concepts/gke-editions#edition_features">GKE editions</a>.</p>

<p>To learn more, read <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-cilium-network-policy">Control cluster-wide communication using network policies</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_15_2024" data-text="March 15, 2024" tabindex="-1">March 15, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2024-1085</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-018">GCP-2024-018 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_14_2024" data-text="March 14, 2024" tabindex="-1">March 14, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>A previous version of the GKE logging agent that rolled out in GKE version 1.28.7-gke.1100000 contained a security vulnerability. This version has been immediately removed.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_11_2024" data-text="March 11, 2024" tabindex="-1">March 11, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Opportunistic bursting and lower Pod minimums are now available on newly created GKE Autopilot clusters at version 1.29.2-gke.1060000 or later, and on existing clusters created at 1.26 or later that have been fully upgraded (including all nodes) to 1.29.2-gke.1060000 or later. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/pod-bursting-gke">Configure Pod bursting on GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Secret Manager add-on for GKE is now available.  With the add-on, you can access the secrets stored in Secret Manager as volumes mounted in Kubernetes Pods.  The add-on is supported on Standard and Autopilot clusters versioned 1.29 and later.  For more info, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/secret-manager-managed-csi-component">Use Secret Manager add-on with GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Private clusters created on GKE versions 1.29.0-gke.1384000 and later use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/network-overview#public-cluster-psc">Private Service Connect (PSC)</a> for nodes to privately communicate with the control plane. There is no price increase for using GKE private clusters running on PSC.</p>

<p>For private clusters created with a different GKE version, the clusters continue to use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/private-cluster-concept#the_control_plane_in_private_clusters">VPC Peering</a> for node-to-control plane communication.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_08_2024" data-text="March 08, 2024" tabindex="-1">March 08, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>Managed ASM installation and node scaling fails on GKE Autopilot clusters on versions between 1.28.6-gke.1095000 and 1.28.7-gke.1025000 and on versions between 1.29.1-gke.1016000 and 1.29.1-gke.1781000. To mitigate this issue, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-upgrades-autopilot#manual-upgrade">upgrade the cluster</a> to version 1.28.7-gke.1026000 or later, or 1.29.2-gke.1060000 or later.</p>

<p>With 2024-R07, clusters created in the Rapid channel are defaulting to an affected version. To avoid creating a cluster on an affected version, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/creating-an-autopilot-cluster#set-version">manually specify</a> version 1.28.7-gke.1026000 or later, or 1.29.2-gke.1060000 or later when creating clusters in the Rapid channel.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>For GKE versions later than 1.29.1-gke.1760000, the NEG, Ingress, L4 internal load balancer with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/service-load-balancer#subsetting">subsetting</a>, and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/external-svc-lb-rbs#backend_service-based">L4 RBS controllers</a> will skip processing the nodes missing the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gke-zonal-topology#zonal-placement-methods"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">topology.kubernetes.io/zone</code></a> label until the zone information is ready. The load balancer controllers will no longer block sync operations when a node is introduced without the label.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_07_2024" data-text="March 07, 2024" tabindex="-1">March 07, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2023-3611</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-017-gke">GCP-2024-017 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Starting in GKE 1.29.2-gke.1035000, you can configure Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) with Google Managed OAuth Client for load balancers configured through GKE Ingress. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ingress-configuration#enable_with_google_managed_oauth_client">Ingress configuration on Google Cloud</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p><strong>(2024-R07) Version updates</strong></p>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.</strong></p>

<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.26 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v12711">1.27.11-gke.1018000</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.27 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v12711">1.27.11-gke.1018000</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.29 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.29.md#v1291">1.29.1-gke.1589000</a> with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GPU workloads running in Autopilot mode can now be configured using the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-gpus">Accelerator Compute Class</a>. This configuration supports resource reservations, Compute Engine committed use discounts, and a new pricing model in GKE versions 1.28.6-gke.1095000 and later, and 1.29.1-gke.1143000 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>NVIDIA H100 (80&nbsp;GB) GPUs are <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-gpus">now available</a> in GKE Autopilot mode in versions 1.28.6-gke.1369000 or later, and 1.29.1-gke.1575000 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_28_2024" data-text="February 28, 2024" tabindex="-1">February 28, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/performance-pods">Performance Compute Class</a>,  designed for running whole-machine CPU workloads, is available in Autopilot mode from versions 1.28.6-gke.1369000 and 1.29.1-gke.1575000 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_26_2024" data-text="February 26, 2024" tabindex="-1">February 26, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>This note was updated on March 20, 2024. The links to the security bulletins related to CVE-2024-0193 and CVE-2023-3610 have been updated.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>CVE-2023-3776</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-014">GCP-2024-014 security bulletin</a>.</p></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE now supports Gemma (2B, 7B), Google&#39;s new state-of-the-art open models. To learn more, refer to the following guides:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/tutorials/serve-gemma-gpu-tgi">Serve Gemma on GKE with GPUs using Hugging Face TGI</a></li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/tutorials/serve-gemma-gpu-vllm">Serve Gemma on GKE with GPUs using vLLM</a></li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/tutorials/serve-gemma-gpu-tensortllm">Serve Gemma on GKE with GPUs using TensorRT-LLM</a></li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/tutorials/serve-gemma-tpu-saxml">Serve Gemma on GKE with TPUs using SaxML</a></li>
</ul>

<p>Deployment to GKE is also supported via Vertex AI Model Garden as part of our Hugging Face, Vertex AI, and GKE integration.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2024-0193</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-012">GCP-2024-012 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>

<ul>

    </div>
