<h2 id="February_21_2024" data-text="February 21, 2024" tabindex="-1">February 21, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/stateful-ha">GKE Stateful HA Operator</a> is now available in GA starting in GKE versions 1.28.5-gke.1113000 and later, or 1.29.0-gke.1272000 and later.  The GKE Stateful HA Operator is enabled in new Autopilot clusters and opt-in for new Standard clusters.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_20_2024" data-text="February 20, 2024" tabindex="-1">February 20, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>A bug in the image streaming feature might cause containers to fail because of a missing file or files.</p>

<p>Containers running on a node with image streaming enabled on the following versions might fail to start or run with errors informing that certain files don&#39;t exist. The following are examples of such errors:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">No such file or directory</code></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">Executable file not found in $PATH</code></li>
</ul>

<p>The following GKE versions are impacted:</p>

<ul>
<li>For 1.27: 1.27.10-gke.1077000 and later</li>
<li>For 1.28: All 1.28 versions</li>
<li>For 1.29: All 1.29 versions</li>
</ul>

<p>GKE is working on fixing the issue. In the meantime, if you are impacted by this issue, please <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/image-streaming#disable">disable image streaming</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now use the GKE API to apply Resource Manager tags to your GKE nodes. GKE attaches these tags to the underlying Compute Engine VMs. You can use these tags to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/tags-firewall-policies">selectively enforce Cloud Firewall network firewall policies</a>. This feature is generally available in GKE version 1.28 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE now delivers insights and recommendations if your cluster&#39;s <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/credential-rotation">Certificate Authority (CA)</a> is expired or will expire in the next 180 days. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/credential-rotation#gke-notification-for-expiring">Find clusters with expiring or expired credentials</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Kubernetes Engine best practice observability packages, including <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-logs#control-plane-logs">control plane logs</a>, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-metrics#control-plane-metrics">control plane metrics</a>, and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-metrics#ksm-package">kube state metrics</a> are now enabled by default for new <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/docs/setup/overview#requirements">managed GKE Enterprise clusters</a> to ensure availability of necessary data when it&#39;s needed for troubleshooting or optimization. Control plane metrics and kube state metrics are <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/gke-editions#edition_features">included</a> in GKE <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/pricing#enterprise_edition">Enterprise Edition</a> at <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/pricing#anthos-costs">no additional charge</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_16_2024" data-text="February 16, 2024" tabindex="-1">February 16, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>The following GKE versions might cause Ubuntu node pools to enter an unhealthy state. Don&#39;t create or upgrade your Ubuntu node pools using these versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.25.16-gke.1497000</li>
<li>1.26.13-gke.1189000</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2023-6932</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-011">GCP-2024-011 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_15_2024" data-text="February 15, 2024" tabindex="-1">February 15, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) and VerticalPodAutoscaler (VPA) may stop autoscaling all workloads in a cluster if it contains misconfigured <code translate="no" dir="ltr">autoscaling/v2</code> HPA objects. The issue impacts clusters running earlier patch versions of GKE version 1.27 and 1.28 (for example, 1.27.3-gke.100).</p>

<p>The fix is available in following cluster versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.27.5-gke.1300 and later</li>
<li>1.28.1-gke.1400 and later</li>
<li>1.29 and later</li>
</ul>

<p>We recommend that affected customers upgrade clusters to these versions to prevent HPA and VPA from misbehaving when there is at least one misconfigured HPA object.</p>

<p>We recommend that affected customers correct misconfigured <code translate="no" dir="ltr">autoscaling/v2</code> HPA objects by making sure the fields in <code translate="no" dir="ltr">spec.metrics.resource.target</code> match, for example:</p>

<ul>
<li>When <code translate="no" dir="ltr">spec.metrics.resource.target.type</code> is <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Utilization</code> then target should be <code translate="no" dir="ltr">averageUtilization</code>;</li>
<li>When <code translate="no" dir="ltr">spec.metrics.resource.target.type</code> is <code translate="no" dir="ltr">AverageValue</code> then target should be <code translate="no" dir="ltr">averageValue</code>.</li>
</ul>

<p>For more details on how to configure <code translate="no" dir="ltr">autoscaling/v2</code> HPA objects, see the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/horizontal-pod-autoscale-walkthrough/#autoscaling-on-multiple-metrics-and-custom-metrics">HorizontalPodAutoscaler Kubernetes documentation</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_14_2024" data-text="February 14, 2024" tabindex="-1">February 14, 2024</h2>

to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes.</p>

<ul>

</ul>

    </div>

<h2 id="February_06_2024" data-text="February 06, 2024" tabindex="-1">February 06, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Clusters on control plane versions 1.26.6-gke.1900 and later might encounter intermittent connection establishment failures.</p>

<p>The chances of failures are low and it doesn&#39;t affect all clusters. The failures should stop completely after a few days since the symptom onset.</p>

<p>Alternatively, upgrade to the following versions instead, which are not affected by this issue:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.26.13-gke.1052000 and later.</li>
<li>1.27.10-gke.1055000 and later.</li>
<li>1.28.6-gke.1095000 and later.</li>
<li>1.29.1-gke.1016000 and later.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_02_2024" data-text="February 02, 2024" tabindex="-1">February 02, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>FQDN network policies are now generally available with the following GKE versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.26.4-gke.500 and later.</li>
<li>1.27.1-gke.400 and later.</li>
<li>1.28 and later.</li>
</ul>

<p>You can further control your GKE workloads&#39; egress traffic to a public or private service or endpoint by using a network policy matching a fully-qualified domain name or a regular expression.</p>

<p>FQDN Network Policy is only available and supported with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/docs/concepts/gke-editions">GKE Enterprise</a>.</p>

<p>To learn more, read <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/fqdn-network-policies">Control Pod egress traffic using FQDN network policies</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_01_2024" data-text="February 01, 2024" tabindex="-1">February 01, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A security vulnerability, CVE-2024-21626, has been discovered in <code translate="no" dir="ltr">runc</code> where a user with permission to create Pods on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes might be able to gain full access to the node file system.</p>

<p>For instructions and more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-005">GCP-2024-005 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now encrypt Pod-to-Pod traffic between nodes in the same cluster or in a multi-cluster environment natively with GKE. Inter-node transparent encryption is now generally available, only with GKE Enterprise, for GKE clusters in the following versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.26.9-gke.1024000 and later.</li>
<li>1.27.6-gke.1506000 and later.</li>
<li>1.28.2-gke.1098000 and later.</li>
<li>1.29 and later.</li>
</ul>

<p>To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/enable-inter-node-transparent-encryption">Encrypt your data in-transit in GKE with user-managed encryption keys</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_31_2024" data-text="January 31, 2024" tabindex="-1">January 31, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">africa-south1</code></a> region in Johannesburg, South Africa is now available.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Clusters that are running GPUs and are upgraded from 1.26 to a 1.27 patch version earlier than 1.27.8 might experience issues with their nodes&#39; GPU device plugins (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">nvidia-gpu-device-plugin</code>). Do the following steps depending on the state of your cluster:</p>

<ul>
<li>If your cluster is running version 1.26 and has GPUs, don&#39;t manually upgrade your cluster until version 1.27.8 is available in your cluster&#39;s release channel. As of the publishing date of this release note, 1.27.8 patch versions are available in the Rapid and Regular channels.</li>
<li>If your cluster is running an earlier 1.27 patch version and the nodes are affected, restart the nodes or manually delete the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">nvidia-gpu-device-plugin</code> Pod on the nodes (the add-on manager will create a new working plugin).</li>
<li>If your cluster is using auto-upgrades, this doesn&#39;t affect you as automatic upgrades will only move clusters to patch versions with the fix.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_24_2024" data-text="January 24, 2024" tabindex="-1">January 24, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The following vulnerability was discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2023-6817</li>
</ul>

<p>For instructions and more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-004-gke">GCP-2024-004 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_22_2024" data-text="January 22, 2024" tabindex="-1">January 22, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>We have identified several clusters where users have granted Kubernetes privileges to the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">system:authenticated</code> group, which includes all users with a Google account. These types of bindings are <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/best-practices/rbac#default-roles-groups">not recommended</a>, as they violate the principle of least privilege and grant access to very large groups of users. See guidance under &#39;What should I do&#39; for instructions on how to find these types of bindings.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-003">GCP-2024-003 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_19_2024" data-text="January 19, 2024" tabindex="-1">January 19, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> This is a correction of the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#August_29_2023">Aug 29, 2023 release note</a>, which incorrectly stated the qualifying patch versions for TPUs. See the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/tpus#availability">availability chart</a> for version qualification information.</span></aside>
<p>You can create Cloud Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) nodes in GKE to run AI workloads, from training to inference models. GKE manages your cluster by automating TPU resource provisioning, scaling, scheduling, repairing, and upgrading. GKE provides TPU infrastructure metrics in Cloud Monitoring, TPU logs, and error reports for better visibility and monitoring of TPU node pools in GKE clusters. TPUs are available with GKE Standard clusters. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/tpus">About TPUs in GKE</a>. See <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/tpus#availability">TPU availability in GKE</a> to find the TPU availability depending on the machine type and version.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_18_2024" data-text="January 18, 2024" tabindex="-1">January 18, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The following vulnerability was discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2023-6111</li>
</ul>

<p>For instructions and more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2024-002-gke">GKE security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_11_2024" data-text="January 11, 2024" tabindex="-1">January 11, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#v1283">1.28.3-gke.1286000</a> is now the default version in the Rapid channel.</li>
<li>The following versions are now available in the Rapid channel:

<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.29.md#v1290">1.29.0-gke.1381000</a></li>
</ul></li>

<li>1.27.7-gke.1293000</li>
<li>1.28.4-gke.1083000</li>
</ul></li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.23 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12417">1.24.17-gke.2364000</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.24 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12516">1.25.16-gke.1041000</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.25 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v12611">1.26.11-gke.1055000</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.26 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1278">1.27.8-gke.1067000</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.27 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#v1283">1.28.3-gke.1203001</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.28 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#v1283">1.28.3-gke.1203001</a> with this release.</li>

    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="129_is_now_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="1.29 is now available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">1.29 is now available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.29 is now available in the Rapid channel. For more information about the content of Kubernetes 1.29, read the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.29.md#urgent-upgrade-notes">Kubernetes 1.29 Release Notes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="new_apis" data-text="New APIs" tabindex="-1">New APIs</h4>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1 FlowSchema</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">PriorityLevelConfiguration</code>
<ul>
<li>Notable changes in <code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1</code>:
<ul>
<li>The PriorityLevelConfiguration <code translate="no" dir="ltr">spec.limited.nominalConcurrencyShares</code> field only defaults to 30 when unspecified, and an explicit value of 0 is not changed to 30.</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_in-tree_volume_support" data-text="Deprecated in-tree volume support" tabindex="-1">Deprecated in-tree volume support</h4>

<ul>
<li>The Ceph CephFS (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/cephfs</code>) and RBD (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/rbd</code>) volume plugins are deprecated in 1.28 and will be removed in a future release.</li>
<li>To determine if you have volumes or Pods using RBD or Ceph volumes, run the following commands. If either of them print output, then you are using a deprecated volume type.
<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl describe pv | egrep -i &#39;Type: *(RBD|CephFS)&#39;</code></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl describe pod -A | egrep -i &#39;Type: *(RBD|CephFS)&#39;</code></li>
</ul></li>
<li>Switch to use an RBD or CephFS CSI driver, such as the drivers provided in the <a href="https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/">Ceph CSI</a> GitHub repo, or use a Google-managed solution such as <a href="https://cloud.google.com/filestore/docs/csi-driver">Filestore</a>.</li>
<li>For more information, refer to the <a href="https://groups.google.com/a/kubernetes.io/g/dev/c/U0--uNBae0Q/m/yhmcWHi3AAAJ">OSS Kubernetes announcement</a> and the <a href="https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/">Ceph CSI</a> GitHub repo.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="new_features" data-text="New Features" tabindex="-1">New Features</h4>

<ul>
<li>The beta
<a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/validating-admission-policy/">ValidatingAdmissionPolicy feature</a> can be opted into by <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/use-beta-apis#available-beta-apis">enabling the beta APIs</a>.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">initContainers</code> can now be configured as <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers/">sidecar containers</a> and kept running alongside normal containers in a Pod. This is only supported by nodes running version 1.29 or later, so avoid using this feature in Pods if there are nodes running earlier versions in the cluster.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_apis" data-text="Deprecated APIs" tabindex="-1">Deprecated APIs</h4>

<ul>
<li>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs are <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-29">deprecated in 1.29</a> in favor of newer versions:
<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3 FlowSchema</code>,
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">PriorityLevelConfiguration</code>
<ul>
<li>Deprecated since 1.29</li>
<li>Instead, use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1</code>, available since 1.29</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
<li>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion</code> field in the Node API is deprecated and will not be populated starting in version 1.33. The field is currently populated with the kubelet version, not the kube-proxy version, and might not accurately reflect the kube-proxy version in use. For more information, see <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-network/4004-deprecate-kube-proxy-version">KEP-4004</a>.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="removed_sha-1_certificate_support" data-text="Removed SHA-1 certificate support" tabindex="-1">Removed SHA-1 certificate support</h4>

<ul>
<li>Starting from version 1.29, GKE no longer supports webhook backends that use TLS certificates signed with the insecure SHA-1 algorithm. To prevent impact on your clusters, you must replace incompatible certificates of <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/#configure-admission-webhooks-on-the-fly">webhook servers</a> and <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/extend-kubernetes/api-extension/apiserver-aggregation/">extension API servers</a> before upgrading your clusters to version 1.29.</li>
<li>GKE will not auto-upgrade clusters with webhook backends using incompatible certificates to 1.29 until you replace the certificates or until version 1.28 reaches end of life. For more information, refer to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/sha1-1-29">Ensure compatibility of TLS certificates before upgrading to GKE 1.29</a>.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="removed_apis" data-text="Removed APIs" tabindex="-1">Removed APIs</h4>

<p>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs are
<a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-29">removed in 1.29</a>
in favor of newer versions:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2 FlowSchema</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">PriorityLevelConfiguration</code>
<ul>
<li>Deprecated since 1.26</li>
<li>Instead, use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3</code> available since 1.26, or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1</code>, available since 1.29</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_08_2024" data-text="January 08, 2024" tabindex="-1">January 08, 2024</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>GKE clusters in Autopilot mode no longer require workload-level logging to be enabled. Pass <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--logging=SYSTEM</code> to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/container/clusters/create-auto"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">create-auto</code></a> or <a href="https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/container/clusters/update"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">update</code></a> to disable workload logs.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_19_2023" data-text="December 19, 2023" tabindex="-1">December 19, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now modify the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">vm.max_map_count</code> Linux kernel attribute for nodes in a GKE Standard cluster node pool using the node system configuration. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-system-config#sysctl-options">Sysctl configuration options</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_18_2023" data-text="December 18, 2023" tabindex="-1">December 18, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The GKE NEG controller now supports IPv6 endpoints with GKE version 1.28.4-gke.1083000 and later.</p>

<p>With this new capability, when you create a dual stack Service in a dual stack GKE cluster, any NEGs associated with the Service will now contain both IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints. Existing dual stack Services utilizing NEGs (i.e. Ingress, Services using Standalone NEGs) will be migrated from &quot;IPv4 only&quot; endpoints to &quot;IPv4 + IPv6&quot; endpoints.</p>

<p>The migration will be completed in approximately one hour. In the event that a NEG contains a single endpoint, you might experience brief downtime of  approximately 1-2 minutes during the migration of that endpoint.</p>

<p>Note that Having IPv6 endpoints in NEGs doesn&#39;t necessarily mean that the load balancer uses IPv6 for communication. How the load balancer communicates with your Pod depends on how the BackendService is configured, such as fields like <code translate="no" dir="ltr">IpAddressSelectionPolicy</code>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>All newly created Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Autopilot clusters starting with 1.27.4-gke.900 will automatically collect and send metrics from the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/managing-metrics#ksm-package">kube-state-metrics package</a> to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/managed-prometheus">Managed Service for Prometheus</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_15_2023" data-text="December 15, 2023" tabindex="-1">December 15, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <strong>Observability</strong> tab in the cluster details page for each cluster and in the GKE cluster list page now shows GPU metrics if the cluster has GPU nodes. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/view-observability-metrics">View observability metrics</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_14_2023" data-text="December 14, 2023" tabindex="-1">December 14, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>We&#39;ve identified an issue with configuring TLS for Gateways in clusters running GKE version 1.28.4-gke.1083000. This affects TLS configurations using either an <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/secure-gateway#secure-using-ssl-certificate">SSLCertificate</a> or a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/secure-gateway#secure-using-certificate-manager">CertificateMap</a>. If you&#39;re upgrading a cluster with existing Gateways, updates made to the Gateway will fail. For brand new Gateways, the load balancers won&#39;t be provisioned. This issue will be fixed in an upcoming GKE 1.28 patch version.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>An attacker who has compromised the Fluent Bit logging container could combine that access with high privileges required by Anthos Service Mesh (on clusters that have enabled it) to escalate privileges in the cluster.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-047">GCP-2023-047 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_12_2023" data-text="December 12, 2023" tabindex="-1">December 12, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="November_29_2023" data-text="November 29, 2023" tabindex="-1">November 29, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The following GKE versions fix an issue that could cause the NVIDIA GPU driver installer image to be garbage collected on Container-optimized OS nodes:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.25.15-gke.1040000 and later</li>
<li>1.26.10-gke.1030000 and later</li>
<li>1.27.6-gke.1513000 and later</li>
<li>1.28.3-gke.1061000 and later</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Starting in GKE version 1.27.6-gke.1248000, clusters in Autopilot mode detect nodes that can&#39;t fit all DaemonSets and, over time, migrate workloads to larger nodes that can fit all DaemonSets. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/deploying-workloads-overview#autopilot-ds-best-practices">Best practices for DaemonSets on Autopilot</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Starting in GKE 1.27.7, you can configure your workloads to use TPU reservations with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-auto-provisioning#tpu">node auto-provisioning</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_22_2023" data-text="November 22, 2023" tabindex="-1">November 22, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A vulnerability (CVE-2023-5717) has been discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes.</p>

<p>GKE clusters are impacted.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-046">GCP-2023-046 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<li>1.24.17-gke.2211000</li>
<li>1.25.15-gke.1033000</li>
<li>1.25.15-gke.1049000</li>
<li>1.26.10-gke.1024000</li>
<li>1.26.10-gke.1038000</li>
<li>1.27.7-gke.1038000</li>
<li>1.27.7-gke.1056000</li>
<li>1.28.3-gke.1098000</li>
</ul></li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.23 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12417">1.24.17-gke.2230000</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.24 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12515">1.25.15-gke.1115000</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.25 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v12610">1.26.10-gke.1073000</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.26 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v12610">1.26.10-gke.1073000</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.28 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#v1283">1.28.3-gke.1118000</a> with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now run workloads on L4 GPUs in Autopilot clusters that use GKE version 1.28.3-gke.1203000 and later. For instructions, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-gpus">Deploy GPU workloads in Autopilot</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_15_2023" data-text="November 15, 2023" tabindex="-1">November 15, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Dynamic Workload Scheduler support on GKE through the Provisioning Request API launched in Preview in version 1.28. Use the Dynamic Workload Scheduler to get large atomic sets of available GPU models in GKE Standard clusters. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/provisioningrequest">Deploy GPUs for batch workloads with ProvisioningRequest</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_14_2023" data-text="November 14, 2023" tabindex="-1">November 14, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The following vulnerabilities were discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes.</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2023-4147</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-042">the GCP-2023-042 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_10_2023" data-text="November 10, 2023" tabindex="-1">November 10, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A vulnerability (CVE-2023-4004) has been discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes. GKE clusters are impacted. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-041">GCP-2023-041 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <strong>Observability</strong> tab for a GKE deployment now shows application performance metrics if the metrics are available. The supported metric sources include Istio, GKE Ingress, NGINX Ingress and gRPC, and HTTP metrics collected by using Google Managed Service for Prometheus. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/app-performance-metrics">Use application performance metrics</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_09_2023" data-text="November 09, 2023" tabindex="-1">November 09, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2023-r23_version_updates" data-text="(2023-R23) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2023-R23) Version updates</h4>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
