    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/managing-metrics#ksm-package">GKE Infrastructure Dashboards and Metrics Packages</a> are now generally available for both GKE Autopilot and Standard clusters with control plane version 1.27.2-gke.1200 and later.</p>

<p>You can now configure your Autopilot or Standard clusters to export a predefined list of metrics emitted by GKE managed kube-state-metrics (KSM) for workloads state and persistent storage. The component will run in the GKE system namespace &quot;gke-managed-cim&quot; to collect the metrics using Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus and send them to Cloud Monitoring. You can <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/view-observability-metrics">view the metrics</a> in the new <strong>Persistent</strong> and <strong>Workloads State</strong> dashboards in the Observability tab.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_08_2023" data-text="November 08, 2023" tabindex="-1">November 08, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Cloud Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) v5e is <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/tpus">generally available</a> in clusters running GKE version 1.27.2-gke.2100 and later.</p>

<p>TPU v5e is purpose-built to bring the cost-efficiency and performance required for medium- and large-scale training and inference. TPU v5e delivers up to 2x higher training performance per dollar and up to 2.5x inference performance per dollar for LLMs and gen AI models compared to Cloud TPU v4. At less than half the cost of TPU v4, TPU v5e makes it possible for more organizations to train and deploy larger, more complex AI models.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>New inference-focused Cloud Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) v5e machine types are available in GKE. These single-host TPU VMs are designed for inference workloads and contain one, four, or eight TPU v5e chips. These <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/tpus#configuration">three new TPU v5e machine types</a> (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">ct5l-hightpu-1t</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ct5l-hightpu-4t</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ct5l-hightpu-8t</code>) are currently available in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">us-central1-a</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">europe-west4-b</code> zones.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_07_2023" data-text="November 07, 2023" tabindex="-1">November 07, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A set of vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-4015, CVE-2023-4623, CVE-2023-4623, CVE-2023-4921) have been discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu nodes.</p>

<p>GKE clusters are impacted.</p>

<p>For more information, see the following security bulletins:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-037">GCP-2023-037</a></li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-038">GCP-2023-038</a></li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-039">GCP-2023-039</a></li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-040">GCP-2023-040</a></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>GKE begins automatically upgrading clusters still running version 1.24 to version 1.25 after <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-schedule#schedule-for-release-channels">1.24 reaches end of life on January 8, 2024</a>. We extended this date from October 31, 2023 to minimize disruptions around the end-of-year holiday period, and will provide patches only for critical vulnerabilities during this extended period. To learn more about the GKE minor version lifecycle, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>. GKE continues to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations#how_kubernetes_deprecations_work_with">pause automatic upgrades</a> until January 8, 2024 for clusters still using deprecated APIs removed in version 1.25, including <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/apis-1-25">beta APIs</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/podsecuritypolicy">PodSecurityPolicy</a>. We recommend that you upgrade your clusters to version 1.25 as soon as possible as GKE minor versions that have reached end of life will no longer receive security patches and bug fixes.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_02_2023" data-text="November 02, 2023" tabindex="-1">November 02, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>A bug that caused failures when many concurrent operations were run on the same cluster (such as when creating multiple node pools) has been fixed.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_31_2023" data-text="October 31, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 31, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE multi-cluster Gateway is now generally available in GKE versions 1.24 and later for GKE Standard clusters, and versions 1.26 and later for GKE Autopilot clusters. Use the <a href="https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/">Gateway API</a> to express the intent of your inbound HTTP(S) traffic into your fleet of GKE clusters. The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/gateway-api#gateway_controller">multi-cluster Gateway controller</a> deploys and manages the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/application-load-balancer">Application Load Balancers</a> that forward traffic to your applications.
 To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/enabling-multi-cluster-gateways">Enable multi-cluster Gateways</a>. For the list of supported Cloud Load Balancers and their features, refer to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gatewayclass-capabilities">GatewayClass capabilities</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_30_2023" data-text="October 30, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 30, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>You can now use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/network-intelligence-center/docs/network-analyzer/insights/kubernetes-engine/gke-node-service-account">GKE node service account insights</a> to troubleshoot common GKE node service account issues. These insights are available in the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/network-intelligence-center/docs/network-analyzer/insight-groups-types#gke-insight">Network Analyzer</a> and the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/recommender/docs/reference/rest">Recommender API</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_23_2023" data-text="October 23, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 23, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/cloud-storage-fuse-csi-driver">Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver</a> now enforces injected sidecar containers to follow the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/#restricted" class="external">Restricted Pod security standard</a>. This change is available in <a href="https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/gcs-fuse-csi-driver/releases/tag/v0.1.6" class="external">v0.1.6</a> of the driver, and in GKE clusters with control planes running the following versions: 1.24.17-gke.2146000, 1.25.14-gke.1466000, 1.26.9-gke.1494000, 1.27.6-gke.1506000, and 1.28.2-gke.1157000 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_20_2023" data-text="October 20, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 20, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>New Autopilot clusters created with versions 1.24.17-gke.2146000, 1.25.14-gke.1466000, and 1.26.9-gke.1494000 or later are now provisioned with e2-small default nodes, which are removed immediately after cluster creation. With this change, DaemonSets are guaranteed to schedule on all candidate nodes if you follow <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/deploying-workloads-overview#autopilot-ds-best-practices">best practices for DaemonSets on Autopilot</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now use the GKE API to apply Resource Manager tags to your GKE resources. GKE attaches these tags to the underlying Compute Engine VMs. You can use these tags to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/tags-firewall-policies">selectively enforce Cloud Firewall network firewall policies</a>. This feature is available in Public Preview in GKE version 1.28 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_19_2023" data-text="October 19, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 19, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2023-r22_version_updates" data-text="(2023-R22) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2023-R22) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated. There are no version updates for 2023-R21.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="no-channel_122" data-text="No channel" tabindex="-1">No channel</h3><ul>
<li>The following control plane and node versions are now available:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12417" class="external">1.24.17-gke.2155000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12514" class="external">1.25.14-gke.1474000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v1269" class="external">1.26.9-gke.1507000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1276" class="external">1.27.6-gke.1506000</a> </li>
</ul></li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="stable-channel_122" data-text="Stable channel" tabindex="-1">Stable channel</h3><ul>
<li>There are no new releases in the Stable release channel.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="regular-channel_122" data-text="Regular channel" tabindex="-1">Regular channel</h3><ul>
<li>There are no new releases in the Regular release channel.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="rapid-channel_122" data-text="Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Rapid channel</h3><ul>
<li>The following versions are now available in the Rapid channel:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12417" class="external">1.24.17-gke.2155000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12514" class="external">1.25.14-gke.1474000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v1269" class="external">1.26.9-gke.1507000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1276" class="external">1.27.6-gke.1506000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#v1282" class="external">1.28.2-gke.1157000</a> </li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following versions are no longer available in the Rapid channel: 1.28.1-gke.201, 1.28.1-gke.1066000</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Compute resources can now be reserved in advance for use with GKE. Create a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/future-reservations-overview">future reservation</a> to request assurance of important or difficult-to-obtain capacity in advance. There are no additional costs for creating future reservation requests. You only start to pay when Compute Engine provisions the reserved resources, and you&#39;re charged at the same cost as on-demand reservations.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_16_2023" data-text="October 16, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 16, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Filestore Enterprise now supports backups on GKE, allowing you to make reliable copies of your data to be stored for later use. To trigger backups on Filestore Enterprise, use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/backup-filestore-volume-snapshots">Kubernetes volume snapshots</a>. Backups are currently not supported for Filestore Enterprise instances with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/filestore/docs/multishares">multishares enabled</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_13_2023" data-text="October 13, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 13, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2023-r20_version_updates" data-text="(2023-R20) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2023-R20) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="no-channel_123" data-text="No channel" tabindex="-1">No channel</h3><ul>
<li>The following control plane and node versions are now available:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12417" class="external">1.24.17-gke.2113000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12514" class="external">1.25.14-gke.1421000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v1269" class="external">1.26.9-gke.1437000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1276" class="external">1.27.6-gke.1445000</a> </li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following control plane versions are no longer available: 1.24.17-gke.1963000, 1.25.14-gke.1256000, 1.26.9-gke.1256000</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="stable-channel_123" data-text="Stable channel" tabindex="-1">Stable channel</h3><ul>
<li>There are no new releases in the Stable release channel.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="regular-channel_123" data-text="Regular channel" tabindex="-1">Regular channel</h3><ul>
<li>There are no new releases in the Regular release channel.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="rapid-channel_123" data-text="Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Rapid channel</h3><ul>
<li>The following versions are now available in the Rapid channel:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12417" class="external">1.24.17-gke.2113000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12514" class="external">1.25.14-gke.1421000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v1269" class="external">1.26.9-gke.1437000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1276" class="external">1.27.6-gke.1445000</a> </li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following versions are no longer available in the Rapid channel: 1.24.17-gke.1963000, 1.25.14-gke.1256000, 1.26.9-gke.1256000</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Containers running in nodes in GKE version 1.28.1-gke.201 or later don&#39;t need to have privileged mode enabled to access TPUs. When upgrading a cluster to 1.28.1-gke.201 or later, we recommend removing <code translate="no" dir="ltr">privileged: true</code> from the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">securityContext</code> of any TPU workload. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/tpus#privileged-mode">Deploy TPU workloads</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Starting in GKE 1.28.1-gke.1066000, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/tpus#host_metrics">two new TPU usage metrics are available</a>: TensorCore utilization and Memory Bandwidth utilization.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_10_2023" data-text="October 10, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 10, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A Denial-of-Service (DoS) vulnerability was recently discovered in multiple implementations of the HTTP/2 protocol (CVE-2023-44487), including the golang HTTP server used by Kubernetes. The vulnerability could lead to a DoS of the Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) control plane. GKE clusters with authorized networks configured are protected by limiting network access, but all other clusters are affected.
  For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-030">GCP-2023-030 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_09_2023" data-text="October 09, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 09, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>If you are using a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/local-ssd#3gen">third generation machine series</a> (for example, C3), GKE configures Local SSD volumes as the local ephemeral storage by default. You no longer need to specify the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--ephemeral-storage-local-ssd</code> flag when provisioning clusters or node pools. When you configure Local SSD volumes as raw block storage with the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--local-nvme-ssd-block</code> flag, specifying the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">count</code> value is now optional.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_06_2023" data-text="October 06, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 06, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>A previously published release note on <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#December_14_2022">December 14, 2022</a> has been updated. Support for migration of GKE Autopilot clusters&#39; datapath provider to Dataplane V2 has been paused. We will update this release note when migration support resumes.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_05_2023" data-text="October 05, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 05, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2023-r19_version_updates" data-text="(2023-R19) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2023-R19) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="no-channel_124" data-text="No channel" tabindex="-1">No channel</h3><ul>
<li>The following control plane and node versions are now available:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1276" class="external">1.27.6-gke.1248000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1276" class="external">1.27.6-gke.1248000</a> </li>
</ul></li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="stable-channel_124" data-text="Stable channel" tabindex="-1">Stable channel</h3><ul>
<li>The following version is no longer available in the Stable channel: 1.26.5-gke.2100</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="regular-channel_124" data-text="Regular channel" tabindex="-1">Regular channel</h3><ul>
<li>There are no new releases in the Regular release channel.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="rapid-channel_124" data-text="Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Rapid channel</h3><ul>
<li>The following versions are now available in the Rapid channel:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1276" class="external">1.27.6-gke.1248000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#v1281" class="external">1.28.1-gke.1066000</a> </li>
</ul></li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>An issue was previously reported with running certain commands in container images when Image streaming is enabled. See the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#August_31_2023">August 31, 2023</a> release note for details. This issue is fixed in the following minor versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.25 with the patch versions 1.25.14-gke.1351000 and later.</li>
<li>1.25 with the patch versions 1.26.9-gke.1345000 and later.</li>
<li>1.27 with the patch versions 1.27.6-gke.100 and later.</li>
<li>1.28 with the patch version 1.28.1-gke.1157000 and later.</li>
</ul>

<p>To receive the fix, upgrade your nodes to an applicable patch version.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_04_2023" data-text="October 04, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 04, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Log rotation is misconfigured on nodes running a COS-based image type (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">cos_containerd</code>). This affects all COS-based nodes running version 1.28 or higher. As a result of this issue, your logs may fill up the disk and cause your nodes to be marked as &#39;Not Ready&#39; and to be auto-repaired. As a workaround, use a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/solutions/automatically-bootstrapping-gke-nodes-with-daemonsets">privileged DaemonSet</a> to change the logrotate path to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/usr/bin/</code> instead of <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/usr/sbin/</code> in Systemd unit <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kube-logrotate.service</code>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_02_2023" data-text="October 02, 2023" tabindex="-1">October 02, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE now delivers insights and recommendations if users have installed webhooks that intercept system resources or webhooks that have no available endpoints. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/optimize-webhooks">Ensure control plane stability when using webhooks</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_29_2023" data-text="September 29, 2023" tabindex="-1">September 29, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>This is a follow-up message to the release note regarding blue-green upgrades from <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#September_18_2023">September 18, 2023</a>. You can now resume upgrading clusters with the blue-green upgrade strategy as the issue with rollback functionality has been fixed. GKE is no longer blocking automatic upgrades due to this issue.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_21_2023" data-text="September 21, 2023" tabindex="-1">September 21, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> This is a correction of the <a href="#November_07_2022">November 07, 2022 release note</a>, which omitted the applicable version numbers for this feature.</span></aside>
<p>When you create a LoadBalancer service in GKE, the Google Cloud controllers automatically create the following <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/firewall-rules">firewall rules</a> and apply them to the GKE nodes to allow inbound connections on the Service port:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Internal load balancer with GKE subsetting or external load balancer with regional backend services (RBS)</strong>: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s2-[cluster-id]-[namespace]-[service-name]-[suffixhash]</code></li>
<li><strong>Internal load balancer without GKE subsetting or external load balancer with target pool</strong>: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s-fw-[loadbalancer-hash]</code></li>
</ul>

<p>For clusters running version 1.25 or later, these rules now include the load balancer IP address in the destination ranges field to further control the inbound connections to the nodes. You can use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud compute firewall-rules describe</code> command to check a relevant firewall. The new field in the output is similar to the following:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded><code translate="no" dir="ltr">destinationRanges:
- [LOADBALANCER_VIRTUAL_IP_ADDRESS]
</code></pre></devsite-code>
<p>For services that use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">externalIP</code>, ensure you have firewall rules that allow traffic to the specified IP addresses.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The Observability dashboards on the GKE Clusters List, Cluster Details, and Workload List pages are now customizable. Additionally, the Cluster Details dashboards can be customized across the entire project, or per-cluster for specific use cases.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_19_2023" data-text="September 19, 2023" tabindex="-1">September 19, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">me-central2</code></a> region in Dammam, Saudi Arabia is now available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_18_2023" data-text="September 18, 2023" tabindex="-1">September 18, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>GKE has temporarily paused all automatic node upgrades due to an issue with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/node-pool-upgrade-strategies#rollback-a-blue-green-upgrade">blue-green upgrades rollback</a> functionality. You can still <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/upgrading-a-cluster#upgrade_nodes">manually upgrade node pools</a> with the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/node-pool-upgrade-strategies#surge">surge upgrade</a> strategy. Do not manually upgrade node pools with blue-green upgrades. GKE is working on a fix for this issue and will post a follow-up note here when the issue is fixed and automatic upgrades resume.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>GKE clusters running version 1.28 or later block new bindings of ClusterRole <code translate="no" dir="ltr">cluster-admin</code> to User <code translate="no" dir="ltr">system:anonymous</code>, Group <code translate="no" dir="ltr">system:authenticated</code>, or Group <code translate="no" dir="ltr">system:unauthenticated</code> due to the security risks of these bindings. GKE does not block existing bindings.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_12_2023" data-text="September 12, 2023" tabindex="-1">September 12, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now use node auto-provisioning for TPU slices. With this feature, Standard clusters with GKE version 1.28 and later provision TPU node pools and multi-host TPU accelerators automatically to ensure the capacity required to schedule AI/ML workloads. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-auto-provisioning#tpu">Configuring TPU node auto-provisioning</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_11_2023" data-text="September 11, 2023" tabindex="-1">September 11, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>Compute Engine persistent disk CSI Drivers <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/gce-pd-csi-driver">deployed on clusters</a> running version 1.26 and later now support filesystem size expansion during restoration from a snapshot or a clone when the PVC data source is larger than the original volume. For more information, see the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gcp-compute-persistent-disk-csi-driver/pull/972" class="external">GitHub pull request</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_07_2023" data-text="September 07, 2023" tabindex="-1">September 07, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>With the recently released version of GKE, version 1.28, you cannot yet use the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/753" class="external">SidecarContainer</a> feature with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/alpha-clusters">alpha clusters</a>. Pods defining restartable Init containers will not start. This is a known issue that will be resolved in a future release.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>Three vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-3676, CVE-2023-3955, CVE-2023-3893) have been discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create Pods on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. These vulnerabilities affect the Windows versions of Kubelet and the Kubernetes CSI proxy.</p>

<p>GKE clusters are only affected if they include Windows nodes.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-026">GCP-2023-026 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>For GKE clusters using <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/dataplane-v2">Dataplane V2</a>, upgrades to GKE version 1.26 might cause GKE to temporarily be unable to configure workloads. In some cases, this might cause existing workloads to temporarily lose networking access. This issue does not impact new clusters and GKE clusters not using Dataplane V2. For clusters running version 1.25 with Dataplane V2 enabled, GKE has temporarily disabled auto-upgrades to version 1.26. We recommend that customers not manually upgrade their Dataplane V2-enabled cluster to GKE version 1.26. This is a known issue for GKE version 1.26 and will be fixed in a future patch version of 1.26.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_05_2023" data-text="September 05, 2023" tabindex="-1">September 05, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2023-r18_version_updates" data-text="(2023-R18) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2023-R18) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="no-channel_125" data-text="No channel" tabindex="-1">No channel</h3><ul>
<li>The following control plane and node versions are now available:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12417" class="external">1.24.17-gke.200</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12513" class="external">1.25.13-gke.200</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v1268" class="external">1.26.8-gke.200</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1275" class="external">1.27.5-gke.200</a> </li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>The following control plane versions are no longer available: 1.23.17-gke.8400, 1.23.17-gke.10000, 1.23.17-gke.10700, 1.24.14-gke.1400, 1.24.14-gke.2100, 1.25.10-gke.2100, 1.26.5-gke.1400</p></li>
<li><p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded from version 1.23 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12414" class="external">1.24.14-gke.2700</a> with this release.</p></li>
<li><p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded from version 1.24 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12510" class="external">1.25.10-gke.2700</a> with this release.</p></li>
<li><p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded from version 1.25 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12510" class="external">1.25.10-gke.2700</a> with this release.</p></li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="stable-channel_125" data-text="Stable channel" tabindex="-1">Stable channel</h3><ul>
<li>The following versions are now available in the Stable channel:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12416" class="external">1.24.16-gke.500</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12512" class="external">1.25.12-gke.500</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v1267" class="external">1.26.7-gke.500</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1274" class="external">1.27.4-gke.900</a> </li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following versions are no longer available in the Stable channel: 1.23.17-gke.8400, 1.24.14-gke.1400, 1.25.10-gke.2100, 1.27.3-gke.1700</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Stable channel will be upgraded from version 1.23 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12414" class="external">1.24.14-gke.2700</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Stable channel will be upgraded from version 1.24 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12510" class="external">1.25.10-gke.2700</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Stable channel will be upgraded from version 1.25 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12510" class="external">1.25.10-gke.2700</a> with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="regular-channel_125" data-text="Regular channel" tabindex="-1">Regular channel</h3><ul>
<li>The following versions are now available in the Regular channel:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12416" class="external">1.24.16-gke.500</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12512" class="external">1.25.12-gke.500</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v1267" class="external">1.26.7-gke.500</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1274" class="external">1.27.4-gke.900</a> </li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following versions are no longer available in the Regular channel: 1.23.17-gke.10000, 1.24.14-gke.2700, 1.25.10-gke.2700, 1.26.5-gke.2700</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Regular channel will be upgraded from version 1.23 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12415" class="external">1.24.15-gke.1700</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Regular channel will be upgraded from version 1.24 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12511" class="external">1.25.11-gke.1700</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Regular channel will be upgraded from version 1.25 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v1266" class="external">1.26.6-gke.1700</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Regular channel will be upgraded from version 1.26 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v1266" class="external">1.26.6-gke.1700</a> with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="rapid-channel_125" data-text="Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Rapid channel</h3><ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1274" class="external">1.27.4-gke.900</a> is now the default version in the Rapid channel.</li>
<li>The following versions are now available in the Rapid channel:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12417" class="external">1.24.17-gke.200</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12513" class="external">1.25.13-gke.200</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v1268" class="external">1.26.8-gke.200</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1275" class="external">1.27.5-gke.200</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#v1281" class="external">1.28.1-gke.200</a> </li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following versions are no longer available in the Rapid channel: 1.23.17-gke.10000, 1.23.17-gke.10700, 1.24.16-gke.500, 1.25.11-gke.1700, 1.26.6-gke.1700, 1.27.3-gke.1700</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.23 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v12417" class="external">1.24.17-gke.200</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.24 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v12512" class="external">1.25.12-gke.500</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.25 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#v1267" class="external">1.26.7-gke.500</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.26 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1274" class="external">1.27.4-gke.900</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.27 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#v1274" class="external">1.27.4-gke.900</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.28 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#v1281" class="external">1.28.1-gke.200</a> with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_in-tree_volume_support" data-text="Deprecated in-tree volume support" tabindex="-1">Deprecated in-tree volume support</h4>

<ul>
<li>The Ceph CephFS (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/cephfs</code>) and RBD (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/rbd</code>) volume plugins are deprecated in 1.28 and will be removed in a future
release.</li>
<li>To determine if you have volumes or Pods using RBD or Ceph volumes, run the following commands. If either of them print output, then you are using a deprecated volume type.
<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl describe pv | egrep -i &#39;Type: *(RBD|CephFS)&#39;</code></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl describe pod -A | egrep -i &#39;Type: *(RBD|CephFS)&#39;</code></li>
</ul></li>
<li>Switch to use an RBD or CephFS CSI driver, such as the drivers provided in the <a href="https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/" class="external">Ceph CSI</a> GitHub repo, or use a Google-managed solution such as <a href="https://cloud.google.com/filestore/docs/csi-driver">Filestore</a>. For more information, refer to the <a href="https://groups.google.com/a/kubernetes.io/g/dev/c/U0--uNBae0Q/m/yhmcWHi3AAAJ?utm_medium=email&amp;utm_source=footer" class="external">OSS Kubernetes announcement</a> and the <a href="https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/" class="external">Ceph CSI</a> GitHub repo.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_api_versions" data-text="Deprecated API versions" tabindex="-1">Deprecated API versions</h4>

<p>These APIs are still served in version 1.28 but are in a deprecation period:</p>

<ul>
<li>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-29" class="external">removed in 1.29</a> in favor of newer versions:
<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2 FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration</code>
<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.26</li>
<li>use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3</code> instead, available since 1.26.</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="128_is_now_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="1.28 is now available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">1.28 is now available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.28 is now available in the Rapid channel. For more information about the content of Kubernetes 1.28, read the
<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#urgent-upgrade-notes" class="external">Kubernetes 1.28 Release Notes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="new_apis" data-text="New APIs" tabindex="-1">New APIs</h4>

<ul>
<li>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl auth whoami command</code> and the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">authentication.k8s.io/v1 SelfSubjectReview API</code> enables checking the authenticated user information as seen by the server.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>To deliver a better default price-performance for applications, all GKE Autopilot clusters with control plane version 1.27.5 and later will use an SSD-based persistent disk for ephemeral storage. This change will only affect newly created clusters and new node pools created in clusters upgraded to version 1.27.5 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>The recently released version of GKE, version 1.28, has a known regression in behavior. After node restart, Pods that have started initialization before the restart will run Init containers in-parallel with regular containers instead of waiting for Init containers to complete.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>It is not yet possible to enable Gateway API support in GKE 1.28 (Standard or Autopilot), this will be fixed in an upcoming patch release to GKE 1.28. Clusters that already have Gateway API enabled before upgrading to GKE 1.28 will continue to be supported. This will not affect existing Gateways.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_01_2023" data-text="September 01, 2023" tabindex="-1">September 01, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Starting on September 1, 2023, a new automation policy is in effect where GKE automatically starts a credential rotation within 30 days of your cluster&#39;s certificate authority expiry date to ensure that your cluster doesn&#39;t have a complete outage. For example, if your cluster&#39;s CA expires on 2024-01-05, an automatic rotation starts on or after 2023-12-06. Automatic credential rotation is a critical update that <strong>ignores any configured maintenance windows</strong>.</p>

<p>This automatic rotation might cause API clients outside the cluster, such as kubectl in a local environment, to stop working unless you update those clients to use the new credentials.</p>

<p>You should plan for and perform credential rotations well in advance of your cluster CA expiring to ensure a smooth transition to new credentials and minimal workload disruptions. Don&#39;t rely on automatic rotation; it is intended to be a last resort to prevent complete outages. To learn more about the stages of credential rotation, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/credential-rotation">Rotate your cluster&#39;s credentials</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_31_2023" data-text="August 31, 2023" tabindex="-1">August 31, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>For GKE nodes running version 1.25 and later, when Image streaming is enabled, the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">mv</code> command and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">renameat2</code> system call might fail on symlink files in container images with the error message &quot;No such device or address&quot;. The issue is caused by a regression on recent Linux kernels. GKE does not currently have a fix for the issue. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/image-streaming#troubleshoot-commands-fail-sym-files">the troubleshooting section</a> for this issue.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_30_2023" data-text="August 30, 2023" tabindex="-1">August 30, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE now supports the ability to create nodes and workloads with multiple network interfaces. You can create new clusters with version 1.27 and later with multi networking enabled. The additional network interfaces on the Pods can be regular interfaces or high performance interfaces where the network interface is directly attached to the Pod. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/setup-multinetwork-support-for-pods">Setup multi-network support for Pods</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Your clusters can now perform operations, such as node auto-provisioning or version upgrades, on multiple node pools in parallel. You no longer have to wait for an operation to complete before you initiate another operation. This feature is enabled for all GKE versions. This change provides you with benefits like the following:</p>

<ul>
<li>More efficient scaling, which results in improved savings and faster workload deployment</li>
<li>Faster, less disruptive node pool upgrades</li>
<li>Fewer &quot;operation already in progress&quot; messages that could delay subsequent planned operations</li>
<li>More reliable rollback behavior to fix upgrade-related disruptions in production</li>
<li>Automatic control plane resize operations won&#39;t block other operations on the cluster</li>
</ul>

<p>The <a href="https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs" class="external">Google Cloud Platform Terraform provider</a> has also been updated to take advantage of this change.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_29_2023" data-text="August 29, 2023" tabindex="-1">August 29, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now sequence the rollout of cluster upgrades across fleets or across scopes. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-rollout-sequencing">About cluster upgrades with rollout sequencing</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now create Cloud Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) nodes in GKE to run AI workloads, from training to inference models. GKE manages your cluster by automating TPU resource provisioning, scaling, scheduling, repairing, and upgrading. GKE provides TPU infrastructure metrics in Cloud Monitoring, TPU logs, and error reports for better visibility and monitoring of TPU node pools in GKE clusters.
TPUs are available with GKE Standard clusters. GKE supports TPU v4 in version 1.26.1.gke-1500 and later, and supports TPU v5e in version 1.27.2-gke.1500 and later. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/tpus">About TPUs in GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_28_2023" data-text="August 28, 2023" tabindex="-1">August 28, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>Version 4.80.0 of the Terraform provider for Google Cloud fixes an issue observed when deploying new GKE Autopilot clusters that would destroy and re-create the cluster due to a change in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">dns_config</code> state. This version of the provider ensures that customers can deploy GKE Autopilot clusters using Cloud DNS as the default in-cluster DNS provider. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cloud-dns#tf-dns-config">Terraform plans to re-create Autopilot cluster due to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">dns_config</code> change</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_25_2023" data-text="August 25, 2023" tabindex="-1">August 25, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE now delivers insights and recommendations to ensure your workloads are ready for disruption using features such as Pod Disruption Budgets. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/workload-disruption-readiness">Ensure stateful workloads are disruption-ready</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_22_2023" data-text="August 22, 2023" tabindex="-1">August 22, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">europe-west10</code></a> region in Berlin, Germany is now available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_17_2023" data-text="August 17, 2023" tabindex="-1">August 17, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now easily identify clusters that use deprecated Kubernetes APIs removed in versions <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/apis-1-25">1.25</a>, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/apis-1-26">1.26</a>, and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/apis-1-27">1.27</a>. Kubernetes deprecation insights are now <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/viewing-deprecation-insights-and-recommendations#use-of-features">available</a> for these versions.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_16_2023" data-text="August 16, 2023" tabindex="-1">August 16, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now troubleshoot issues with <a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/monitoring/dashboards/gke-troubleshooting/cpu">CPU limit utilization</a> and <a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/monitoring/dashboards/gke-troubleshooting/memory">Memory limit utilization</a> of containers running in GKE by using the new &quot;interactive playbook&quot; dashboards in Cloud Monitoring.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/managing-metrics#ksm-package">GKE Infrastructure Dashboards and Metrics Packages</a> are now available for both GKE Autopilot and Standard clusters with control plane version 1.27.2-gke.1200 and later. You can now configure Autopilot or Standard clusters to export a predefined list of metrics emitted by GKE managed KSM (kube-state-metrics) for workloads state and Persistent Storage. These metrics are collected by Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus and are sent to Cloud Monitoring. You can also view new dashboards (Persistent and Workloads state) rendering those metrics in the Observability tab. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/view-observability-metrics">View observability metrics</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_10_2023" data-text="August 10, 2023" tabindex="-1">August 10, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Public clusters upgraded to GKE versions 1.24 and later will eventually be migrated to use Private Service Connect (PSC) for private control plane communication. After the control plane has been reconfigured, GKE schedules an update for your cluster&#39;s nodes to use the new private IP address to communicate with control plane. Each node pool is marked for recreation. You can use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/maintenance-windows-and-exclusions">maintenance windows</a> to control when your nodes are recreated. There is no price increase for using GKE public clusters running on PSC. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/network-overview#public-cluster-psc">Public clusters with Private Service Connect</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_09_2023" data-text="August 09, 2023" tabindex="-1">August 09, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>CVE-2023-0464, CVE-2023-0465, CVE-2023-0466, and CVE-2023-2650 have been patched in Filestore CSI driver in GKE versions 1.23 and 1.24, for newly created clusters.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The Filestore CSI driver now supports smaller share sizes (10Gi) for Filestore multishares for GKE for enterprise instances starting in version 1.27.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="August_04_2023" data-text="August 04, 2023" tabindex="-1">August 04, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>GKE Autopilot supports the creation of certificate signing request (CSR) objects on new clusters with version 1.27 or later, as long as those CSRs do not conflict with system components identities, and Google-managed IAM service accounts. This feature will be enabled for existing 1.27 clusters within the next few weeks.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_02_2023" data-text="August 02, 2023" tabindex="-1">August 02, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now run workloads on A100 80GB GPUs in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-gpus">Autopilot clusters</a> that use GKE version 1.27 and later.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="July_25_2023" data-text="July 25, 2023" tabindex="-1">July 25, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="http://cloud/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/managing-logs#control-plane-logs">Kubernetes control plane logs</a> and <a href="http://cloud/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/managing-metrics#control-plane-metrics">Kubernetes control plane metrics</a> are now available for GKE Autopilot clusters with control plane version 1.22.0 and later and 1.22.13 and later, respectively. You can now configure Autopilot cluster to export logs and certain metrics emitted by the Kubernetes API server, scheduler, and controller manager to Cloud Logging and Cloud Monitoring.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_24_2023" data-text="July 24, 2023" tabindex="-1">July 24, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>In new Autopilot clusters running GKE version 1.27 and later, GKE assigns IP addresses for GKE Services from a Google-managed range: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">34.118.224.0/20</code> by default. With this feature, you don&#39;t need to specify your own IP address range for Services. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/alias-ips#cluster_sizing_secondary_range_svcs">Subnet secondary IP address range for Services</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Autopilot supports extended duration Pods from 1.27 or later with the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=false</code> annotation. To learn more,  see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/extended-duration-pods">how to extend the run time of Autopilot Pods</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_21_2023" data-text="July 21, 2023" tabindex="-1">July 21, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p><strong>Update to the Issue release note published on July 19, 2023</strong></p>

<p>We investigated this issue and are rolling back the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--no-enable-insecure-kubelet-readonly-port</code> flag in the gcloud CLI. New or existing clusters where the port is still enabled aren&#39;t affected. If you already disabled the port, your cluster will continue to work, but you may notice inconsistency in whether the port is fully disabled on every node of the cluster. We&#39;ll publish a release note if we have new updates related to the kubelet read-only port.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_20_2023" data-text="July 20, 2023" tabindex="-1">July 20, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.25 and later, there is a bug fix in the Ingress Controller to unset the Cloud Armor Ingress Security Policy when removed from the BackendConfig.</p>

<p>Users who have manually attached the Security Policy to a backend service should no longer use this method and should use the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ingress-configuration#cloud_armor">BackendConfig to continue using Cloud Armor Security Policies</a> prior to cluster upgrades to GKE version 1.25 and later.</p>

<p>With this fix, the Ingress Controller will reconcile using the configuration in the BackendConfig, thus unsetting any Security Policies added manually to a backend service.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_19_2023" data-text="July 19, 2023" tabindex="-1">July 19, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>There&#39;s a known issue causing the gcloud CLI to crash when you run the command to disable the insecure kubelet read-only port, as described in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/disable-kubelet-readonly-port">Stop using the insecure kubelet read-only port in GKE clusters</a>. We&#39;re investigating this issue and will publish an update when it&#39;s fixed.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Starting in GKE version 1.27 and gke-metrics-agent version 2.0.0, the memory request and limit of <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gke-metrics-agent</code> will increase by an extra 60MiB. This change makes the system metrics collection more stable and reliable.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_14_2023" data-text="July 14, 2023" tabindex="-1">July 14, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>New Autopilot clusters created with version <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.27.3-gke.100</code> or later are now provisioned with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-small</code> default nodes, which are removed immediately after cluster creation. With this change, DaemonSets are guaranteed to schedule on all candidate nodes, as long as you follow <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/deploying-workloads-overview#autopilot-ds-best-practices">best practices for DaemonSets on Autopilot</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_13_2023" data-text="July 13, 2023" tabindex="-1">July 13, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The managed <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/cloud-storage-fuse-csi-driver">Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver</a> for GKE is now GA in versions 1.26.5 and later. You can use this driver to consume Cloud Storage buckets for GKE workloads.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_12_2023" data-text="July 12, 2023" tabindex="-1">July 12, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p><strong>Revision for the release note announced on June 26, 2023</strong></p>

<p>Starting August 2023, Cloud DNS will become the default DNS provider for new GKE Autopilot clusters created with version 1.25.9-gke.400 or later, or version 1.26.4-gke.500 or later (effectively replacing kube-dns). The rollout will be gradual and expected to be completed by August 11, 2023. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cloud-dns">Cloud DNS for GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Dataplane V2 observability is now available in Public Preview starting in GKE versions 1.26.4-gke.500 or later, or 1.27.1-gke.400 or later. You can now enable Dataplane V2 metrics and observability tools on your cluster. Dataplane V2 metrics are included in new Autopilot clusters and opt-in for new Standard clusters. You can opt-in to enable Dataplane V2 observability tools for Autopilot and Standard clusters. Existing clusters can also be updated to enable metrics and observability tooling.</p>

<p>For more information, check out <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-dpv2-observability">GKE Dataplane V2 observability</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.24 and later, new beta APIs are, by default, disabled in new clusters. Starting in version 1.27, which is the first new minor version since 1.24 where new beta APIs are introduced, you can enable new APIs on cluster creation or for an existing cluster. </p>

<p>For more information, see how to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/use-beta-apis">Use Kubernetes beta APIs with GKE clusters</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_11_2023" data-text="July 11, 2023" tabindex="-1">July 11, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now troubleshoot common GKE issues by using the new &quot;interactive playbook&quot; dashboards in Cloud Monitoring: <a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/monitoring/dashboards/gke-troubleshooting/unschedulable">unschedulable pods</a> and <a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/monitoring/dashboards/gke-troubleshooting/crashloop">crashlooping containers</a>.  You can also access the interactive playbooks from GKE UI insights and set alerts that will allow you to know once those issues occurs.</p>

<p>For information about using these dashboards, see the GKE troubleshooting documentation for <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/troubleshooting#PodUnschedulable">unschedulable pods</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/troubleshooting#CrashLoopBackOff">crashlooping</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Starting in GKE version 1.27, cluster autoscaler always considers Compute Engine Reservations when making the scale-up decisions. The node pools with matching unused reservations are prioritized when choosing the node pool to scale up, even when the node pool is not the most efficient one. Additionally, unused reservations are always prioritized when balancing multi-zonal scale-ups. </p>

<p>For more information, see how to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-autoscaler">use cluster autoscaler</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_10_2023" data-text="July 10, 2023" tabindex="-1">July 10, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The new release of the GKE Gateway controller (2023-R2) is now generally available. With this release, the GKE Gateway controller will provide the following new capabilities:</p>

<ul>
<li>New GatewayClasses supporting the regional external Application Load Balancer</li>
<li>Identity-aware Proxy (IAP) Integration</li>
<li>Custom request and response headers</li>
<li>URL Rewrites and Path Redirects</li>
</ul>

<p>To learn more, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gatewayclass-capabilities">supported capabilities per GatewayClass</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_07_2023" data-text="July 07, 2023" tabindex="-1">July 07, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2023-r15_version_updates" data-text="(2023-R15) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2023-R15) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">

<h2 id="June_28_2023" data-text="June 28, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 28, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>FQDN Network Policy, currently in Public Preview, can now be enabled on GKE Autopilot clusters, by updating your clusters. To lean more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/fqdn-network-policies">Control Pod egress traffic using FQDN network policies</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_27_2023" data-text="June 27, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 27, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A new vulnerability (CVE-2023-2235) has been discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on the node. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-018">GCP-2023-018 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>With CVE-2023-31436, an out-of-bounds memory access flaw was found in the Linux kernel&#39;s traffic control (QoS) subsystem in how a user triggers the qfq_change_class function with an incorrect MTU value of the network device used as lmax. This flaw allows a local user to crash or potentially escalate their privileges on the system.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-017">GCP-2023-017 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_26_2023" data-text="June 26, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 26, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Starting June 26, 2023, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/dns">Cloud DNS</a> becomes the default DNS provider for new GKE Autopilot clusters created with version 1.25.9-gke.400 or later or version 1.26.4-gke.500 or later, effectively replacing kube-dns. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cloud-dns">Cloud DNS for GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Managed Service for Prometheus is enabled by default in new GKE Standard clusters running version 1.27 and later. Existing clusters that upgrade to 1.27 will not automatically enable this feature. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/managed-prometheus/setup-managed#enable-mgdcoll-gke">Enable managed collection: GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_23_2023" data-text="June 23, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 23, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Automatic GPU driver installation is available in version 1.27.2-gke.1200 and later, which enables you to install NVIDIA GPU drivers on nodes without manually applying a DaemonSet.</p>

<p>For instructions, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gpus#create">Running GPUs</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_22_2023" data-text="June 22, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 22, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Autopilot now supports the ability to deploy your own service mesh. Many service meshes, such as Istio or LinkerD, require CAP_NET_ADMIN Linux capability to function, which is disabled on Autopilot clusters by default to reduce the size of the security attack surface. You can now optionally enable NET_ADMIN on your Autopilot clusters if you need this capability for your service meshes or other opt-in use cases. See <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/autopilot-security#linux_workload_limitations">Autopilot Security</a> for more information for how to enable NET_ADMIN.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_21_2023" data-text="June 21, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 21, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A new vulnerability, CVE-2023-0468, has been discovered in the Linux kernel that could allow an unprivileged user to escalate privileges to root when io_poll_get_ownership will keep increasing req-&gt;poll_refs on every io_poll_wake then overflow to 0 which will fput req-&gt;file twice and cause a struct file refcount issue. GKE clusters, including Autopilot clusters, with Container-Optimized OS using Linux Kernel version 5.15 are affected. GKE clusters using Ubuntu images or using GKE Sandbox are unaffected.</p>

<p>For instructions and more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-015-gke">GKE security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE support for <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/hyperdisk">Hyperdisk Throughput and Hyperdisk Extreme</a> as an attached persistent disk option is now generally available. Support is available for both Autopilot and Standard clusters running GKE versions 1.26 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_16_2023" data-text="June 16, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 16, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>Two new security issues were discovered in Kubernetes where users may be able to launch containers that bypass policy restrictions when using ephemeral containers and either ImagePolicyWebhook (CVE-2023-2727) or the ServiceAccount admission plugin (CVE-2023-2728).</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-014">GCP-2023-014 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_15_2023" data-text="June 15, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 15, 2023</h2>
