<h2 id="June_14_2023" data-text="June 14, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 14, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Clusters with low or no utilization can be identified by <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/idle-clusters">Idle Cluster insights</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_12_2023" data-text="June 12, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 12, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/viewing-deprecation-insights-and-recommendations">deprecation insights</a> to identify clusters on versions 1.21 to 1.24 that use Pod Security Policy, which is unsupported on GKE version 1.25 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Dual-stack LoadBalancer Services are now available in Preview. Dual-stack LoadBalancer Services are supported on both GKE Standard and Autopilot dual-stack clusters. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/service#single-stack_and_dual-stack_services">Single-stack and dual-stack Services</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_09_2023" data-text="June 09, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 09, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>New Autopilot clusters that run GKE version 1.25.5-gke.1000 and later automatically use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/image-streaming">Image streaming</a> to pull eligible images.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In addition to the existing egress network policy GKE already supports, you can now control the egress traffic of your Pods by using a network policy that matches a fully-qualified domain name or a regular expression. FQDN Network Policy is now available in Preview for clusters in version 1.26.4-gke.500 and later, and 1.27.1-gke.400 and later. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/fqdn-network-policies">Control Pod egress traffic using FQDN network policies</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_08_2023" data-text="June 08, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 08, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The PD CSI Driver will be automatically enabled on upgrades to 1.25, for clusters with the add-on disabled. There are no cost implications for enabling the driver, and it requests only a small amount of node resources. This upgrade enables <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gce-pd</code> volumes to continue working on Kubernetes clusters version 1.25 and later. You can still disable the driver manually after upgrade. For more details, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/small-cluster-tuning#configuring_add-ons">Configuring add-ons</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_07_2023" data-text="June 07, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 07, 2023</h2>

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

<h2 id="June_06_2023" data-text="June 06, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 06, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A new vulnerability (CVE-2023-1872) has been discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation to root on the node.
  For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-008">GCP-2023-008</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A new vulnerability (CVE-2023-2878) has been discovered in the secrets-store-csi-driver where an actor with access to the driver logs could observe service account tokens. These tokens could then potentially be exchanged with external cloud providers to access secrets stored in cloud vault solutions. On GKE, the severity is None. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-009">GCP-2023-009 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_05_2023" data-text="June 05, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 05, 2023</h2>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for

information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="June_01_2023" data-text="June 01, 2023" tabindex="-1">June 01, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Agones on GKE users will get <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/isolate-agones-controller-gke">recommendations and insights</a> if they did not install the Agones controller on dedicated nodes.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_26_2023" data-text="May 26, 2023" tabindex="-1">May 26, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <strong>Observability</strong> tab for each of your GKE clusters now includes metrics for ephemeral storage. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/view-observability-metrics#metrics_for_clusters_and_workloads">View observability metrics</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_25_2023" data-text="May 25, 2023" tabindex="-1">May 25, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>For VPC peering-based private clusters running version 1.27 or later, traffic from kube-apiserver to nodes routes through <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/control-plane-node-communication/#konnectivity-service" class="external">the Konnectivity service</a>. If your cluster was created before 2020-09-17, this traffic from does not route through Konnectivity unless you have <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ip-rotation">rotated the control plane IP address</a> after 2020-09-17.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>CVE-2022-4450, CVE-2022-2097, CVE-2023-0286, CVE-2023-0215, and CVE-2022-4304 have been patched in all minor versions for all existing and new clusters using the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/gce-pd-csi-driver">Compute Engine persistent disk CSI driver</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_23_2023" data-text="May 23, 2023" tabindex="-1">May 23, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>CVE-2023-26604 has been fixed in clusters running version 1.25 using the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/filestore-csi-driver">Filestore CSI driver</a>. The fix is transparent, but to mitigate instability, it is available by <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/upgrading-a-cluster">manually upgrading the cluster</a> to the newest 1.25 patch version. The CVE is not present in clusters running version 1.26 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_22_2023" data-text="May 22, 2023" tabindex="-1">May 22, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The C3 machine family is generally available for GKE Standard clusters running on version 1.22 and later. You can select this family by using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--machine-type</code> flag when creating a cluster or node pool. </p>

<p>The following features are not supported for this machine family: </p>

<ul>
<li>Node auto-provisioning.</li>
<li>Confidential GKE nodes.</li>
<li>Local SSD.</li>
<li>Standard persistent disks (pd-standard).</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, refer to the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/general-purpose-machines#c3_machine_types">C3 machine series</a> documentation.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_18_2023" data-text="May 18, 2023" tabindex="-1">May 18, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>Two new vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-1281, CVE-2023-1829) have been discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation to root on the node. GKE Standard clusters are affected. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-005">GCP-2023-005 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_16_2023" data-text="May 16, 2023" tabindex="-1">May 16, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="127_is_now_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="1.27 is now available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">1.27 is now available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.27 is now available in the Rapid channel. For more information about the content of Kubernetes 1.27, read the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.27.md#urgent-upgrade-notes" class="external">Kubernetes 1.27 Release Notes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="removed_api_versions" data-text="Removed API versions" tabindex="-1">Removed API versions</h4>

<p>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-27" class="external">removed in 1.27</a> in favor of newer versions:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>storage.k8s.io/v1beta1 CSIStorageCapacity</p>

<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.24</li>
<li>use storage.k8s.io/v1 instead, available since 1.24</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_api_versions" data-text="Deprecated API versions" tabindex="-1">Deprecated API versions</h4>

<p>These APIs are still served in version 1.27 but are in a deprecation period:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-29" class="external">removed in 1.29</a> in favor of newer versions:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2 FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration</p>

<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.26</li>
<li>use flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3 instead, available since 1.26</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_12_2023" data-text="May 12, 2023" tabindex="-1">May 12, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The g2-standard machine family with NVIDIA L4 is generally available for node pools in clusters running GKE version 1.22 and later. To select the machine family, use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--machine-type</code> flag in your create command.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_09_2023" data-text="May 09, 2023" tabindex="-1">May 09, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Now in GA for both GKE Standard and Autopilot clusters with GKE version 1.26 and later, you can add more IPv4 secondary Pod ranges to a new or existing cluster with the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--additional-pod-ipv4-ranges</code> flag. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/multi-pod-cidr">Adding Pod IP addresses</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_03_2023" data-text="May 03, 2023" tabindex="-1">May 03, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.26, for VPC peering-based private clusters that were created after 2020-08, <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/control-plane-node-communication/#konnectivity-service" class="external">the Konnectivity service</a> will be initialized but not used. Traffic from kube-apiserver to nodes continues to route directly.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_02_2023" data-text="May 02, 2023" tabindex="-1">May 02, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>We&#39;re working on automatically enabling the PD CSI Driver on upgrades to 1.25, for clusters with the add-on disabled. There are no cost implications for enabling the driver, and it requests only a small amount of node resources. This upgrade enables <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gce-pd</code> volumes to continue working on Kubernetes clusters version 1.25 and greater. You can still disable the driver manually after upgrade. For more details, please read <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/small-cluster-tuning#configuring_add-ons">here</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The managed <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/cloud-storage-fuse-csi-driver">Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver</a>  for GKE is now available in Preview in GKE versions 1.26.3 and later.  You can use this driver to consume Cloud Storage buckets for GKE workloads.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_19_2023" data-text="April 19, 2023" tabindex="-1">April 19, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2023-r09_version_updates" data-text="(2023-R09) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2023-R09) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="April_11_2023" data-text="April 11, 2023" tabindex="-1">April 11, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>Two new vulnerabilities, CVE-2023-0240 and CVE-2023-23586, have been discovered in the Linux kernel that could allow an unprivileged user to escalate privileges. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-003">GCP-2023-003 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>In GKE 1.27 and later, GKE nodes will not keep compressed image layers in containerd&#39;s content store once they have been unpacked, by setting <code translate="no" dir="ltr">discard_unpacked_layers=true</code> in containerd configuration. This change will not impact workloads running as Kubernetes Pods and Containers. However, if your workload relies on the image layers in containerd&#39;s content store, please make sure your workload can handle the case where image layers are missing.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="March_30_2023" data-text="March 30, 2023" tabindex="-1">March 30, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">me-central1</code></a> region in Doha, Qatar is now available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_29_2023" data-text="March 29, 2023" tabindex="-1">March 29, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Starting from GKE 1.26, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-autoscaler">cluster autoscaler</a> can drain Pods from multiple nodes in parallel. The removal criteria are not changing, so the end state after scale down is going to be the same, but it will be achieved faster.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_23_2023" data-text="March 23, 2023" tabindex="-1">March 23, 2023</h2>

<h2 id="March_21_2023" data-text="March 21, 2023" tabindex="-1">March 21, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><p>Starting on March 21, 2023, traffic to k8s.gcr.io will be redirected to registry.k8s.io, following the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2023/03/10/image-registry-redirect/">community announcement</a>. This change will happen gradually to reduce disruption, and should be transparent to the majority of GKE clusters.</p>

<p>To check for edge cases, and mitigate a potential impact, follow the step-by-step guidance in <a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2023/03/10/image-registry-redirect/#how-can-i-check-if-i-am-impacted">k8s.gcr.io Redirect to registry.k8s.io - What You Need to Know</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_07_2023" data-text="March 07, 2023" tabindex="-1">March 07, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Backend Service-based external Network load balancers are now generally available with GKE. Regional Backend Service is a foundational element of a Google Cloud Load Balancer and using it for your external LoadBalancer Services will unlock new capabilities going forward. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/external-svc-lb-rbs">how to deploy a backend service-based external network load balancer</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="March_01_2023" data-text="March 01, 2023" tabindex="-1">March 01, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A new vulnerability (CVE-2022-4696) has been discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to a privilege escalation on the node. GKE clusters, including Autopilot clusters, are impacted. GKE clusters using GKE Sandbox are not affected. For instructions and more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2023-001-gke">GKE security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="February_17_2023" data-text="February 17, 2023" tabindex="-1">February 17, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In Standard clusters with GKE version 1.26 and later, you can now audit workloads to validate if they are compatible with Autopilot clusters. Use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl get audit</code> to see the cluster objects.</p></div>

<h2 id="February_07_2023" data-text="February 07, 2023" tabindex="-1">February 07, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><p>For clusters running on GKE version
1.21—which reaches <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-schedule#schedule-for-release-channels">end of life on January 31, 2023</a>—you
can apply a one-time <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/maintenance-windows-and-exclusions#exclusions">maintenance exclusion</a> to prevent the cluster from being upgraded until April 30, 2023.
For more information, see the note at
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations#auto-upgrades-resume">When does GKE resume automatic upgrades?</a></p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_03_2023" data-text="February 03, 2023" tabindex="-1">February 03, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#January_27_2023"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">POD_FINDER_IP_MISMATCH</code></a> errors that caused Pods to fail to access Google Cloud APIs are fixed in the following GKE versions in the Rapid release channel:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.22.17-gke.3100 or later</li>
<li>1.23.16-gke.200 or later</li>
<li>1.24.9-gke.3200 or later</li>
<li>1.25.6-gke.200 or later</li>
<li>1.26.1-gke.400 or later</li>
</ul>

<p>To fix the issue, upgrade your nodes to any of these versions.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="January_27_2023" data-text="January 27, 2023" tabindex="-1">January 27, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>If containerd restarts on a node that has existing running Pods that use Workload Identity, those specific Pods might fail to access Google Cloud APIs and might return POD_FINDER_IP_MISMATCH errors. This affects nodes with the following GKE versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.22.16-gke.2100 and later</li>
<li>1.23.14-gke.1900 and later</li>
<li>1.24.7-gke.700 and later </li>
<li>1.25.0 and later</li>
<li>1.26.0 and later</li>
</ul>

<p>This issue will be fixed in a future release</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>A known issue with kube-dns receiving a DNS response from an upstream DNS resolver with a large TTL has been fixed. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/kube-dns#large-ttl">Large TTL from DNS upstream servers</a></p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Starting from GKE control plane versions 1.26.0-gke.2200, 1.25.5-gke.2200, 1.24.9-gke.2200 or later, SingleStack IPv6 and DualStack (IPv4/IPv6) services, stub domains, and upstream nameservers are supported with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cloud-dns">Cloud DNS for GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Public zonal clusters upgraded to GKE versions 1.24 and later will eventually be migrated to use Private Service Connect (PSC) for private control plane communication. There is no price increase for using GKE public clusters running on PSC.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_26_2023" data-text="January 26, 2023" tabindex="-1">January 26, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now specify a minimum CPU platform in the Balanced compute class in Autopilot clusters running GKE version 1.25 and later if your workloads have specialized CPU requirements such as a high base frequency or optimized power management functionality. For instructions, refer to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/min-cpu-platform">Choose a minimum CPU platform</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The Balanced <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/autopilot-compute-classes">compute class</a> is now generally available in Autopilot clusters running GKE version 1.25 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_24_2023" data-text="January 24, 2023" tabindex="-1">January 24, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now expose <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-hostport">randomly assigned host ports</a> in Pods on GKE Autopilot running version 1.24.7-gke.1200 and later or 1.25.3-gke.1100 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_17_2023" data-text="January 17, 2023" tabindex="-1">January 17, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now attach <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/local-ssd">ephemeral and block devices backed by Local NVMe</a> SSDs during GKE node pool creation, using the Ephemeral Storage Local SSD API and the Local NVMe SSD Block API respectively, with node version 1.25.3-gke.1800 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_13_2023" data-text="January 13, 2023" tabindex="-1">January 13, 2023</h2>

<h2 id="January_12_2023" data-text="January 12, 2023" tabindex="-1">January 12, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>Two new vulnerabilities (CVE-2022-3786 and CVE-2022-3602) have been discovered in OpenSSL v3.0.6 that can potentially cause a crash. While this has been rated a High in the NVD database, GKE endpoints use boringSSL or an older version of OpenSSL that is not affected, so the rating has been reduced to a Medium for GKE. For more information, refer to the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-026">GCP-2022-026 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_09_2023" data-text="January 09, 2023" tabindex="-1">January 09, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The release notes for <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#126_is_now_available_in_the_rapid_channel">1.26 available in the Rapid channel</a> were modified with an additional notable change:</p>

<ul>
<li>New node pools created on 1.26 will default to use the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/cgroups/" class="external">cgroupv2 resource management subsystem</a> enabling the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2022/08/31/cgroupv2-ga-1-25/" class="external">latest container resource management capabilities</a>. <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-system-config#cgroup-mode-options">Node System Configuration</a> can be used to switch between cgroup settings.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Windows Server 2022 OS image is generally available on GKE. You can now create
Windows Node pools with Windows Server 2022 OS images using the command line.
For more information, see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/creating-a-cluster-windows#create_a_cluster_and_node_pools">Creating a cluster using Windows Server node pools</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_05_2023" data-text="January 05, 2023" tabindex="-1">January 05, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p><em>2023-01-09 update</em>: Added an additional Notable change to 1.26 for this release note.</p></div>
    </div>

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="removed_api_versions" data-text="Removed API versions" tabindex="-1">Removed API versions</h4>

<p>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-26" class="external">removed in 1.26</a> in favor of newer versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta1 FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration
<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.23</li>
<li>use flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2 instead, available since 1.23</li>
</ul></li>
<li>autoscaling/v2beta2 HorizontalPodAutoscaler
<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.23</li>
<li>use autoscaling/v2 instead, available since 1.23 (or autoscaling/v1)</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="new_api_versions" data-text="New API versions" tabindex="-1">New API versions</h4>

<ul>
<li>flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3 FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration
<ul>
<li>The PriorityLevelConfiguration <code translate="no" dir="ltr">spec.limited.assuredConcurrencyShares</code> field is renamed to
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">spec.limited.nominalConcurrencyShares</code></li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_api_versions" data-text="Deprecated API versions" tabindex="-1">Deprecated API versions</h4>

<p>These APIs are still served in version 1.26 but are in a deprecation period:</p>

<ul>
<li>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be removed in 1.27 in favor of newer versions:
<ul>
<li>storage.k8s.io/v1beta1 CSIStorageCapacity</li>
<li>deprecated since 1.24</li>
<li>use storage.k8s.io/v1 instead, available since 1.24</li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be removed in 1.29 in favor of newer versions:
<ul>
<li>flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2 FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration</li>
<li>deprecated since 1.26</li>
<li>use flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3 instead, available since 1.26</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="126_is_now_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="1.26 is now available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">1.26 is now available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.26 is now available in the Rapid channel. Before upgrading, read the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.26.md#urgent-upgrade-notes" class="external">Kubernetes 1.26 Release Notes</a>, especially the action required and deprecation sections.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="notable_changes" data-text="Notable changes" tabindex="-1">Notable changes</h4>

<ul>
<li>kubectl 1.26 removes compiled-in support for Azure and Google Cloud authentication methods.
<ul>
<li>The removal doesn&#39;t affect operators that are deployed in the cluster and use Kubernetes service accounts to communicate with the API server, Kubernetes service account authentication continues to work as-is.</li>
<li>GKE has released an updated authentication plugin, gke-gcloud-auth-plugin. This plugin uses the client-go Credential Plugins framework to provide authentication tokens to communicate with GKE clusters.</li>
<li>For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/auth-plugin">Deprecated authentication plugin for Kubernetes clients</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cluster-access-for-kubectl#install_plugin">Install required plugins</a>.</li>
<li>New node pools created on 1.26 will default to use the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/cgroups/" class="external">cgroupv2 resource management subsystem</a> enabling the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2022/08/31/cgroupv2-ga-1-25/" class="external">latest container resource management capabilities</a>. <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-system-config#cgroup-mode-options">Node System Configuration</a> can be used to switch between cgroup settings.</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_04_2023" data-text="January 04, 2023" tabindex="-1">January 04, 2023</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now run GPU-based workloads in GA in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-gpus">Autopilot clusters</a> that use GKE version 1.24.2-gke.1800 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_22_2022" data-text="December 22, 2022" tabindex="-1">December 22, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Dual-stack clusters in GKE are now generally available. Dual-stack networking is supported on both Standard and Autopilot clusters. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/alias-ips#dual-stack">Use an IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack network to create a dual-stack cluster</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_21_2022" data-text="December 21, 2022" tabindex="-1">December 21, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A new vulnerability (CVE-2022-2602) has been discovered in the io_uring subsystem in the Linux kernel that can allow an attacker to potentially execute arbitrary code.
  For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-025">GCP-2022-025 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now enable NCCL Fast Socket on your multi-GPU workloads.   NCCL Fast Socket is a transport layer plugin designed to improve  NVIDIA Collective Communication Library (NCCL) performance on Google Cloud.  To enable NCCL Fast Socket, you must be using a GKE Standard cluster with control plane version 1.25.2-gke.1700 or later. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/nccl-fast-socket">Improve workload efficiency using NCCL Fast Socket</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_19_2022" data-text="December 19, 2022" tabindex="-1">December 19, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>CVE-2022-37434, CVE-2022-40674, CVE-2022-1586, CVE-2022-1587 have been patched in the PD CSI driver in 1.22, 1.23, 1.24 for newly created clusters. CVE-2022-37434, CVE-2021-3999, CVE-2022-40674, CVE-2022-1586, CVE-2022-1587 have been patched in the PD CSI driver in 1.25 for newly created clusters.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_16_2022" data-text="December 16, 2022" tabindex="-1">December 16, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/https">Global external HTTP(S) load balancer</a> is now supported with the GKE Gateway controller in Preview. You can now configure GKE clusters with control plane version 1.24 or later in Rapid channel to use a global external HTTP(S) load balancer to expose web services to the Internet, in a single cluster or multi-cluster architecture. You can benefit from many advanced traffic management capabilities offered by the new generation of Google Cloud global external HTTP(S) load balancers natively in GKE by <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/deploying-gateways">using the Kubernetes Gateway API and specifying a new Gateway class</a>. To see the difference between Gateway classes compatible with our GKE Gateway controller, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gatewayclass-capabilities">here</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_14_2022" data-text="December 14, 2022" tabindex="-1">December 14, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for

information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v1254" class="external">1.25.4-gke.1600</a> is now the default version in the Rapid channel</li>
<li>The following versions are now available in the Rapid channel: 
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v12216" class="external">1.22.16-gke.2000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.23.md#v12314" class="external">1.23.14-gke.1800</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v1248" class="external">1.24.8-gke.2000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v1254" class="external">1.25.4-gke.2100</a> </li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following versions are no longer available in the Rapid channel:
<ul>
<li>1.22.15-gke.100</li>
<li>1.23.12-gke.1600</li>
<li>1.24.5-gke.600</li>
<li>1.25.3-gke.800</li>
</ul></li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.21 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v12215" class="external">1.22.15-gke.1000</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.22 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.23.md#v12313" class="external">1.23.13-gke.900</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.23 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.23.md#v12313" class="external">1.23.13-gke.900</a> with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.25 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v1254" class="external">1.25.4-gke.1600</a> with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cloud-dns">Cloud DNS for GKE</a> (cluster scope) is now Generally Available. You can now configure GKE clusters with control plane version 1.24.7-gke.800, 1.25.3-gke.700 or later to use Cloud DNS as the DNS provider for in-cluster name resolution, and replace the existing DNS service based on kube-dns.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><em>10/06/2023 update</em>: This migration is currently paused.</p>

<p>GKE Autopilot clusters may now migrate the cluster&#39;s datapath provider to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/dataplane-v2">Dataplane V2</a>. Migration is triggered during a control plane upgrade (see version requirements below). The migration is complete once all nodes running the legacy datapath have been recreated. Node pools created after the control plane upgrade will be created using Dataplane V2.</p>

<ul>
<li><p>For clusters running 1.24 without Dataplane V2, upgrading to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.24.7-gke.300</code> or a higher 1.24 version will begin the migration to Dataplane V2.</p></li>
<li><p>For clusters running 1.25 without Dataplane V2, upgrading to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.25.3-gke.200</code> or a higher 1.25 version will begin the migration to Dataplane V2.</p></li>
</ul>

<p>To determine whether you are in the process of migrating the datapath, run:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Bash"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>container<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>clusters<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>describe<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>&lt;CLUSTER&gt;<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>--region<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>&lt;REGION&gt;<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>--project<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>&lt;PROJECT&gt;<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>--format<span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"value(networkConfig.datapathProvider)"</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
<p>Clusters migrating to Dataplane V2 will have the datapath provider field of the cluster set to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">MIGRATE_TO_ADVANCED_DATAPATH</code>.</p>

<p>Clusters that have migrated to Dataplane V2 will have the datapath provider field of the cluster set to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ADVANCED_DATAPATH</code>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_13_2022" data-text="December 13, 2022" tabindex="-1">December 13, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/compact-placement">Compact placement policy</a> is now generally available. Set up a compact placement policy to specify that nodes within the node pool should be placed in closer physical proximity to each other within a zone. Having nodes closer to each other can reduce network latency between nodes, which can be useful for tightly-coupled batch workloads.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_12_2022" data-text="December 12, 2022" tabindex="-1">December 12, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Public clusters upgraded to GKE versions 1.25 and later will eventually be migrated to use Private Service Connect (PSC) for private control plane communication. There is no price increase for using GKE public clusters running on PSC.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_05_2022" data-text="December 05, 2022" tabindex="-1">December 05, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

<h2 id="November_29_2022" data-text="November 29, 2022" tabindex="-1">November 29, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/managing-logs#control-plane-logs">Kubernetes control plane logs</a> are now Generally Available. You can now configure GKE clusters with control plane version 1.22.0 or later to export to Cloud Logging logs emitted by the Kubernetes API server, Scheduler, and Controller Manager.</p>

<p>These logs are stored in Cloud Logging and can be queried in the Cloud Logging Log Explorer or Cloud Logging API. These logs can also be sent to Google Cloud Storage, BigQuery, or Pub/Sub using the Log Router.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/viewing-deprecation-insights-and-recommendations">deprecation insights</a> to identify clusters on versions 1.23 and earlier that <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/docker-containerd">use Docker-based node images</a>, which are unsupported on GKE version 1.24 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_22_2022" data-text="November 22, 2022" tabindex="-1">November 22, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>GKE version 1.21.14-gke.9500 has an issue where Pods in certain conditions might get stuck terminating indefinitely, due to a Linux kernel bug. The version has been removed and is no longer available for new clusters. If your node pools are running 1.21.14-gke.9500 and experience the issue, we recommend <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/upgrading-a-cluster#upgrade_nodes">downgrading the node pool</a> to 1.21.14-gke.8500.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_21_2022" data-text="November 21, 2022" tabindex="-1">November 21, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <strong>Logs</strong> tab available for each cluster on the <strong>Kubernetes Engine &gt; Clusters</strong> page now includes suggested queries for your logs. For more information about using your GKE logs, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/using-logs#accessing_your_logs">Viewing your GKE logs</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_18_2022" data-text="November 18, 2022" tabindex="-1">November 18, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Autopilot clusters support <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/compact-placement">compact placement policies</a> in version 1.25 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_17_2022" data-text="November 17, 2022" tabindex="-1">November 17, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Autopilot clusters support <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/troubleshooting/troubleshooting-autopilot-clusters#unreliable-workloads-specific-node">signaling to GKE that a particular node is problematic</a> in version 1.24 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_11_2022" data-text="November 11, 2022" tabindex="-1">November 11, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/filestore-csi-driver">The Filestore CSI driver</a> has patched the following CVEs for newly created clusters running GKE version 1.23 and later:</p>

<ul>
<li>CVE-2022-37434</li>
<li>CVE-2019-19126</li>
<li>CVE-2019-25013</li>
<li>CVE-2022-23219</li>
<li>CVE-2021-35942</li>
<li>CVE-2020-10029</li>
<li>CVE-2021-3326</li>
<li>CVE-2022-23218</li>
<li>CVE-2020-1752</li>
<li>CVE-2021-3999</li>
<li>CVE-2020-27618</li>
<li>CVE-2021-27645</li>
<li>CVE-2016-10228</li>
<li>CVE-2020-6096</li>
<li>CVE-2021-33574</li>
<li>CVE-2022-29458</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_10_2022" data-text="November 10, 2022" tabindex="-1">November 10, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now use use compact placement for node auto-provisioning in Standard clusters with GKE version 1.25 and later. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/compact-placement#compact-placement-node-autoprovision">Use compact placement for node auto-provisioning</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_09_2022" data-text="November 09, 2022" tabindex="-1">November 09, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Gateway for Single Cluster is now generally available in GKE version 1.24 and later. Use the Gateway API to express the intent of your inbound HTTP(S) traffic into your GKE cluster and the Gateway controller will instrument and fully manage the external and/or internal HTTP(S) load balancer(s) that forwards traffic to your applications. For complete details about the GKE Gateway controller, refer to the following <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/gateway-api">documentation</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_08_2022" data-text="November 08, 2022" tabindex="-1">November 08, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A security vulnerability, CVE-2022-39278, has been discovered in Istio, which is used in Anthos Service Mesh, that allows a malicious attacker to crash the control plane. GKE doesn&#39;t ship with Istio and isn&#39;t affected by this vulnerability. However, if you separately installed Anthos Service Mesh or Istio in your GKE cluster, refer to the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/service-mesh/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-020">Anthos Service Mesh security bulletin</a> for more information.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_07_2022" data-text="November 07, 2022" tabindex="-1">November 07, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>When you create a LoadBalancer service in GKE, the Google Cloud controllers automatically create the following <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/firewall-rules">firewall rules</a> and apply them to the GKE nodes to allow inbound connections on the Service port:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Internal load balancer with GKE subsetting or external load balancer with regional backend services (RBS)</strong>: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s2-[cluster-id]-[namespace]-[service-name]-[suffixhash]</code></li>
<li><strong>Internal load balancer without GKE subsetting or external load balancer with target pool</strong>: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s-fw-[loadbalancer-hash]</code></li>
</ul>

<p>These rules now include the load balancer IP address in the destination ranges field to further control the inbound connections to the nodes. You can use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud compute firewall-rules describe</code> command to check a relevant firewall. The new field in the output is similar to the following:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Transact-SQL" syntax-guessed><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-nl">destinationRanges</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-o">-</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">LOADBALANCER_VIRTUAL_IP_ADDRESS</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">]</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="November_03_2022" data-text="November 03, 2022" tabindex="-1">November 03, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now easily identify clusters that use certificates <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/webhookcompatibility">incompatible</a> with Kubernetes version 1.23. Kubernetes 1.23 <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/viewing-deprecation-insights-and-recommendations">deprecation insights</a> are now available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products/#product-launch-stages">Preview</a> for clusters of at least version 1.22.6-gke.1000.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_28_2022" data-text="October 28, 2022" tabindex="-1">October 28, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A new vulnerability, CVE-2022-20409, has been discovered in the Linux kernel that could allow an unprivileged user to escalate to system execution privilege. For instructions and more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-022-gke">GKE security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_27_2022" data-text="October 27, 2022" tabindex="-1">October 27, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A new vulnerability, CVE-2022-3176, has been discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to local privilege escalation. This vulnerability allows an unprivileged user to achieve full container breakout to root on the node. For instructions and more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-021-gke">GKE security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<li>The following versions are no longer available in the Rapid channel:

<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v12114" class="external">1.21.14-gke.5300</a> 
with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel

<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v12213" class="external">1.22.13-gke.1000</a> 
with this release.</li>

</div></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_14_2022" data-text="October 14, 2022" tabindex="-1">October 14, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Cost Allocation has been released for general availability. With GKE Cost Allocation, you can see cost breakdowns in clusters for namespaces, and pod labels for utilized CPU and MEM. For complete details, refer to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cost-allocations">View detailed breakdown of cluster costs</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_12_2022" data-text="October 12, 2022" tabindex="-1">October 12, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Creating public clusters on GKE versions 1.23 or later might fail with the following error due to a missing API permission in certain compliance regimes (FedRAMP High, US Regions and Support, EU Regions and Support, EU Regions and Support with Sovereign Controls):</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded><code translate="no" dir="ltr">ManagedResourceService.AddServiceBundle, PERMISSION_DENIED&#39;/&gt; APPLICATION_ERROR;google.cloud.servicedirectory.v1beta1/ManagedResourceService.AddServiceBundle;Request is disallowed by organization&#39;s constraints/gcp.restrictServiceUsage constraint for &#39;projects/&lt;projectID&gt; attempting to use service &#39;servicedirectory.googleapis.com&#39;
</code></pre></devsite-code>
<p>To fix this issue, refer to the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/docs/release-notes#October_05_2022">October 5, 2022 Assured Workloads release note</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_05_2022" data-text="October 05, 2022" tabindex="-1">October 05, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2022-r24_version_updates" data-text="(2022-R24) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2022-R24) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="no-channel_147" data-text="No channel" tabindex="-1">No channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>The following control plane and node versions are now available: 
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v12114" class="external">1.21.14-gke.7100</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v12215" class="external">1.22.15-gke.100</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.23.md#v12312" class="external">1.23.12-gke.100</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v1245" class="external">1.24.5-gke.600</a> </li>
</ul></li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="stable-channel_147" data-text="Stable channel" tabindex="-1">Stable channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>The following versions are now available in the Stable channel: 
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v12114" class="external">1.21.14-gke.5300</a> </li>
</ul></li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="regular-channel_147" data-text="Regular channel" tabindex="-1">Regular channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li><p>The following versions are now available in the Regular channel: </p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v12114" class="external">1.21.14-gke.5300</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v12213" class="external">1.22.13-gke.1000</a> </li>
</ul></li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="rapid-channel_147" data-text="Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Rapid channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li><p>The following versions are now available in the Rapid channel: </p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v12114" class="external">1.21.14-gke.7100</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v12215" class="external">1.22.15-gke.100</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.23.md#v12312" class="external">1.23.12-gke.100</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v1245" class="external">1.24.5-gke.600</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#v1251" class="external">1.25.1-gke.500</a> </li>
</ul></li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_30_2022" data-text="September 30, 2022" tabindex="-1">September 30, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now run GPU-based workloads in Preview in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-gpus">Autopilot clusters</a> that use GKE version 1.24.2-gke.1800 and later. For more information, see the Google Cloud <a href="https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/containers-kubernetes/run-gpu-workloads-on-gke-autopilot">blog post</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In Autopilot clusters running GKE version 1.24.1-gke.1400 and later, you can now use the Balanced <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-compute-classes">compute class</a> to schedule your workloads that require very high memory or CPU requests.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_28_2022" data-text="September 28, 2022" tabindex="-1">September 28, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/managing-metrics#control-plane-reqs%22">GKE control plane metrics</a> is now available for clusters running Kubernetes control plane version 1.22.13 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The Calico CNI authentication errors that caused pods to get stuck in <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Terminating</code> or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Pending</code> state (see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#August_19_2022">August 19, 2022</a> release notes) are fixed in the following GKE versions in the Rapid release channel:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.24.4-gke.500 or later</li>
<li>1.23.11-gke.300 or later</li>
<li>1.22.14-gke.300 or later</li>
</ul>

<p>To fix the issue, upgrade your control plane to any of these versions. If you prefer not to use the Rapid channel, open a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/support-hub/">Google Cloud Support</a> ticket to have your cluster patched internally.</p></div>
    </div>

opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

</ul></li>

version 1.20 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v12114" class="external">1.21.14-gke.2700</a>

<li><p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded from

with this release.</p></li>

<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v12212" class="external">1.22.12-gke.2300</a> </li>
</ul></li>

<li><p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Stable channel will be upgraded from version 1.21 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v12212" class="external">1.22.12-gke.1200</a> with this release.</p></li>
<li><p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Stable channel will be upgraded from version 1.22 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v12212" class="external">1.22.12-gke.1200</a> with this release.</p></li>

<li><p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Regular channel will be upgraded from version 1.21 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v12212" class="external">1.22.12-gke.2300</a> with this release.</p></li>
<li><p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Regular channel will be upgraded from version 1.22 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v12212" class="external">1.22.12-gke.2300</a> with this release.</p></li>

<li><p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from version 1.24 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#v1243" class="external">1.24.3-gke.2100</a> with this release.</p></li>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p><em>2022-09-22</em> update: Updated new default versions for the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes-stable#September_13_2022">2022-R22</a> 
 release in the <em>Stable channel</em>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_22_2022" data-text="September 22, 2022" tabindex="-1">September 22, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">a2-ultragpu</code> machine family is available in Preview for node pools in clusters running GKE version 1.24 and later. To select the machine family, use the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/beta/container/node-pools/create#--machine-type"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">--machine-type</code></a> flag in your create command.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_15_2022" data-text="September 15, 2022" tabindex="-1">September 15, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>CVE-2022-2068 has been patched in the Filestore CSI driver for GKE clusters running version 1.23 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Starting from GKE version 1.25 and gke-metrics-agent version 1.0.0, we increase the memory request and limit of gke-metrics-agent to 100 MiB. This change makes the system metrics collection more stable and reliable.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_14_2022" data-text="September 14, 2022" tabindex="-1">September 14, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="125_is_now_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="1.25 is now available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">1.25 is now available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.25 is now available in the Rapid channel. Before upgrading, read the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.25.md#urgent-upgrade-notes" class="external">Kubernetes 1.25 Release Notes</a>, especially the action required and deprecation sections.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="notable_changes" data-text="Notable changes" tabindex="-1">Notable changes</h4>

<p>Support for the deprecated <code translate="no" dir="ltr">quobyte</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">storageOS</code> volume types is removed in 1.25.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="removed_api_versions" data-text="Removed API versions" tabindex="-1">Removed API versions</h4>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/04/06/podsecuritypolicy-deprecation-past-present-and-future/" class="external">PodSecurityPolicy</a> 
<ul>
<li>policy/v1beta1 PodSecurityPolicy</li>
<li>Deprecated in 1.21 and removed in 1.25.</li>
<li>1.24 is the last version supporting the beta PodSecurityPolicy feature. Use of this feature must be discontinued before clusters will upgrade to 1.25. See <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/podsecuritypolicy">PodSecurityPolicy deprecation</a> for more information.</li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs are <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/apis-1-25">removed in 1.25</a> in favor of their newer versions:
<ul>
<li>discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 EndpointSlice, deprecated since 1.21</li>
<li>policy/v1beta1 PodDisruptionBudget, deprecated since 1.21</li>
<li>batch/v1beta1 CronJob, deprecated since 1.21</li>
<li>node.k8s.io/v1beta1 RuntimeClass</li>
<li>autoscaling/v2beta1 HorizontalPodAutoscaler</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_api_versions" data-text="Deprecated API versions" tabindex="-1">Deprecated API versions</h4>

<p>These APIs are still served in version 1.25 but are in a deprecation period:</p>

<ul>
<li>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-26" class="external">removed in 1.26</a> in favor of newer versions:
<ul>
<li>flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta1 FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration
<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.23</li>
<li>use flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2 instead, available since 1.23</li>
</ul></li>
<li>autoscaling/v2beta2 HorizontalPodAutoscaler
<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.23</li>
<li>use autoscaling/v2 instead, available since 1.23 (or autoscaling/v1)</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-27" class="external">removed in 1.27</a> in favor of newer versions:
<ul>
<li>storage.k8s.io/v1beta1 CSIStorageCapacity, deprecated since 1.24</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">me-west1</code></a> region in Tel Aviv, Israel
is now available.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>On GKE Standard clusters using control plane version 1.24.2-gke.300 or later, you can configure the cluster and node pools to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/managing-logs#throughput">deploy an alternative version of the Logging agent designed to maximize logging throughput</a>. The default Logging agent running in each GKE cluster guarantees at least 100 KB per second log throughput per node for system and workload logs. This Logging agent variant provides a 100x improvement, allowing for throughput as high as 10 MB per second on nodes that have at least 2 unused CPU cores. </p>

<p>Additionally, all GKE clusters with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/managing-metrics#system-metrics">system metrics</a> enabled now export a new metric (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/node/logs/input_bytes</code>), which indicates the number of log bytes generated on a node. <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/managing-logs#identify-throughput">Using this metric</a> can help you decide which variant of the logging agent makes sense to deploy in your cluster or node pools.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_08_2022" data-text="September 08, 2022" tabindex="-1">September 08, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The Calico issue link included in the  <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#August_19_2022">August 19, 2022</a> release notes issue was updated to the <a href="https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/issues/4857" class="external">Calico issue #4857</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_07_2022" data-text="September 07, 2022" tabindex="-1">September 07, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ip-masq-agent</code> is not able to boot up on Arm nodes in GKE clusters with control planes running the following versions:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>2022-R18: 1.23.8-gke.1900, 1.24.2-gke.1900</p></li>
<li><p>2022-R19: 1.24.3-gke.200</p></li>
<li><p>2022-R20: 1.23.9-gke.900, 1.24.3-gke.900</p></li>
</ul>

<p>This regression has been fixed. Please upgrade your control plane to versions included in the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#2022-r21_version_updates">2022-R21</a> release.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>CVE-2021-4160, CVE-2022-1664, CVE-2022-1292, and CVE-2022-29155 have been patched in the Filestore CSI driver for newly created clusters.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="August_23_2022" data-text="August 23, 2022" tabindex="-1">August 23, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>For <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/alias-ips">VPC-native clusters</a>, the user-managed secondary range for Services can now be shared among clusters in the same subnet. The Services range no longer needs to be unique for clusters on the same subnet. Shared Services ranges are backwards-compatible with all GKE versions.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>CVE-2022-24675 CVE-2022-2068 CVE-2022-28327 have been patched in the PD CSI driver in 1.23 for newly created clusters.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_19_2022" data-text="August 19, 2022" tabindex="-1">August 19, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>GKE clusters that run versions 1.22 or later and use Calico Network Policy might experience issues with terminating Pods. The Calico CNI plugin shows error terminating Pods, and eviction takes too long.</p>

<p>Pods that experience this issue display an error message similar to the following:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Text only" syntax-guessed><code translate="no" dir="ltr">Warning FailedKillPod 36m (x389 over 121m) kubelet error killing pod: failed to "KillPodSandbox" for "af9ab8f9-d6d6-4828-9b8c-a58441dd1f86" with KillPodSandboxError: "rpc error: code = Unknown desc = networkPlugin cni failed to teardown pod "myclient-pod-6474c76996" network: error getting ClusterInformation: connection is unauthorized: Unauthorized"
</code></pre></devsite-code>
<p>To resolve this issue, restart the calico-node pods or restart kubelet.</p>

<p>This link was updated on September 8, 2022: For more information about this issue, see <a href="https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/issues/4857" class="external">Calico issue #4857</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_18_2022" data-text="August 18, 2022" tabindex="-1">August 18, 2022</h2>

<h2 id="August_15_2022" data-text="August 15, 2022" tabindex="-1">August 15, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The GKE Clusters List page now includes a new Observability tab. This tab shows infrastructure health metric trends such as CPU, Memory, container restarts and Control Plane metrics. It also provides visibility into ingestion into Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus and Cloud Logging. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/view-observability-metrics">View observability metrics</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_08_2022" data-text="August 08, 2022" tabindex="-1">August 08, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Newly created GKE Clusters on version 1.24 or later using Services without <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.spec.ports</code> field defined will cause a crash-loop of the ingress-gce controller (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">l7lbcontroller</code> pod). This will result in not being able to provide L7 Ingress, L4 Internal LoadBalancer Service with Subsetting turned on, and L4 Network LoadBalancer based on Regional Backend Services in the cluster.</p>

<p>To recover from this situation, delete the Service without a port specified or recreate the cluster without any Service with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.spec.ports</code> undefined.</p></div>
    </div>
