<h2 id="August_03_2022" data-text="August 03, 2022" tabindex="-1">August 03, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The maximum number of Pods that can run on each node has increased from 110 to 256 with GKE version 1.23.5-gke.1300 or later. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/flexible-pod-cidr#overview">Optimizing IP address allocation</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE total size control is now available in GKE version 1.24 clusters. For autoscaled node pools you can now set the minimum and maximum number of the total number of nodes across all zones, rather than specify a per zone limit. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-autoscaler#minimum_and_maximum_node_pool_size">Cluster autoscaler</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_27_2022" data-text="July 27, 2022" tabindex="-1">July 27, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE node system configuration now supports setting the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-system-config#cgroup-mode-options">cgroup mode</a> to use the cgroupv2 resource management subsystem.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="July_22_2022" data-text="July 22, 2022" tabindex="-1">July 22, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE Gateway integration with Cloud Certificate Manager is now available as Public Preview in GKE versions 1.20 and later. Use the new TLS features and high scale offered by Cloud Certificate Manager with GKE Gateway. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/gateway-security">Gateway Security</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_21_2022" data-text="July 21, 2022" tabindex="-1">July 21, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/managing-metrics#control-plane-metrics">Kubernetes control plane metrics</a> are now Generally Available. You can now configure GKE clusters with control plane version 1.23.6-gke.1500 or later to export to Cloud Monitoring certain metrics emitted by the Kubernetes API server, scheduler, and controller manager.</p>

<p>These metrics are stored in Cloud Monitoring in a Prometheus-compatible format. They can be queried by sending either a PromQL or MQL query to the Cloud Monitoring API. They can also be used anywhere within Cloud Monitoring, including in custom dashboards or alerting rules.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>If you start a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/credential-rotation#completing_the_rotation">credential rotation</a> or an <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ip-rotation#completing_the_rotation">IP address rotation</a>, ensure that you manually complete the rotation. If an operation causes a control plane re-creation while the rotation remains incomplete, your cluster might enter a broken state.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="July_15_2022" data-text="July 15, 2022" tabindex="-1">July 15, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Clusters that are using custom or manually created EndpointSlices (EPS) can cause Ingresses and NEGs to stop syncing if missing the service label kubernetes.io/service-name: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">&lt;service-name&gt;</code>. This issue affects clusters running GKE 1.21, 1.22, and 1.23. Users should add the service label to all custom-made EndpointSlices to ensure that their Ingresses and NEGs continue to be synced.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Cluster autoscaler Location Policy is now generally available in GKE version 1.24.1-gke.800. This change allows users to pick one of two different spreading policies. For more information see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-autoscaler#location_policy">Location policy</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_13_2022" data-text="July 13, 2022" tabindex="-1">July 13, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now run Arm-based workloads in Preview in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/create-arm-clusters-nodes">Standard clusters</a> with GKE version 1.24 and later, and in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-arm-workloads">Autopilot clusters</a> with GKE version 1.24.1-gke.1400 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now select <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/autopilot-compute-classes">compute classes</a> to run GKE Autopilot workloads that have specialized hardware requirements, such as Arm architecture. The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Scale-Out</code> compute class is available in Preview in Autopilot clusters running GKE version 1.24.1-gke.1400 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_06_2022" data-text="July 06, 2022" tabindex="-1">July 06, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/node-pool-upgrade-strategies#blue-green-upgrade-strategy">blue-green upgrade mechanism</a> is now available to upgrade your GKE node pools, and can be selected per node pool instead of the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-upgrades#surge">default surge upgrade mechanism</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A new vulnerability (CVE-2022-1786) has been discovered in the Linux kernel versions 5.10 and 5.11. This vulnerability allows an unprivileged user with local access to the cluster to achieve a full container breakout to root on the node. Only clusters that run Container-Optimized OS are affected. GKE Ubuntu versions use either version 5.4 or 5.15 of the kernel and are not affected. For more information, refer to the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-017">GCP-2022-017 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>GKE Cost Allocation has been released for public preview. With GKE Cost
Allocation public preview, you will be able to see cost breakdowns in clusters
for namespaces, and pod labels for utilized CPU and MEM. For complete details,
refer to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cost-allocations">View detailed breakdown of cluster costs</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_29_2022" data-text="June 29, 2022" tabindex="-1">June 29, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now give multiple containers time-shared access to the full compute resources of a single NVIDIA GPU accelerator. Time-sharing GPUs is generally available in GKE version 1.23.7-gke.1400 and later. For more information, refer to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/timesharing-gpus">Time-sharing GPUs on GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_24_2022" data-text="June 24, 2022" tabindex="-1">June 24, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>Three new memory corruption vulnerabilities (CVE-2022-29581, CVE-2022-29582, CVE-2022-1116) have been discovered in the Linux kernel. These vulnerabilities allow an unprivileged user with local access to the cluster to achieve a full container breakout to root on the node. All Linux clusters (Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu) are affected. For more information, refer to the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-016-gke">GCP-2022-016 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now create dual-stack clusters in Alpha Compute Engine API-enabled projects with GKE versions 1.24.1-gke.1000 and later. With dual-stack networking, GKE assigns an IPv4 and an IPv6 address to the cluster nodes and Pods. You can create dual-stack Services of type ClusterIP or NodePort.
This feature is now available in Preview. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/alias-ips#dual_stack_network">Dual-stack networking</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="June_22_2022" data-text="June 22, 2022" tabindex="-1">June 22, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>To deliver a better default price-performance for applications, all GKE clusters created with control plane version 1.24 and later have the Balanced Persistent Disk (PD) by default for attached volumes. Additionally,  the node boot disk default has also been changed to Balanced Persistent Disk (PD).</p>

<p>The new default for attached volumes is applied to all clusters running control plane version 1.24 and later. The new default node boot disk is applied to all new node pools of any node pool version created in a cluster with control plane version 1.24 and later. Existing preferences will not be changed.</p>

<p>For more information on boot disks, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/custom-boot-disks">Configuring a custom boot disk</a>.</p>

<p>For more information on attached volumes see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/persistent-volumes">Persistent volumes and dynamic provisioning</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_15_2022" data-text="June 15, 2022" tabindex="-1">June 15, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/confidential-gke-nodes">Confidential GKE Nodes</a> is now generally available in GKE version 1.22 and later for stateful workloads using persistent disks, and in all GKE versions for stateless workloads. Use Confidential GKE Nodes to encrypt your workload data in-use through Compute Engine <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/confidential-vm/docs/about-cvm#confidential-vm">Confidential VMs</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="124_is_now_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="1.24 is now available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">1.24 is now available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.24 is now available in the Rapid channel. Before upgrading, read the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.24.md#urgent-upgrade-notes" class="external">Kubernetes 1.24 Release Notes</a>, especially the action required and deprecation sections.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="notable_changes" data-text="Notable changes" tabindex="-1">Notable changes</h4>

<ul>
<li>GKE does not support node images that use Docker as the runtime in GKE version 1.24 and later. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/docker-containerd">migrating from Docker to containerd</a>.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">Secret</code> API objects containing service account tokens are not automatically created in 1.24.
<ul>
<li>This change improves security by reducing readable, permanent, Secret-based tokens to ones that have been explicitly requested, and improves performance by reducing the amount of persisted Secret data and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/encrypting-secrets#limitations">avoiding unnecessary utilization of application-layer secrets encryption</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Existing Secret-based tokens from previous versions remain valid on upgrade</strong>.</li>
<li>Secret-based tokens are not used by nodes or pods on version 1.21 and later.</li>
<li>Only node versions 1.22 and later are supported running against 1.24 clusters.</li>
<li>Clients retrieving tokens directly from the API can still obtain a token using these methods supported in all available GKE versions:
<ul>
<li>Preferred: Use the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/authentication-resources/token-request-v1/" class="external">TokenRequest API</a> to obtain time-bound tokens that are not readable by other API clients. The <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubectl/kubectl-commands#-em-token-em-" class="external"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl create token</code></a> command is available in kubectl 1.24+ to simplify use of this API from the command line.</li>
<li>Secret-based tokens can still be obtained by <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#manually-create-a-service-account-api-token" class="external">creating a Secret object and waiting for it to be populated with a token</a>.</li>
</ul></li>
<li>Examples of incorrect ways to obtain Secret-based tokens from the API include:
<ul>
<li>Scanning the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">secrets[*].name</code> field of a ServiceAccount object; this field lists secrets usable by pods running as that service account, not for other purposes, and secrets in that list have never been guaranteed to be service account token secrets.</li>
<li>Looking for existing Secret objects of type <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/service-account-token</code> created by other clients; a Secret created by another client is owned by that client, and cannot be assumed to be stable for use by other clients.</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>Kubernetes 1.24 <a href="https://go.dev/doc/go1.18#sha1" class="external">deprecates support for insecure serving certificates signed with a SHA-1 hash</a>. Aggregated API servers, admission webhooks, and custom resource conversion webhooks using TLS certificates that are signed by SHA-1 should replace the serving certificates as soon as possible.</p>

<ul>
<li><p>At cluster version 1.24.0 and later, GKE provides a Cloud Audit log to check if your cluster contains an affected service. You can use the following filter to search for the logs of a 1.24+ cluster:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Carbon" syntax-guessed><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">logName</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"projects/$PROJECT/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-nx">resource</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-k">type</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"k8s_cluster"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-nx">operation</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">producer</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"k8s.io"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s">"invalid-cert.kubernetes.io"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-err">```</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></li>
<li><p>If you are not affected you won&#39;t see any logs. If you do see such an audit log, it will include the name of the service (whether webhook or aggregated API).</p></li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="new_api_versions" data-text="New API versions" tabindex="-1">New API versions</h4>

<ul>
<li>storage.k8s.io/v1 CSIStorageCapacity</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Nodes on version 1.24.0-gke.1000 with more than 80GB of memory will fail to start successfully due to a known bug, which will be resolved in future 1.24 versions.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_api_versions" data-text="Deprecated API versions" tabindex="-1">Deprecated API versions</h4>

<p>These APIs are still served in version 1.24 but are in a deprecation period:</p>

<ul>
<li><p><a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/04/06/podsecuritypolicy-deprecation-past-present-and-future/" class="external">PodSecurityPolicy</a> </p>

<ul>
<li>policy/v1beta1 PodSecurityPolicy</li>
<li>Deprecated in 1.21 with <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#psp-v125" class="external">removal targeted</a> for version 1.25.</li>
<li>1.24 is the last version supporting the beta PodSecurityPolicy feature. Use of this feature must be discontinued before clusters will upgrade to 1.25. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/podsecuritypolicy">PodSecurityPolicy deprecation</a>.</li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-25" class="external">removed in 1.25</a> in favor of their newer versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 EndpointSlice, deprecated since 1.21</li>
<li>policy/v1beta1 PodDisruptionBudget, deprecated since 1.21</li>
<li>batch/v1beta1 CronJob, deprecated since 1.21</li>
<li>node.k8s.io/v1beta1 RuntimeClass</li>
<li>autoscaling/v2beta1 HorizontalPodAutoscaler</li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-26" class="external">removed in 1.26</a> in favor of newer versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta1 FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration
<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.23</li>
<li>use flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2 instead, available since 1.23</li>
</ul></li>
<li>autoscaling/v2beta2 HorizontalPodAutoscaler
<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.23</li>
<li>use autoscaling/v2 instead, available since 1.23 (or autoscaling/v1)</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-27" class="external">removed in 1.27</a> in favor of new versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>storage.k8s.io/v1beta1 CSIStorageCapacity, deprecated since 1.24</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_25_2022" data-text="May 25, 2022" tabindex="-1">May 25, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now easily assess the running cost implications at cluster creation time.
The GKE cluster cost widget lets you get an estimated cost range when you are creating a cluster.</p>

<p>This information can help you get a better understanding of the upper and lower monthly cost to expect based on your cluster autoscaling setup.
This feature is now available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products/#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>.</p>

<p>For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/containers-kubernetes/introducing-the-new-gke-cost-estimator">Introducing GKE cost estimator, built right into the Google Cloud console</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>GKE clusters that run control plane versions 1.21 or later and node versions 1.16 or earlier might experience:</p>

<ul>
<li>Readiness check failures.</li>
<li>Network endpoint groups (NEGs)  and load balancers (LBs) not created or synced. </li>
</ul>

<p>This occurs because the Ingress controllers running in GKE cluster control plane versions 1.21 or later are not compatible with node versions 1.16 and earlier. To resolve this issue, upgrade your node pools.</p>

<p>For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/troubleshooting#node_version_not_compatible_with_control_plane_version">Node version not compatible with control plane version</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_24_2022" data-text="May 24, 2022" tabindex="-1">May 24, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">us-east5</code></a> region in Columbus, Ohio
is now available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_20_2022" data-text="May 20, 2022" tabindex="-1">May 20, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now quickly identify which of your workloads are underutilized in the Cost Optimization tab. You can also quickly apply suggested values for resource requests and limits (or your own preferred values).</p>

<p>This feature is now available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products/#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/containers-kubernetes/workload-rightsizing-now-available-for-gke">GKE workload rightsizing</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="May_13_2022" data-text="May 13, 2022" tabindex="-1">May 13, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/tags">Tags</a> are now available. You can use tags to group or organize your clusters according to custom business dimensions. This is in addition to the hierarchical resource organization provided by Google Cloud&#39;s resource manager. The integration of tags with policy engines (via conditional rules) such as <a href="https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/tags-access-control">IAM</a> or <a href="https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/organization-policy/tags-organization-policy">Organization Policy</a>, also allows you to apply centralized policies to custom security perimeters defined through tag bindings.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="April_27_2022" data-text="April 27, 2022" tabindex="-1">April 27, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>Two security vulnerabilities, <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2022-1055" class="external">CVE-2022-1055</a> and <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2022-27666" class="external">CVE-2022-27666</a> have been discovered in the Linux kernel. Each can lead to a local attacker being able to perform a container breakout, privilege escalation on the host, or both. These vulnerabilities affect all GKE node operating systems (Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu). For instructions and more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-014-gke">GCP-2022-014 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="April_20_2022" data-text="April 20, 2022" tabindex="-1">April 20, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">europe-west8</code></a> region in Milan
is now available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_13_2022" data-text="April 13, 2022" tabindex="-1">April 13, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Egress NAT policy to configure IP masquerade is now generally available on GKE Autopilot clusters with Dataplane v2 in versions 1.22.7-gke.1500+ or 1.23.4-gke.1600+. For configuration examples of Egress NAT policy, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/egress-nat-policy-ip-masq-autopilot">Egress NAT Policy</a> documentation.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A security vulnerability, CVE-2022-23648, has been discovered in containerd&#39;s handling of path
traversal in the OCI image volume specification. Containers launched through containerd&#39;s CRI
implementation with a specially-crafted image configuration could gain full read access to
arbitrary files and directories on the host. This vulnerability may bypass any policy-based
enforcement on container setup (including a Kubernetes Pod Security Policy). This
vulnerability affects all GKE node operating systems
(Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu) which use containerd by default. All
GKE, Autopilot, and GKE Sandbox nodes are affected.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-013">GCP-2022-013 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="March_22_2022" data-text="March 22, 2022" tabindex="-1">March 22, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>There is a misconfiguration with Simultaneous Multi-Threading (SMT), also known as Hyper-threading, on GKE Sandbox images. The misconfiguration leaves nodes potentially exposed to side channel attacks such as Microarchitectural Data Sampling (MDS) (for more context, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/sandbox-pods#hyper-threading_is_disabled">GKE Sandbox documentation</a>).
We do not recommend using the following affected versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.22.4-gke.1501</li>
<li>1.22.6-gke.300</li>
<li>1.23.2-gke.300</li>
<li>1.23.3-gke.600</li>
</ul>

<p>For instructions and more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-011">GKE security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="March_16_2022" data-text="March 16, 2022" tabindex="-1">March 16, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Starting in GKE version 1.22, the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/gce-pd-csi-driver">Compute Engine persistent disk CSI driver</a> is generally available for Windows clusters.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_15_2022" data-text="March 15, 2022" tabindex="-1">March 15, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The following GKE versions fix a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#0bde303b">known issue</a> in which random TCP connection resets might happen for GKE nodes that use Container-Optimized OS with Docker (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">cos</code>). To fix the issue, upgrade your nodes to any of these versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.20.15-gke.3400 and later</li>
<li>1.21.10-gke.1300 and later</li>
<li>1.22.7-gke.1300 and later</li>
<li>1.23.4-gke.1300 and later</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.23.2-gke.300 and later, you can now use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/autopilot-network-tags">network tags to dynamically apply firewall rules</a> to nodes in your GKE Autopilot clusters and auto-provisioned GKE Standard node pools without disrupting running workloads.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_09_2022" data-text="March 09, 2022" tabindex="-1">March 09, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The following GKE versions fix a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#December_14_2021">known issue</a> in which the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE</code> file capability was dropped from the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">metrics-server</code>. To fix the issue, upgrade your control plane to any of these versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.21.9-gke.1002 and later</li>
<li>1.21.10-gke.400 and later</li>
<li>1.22.6-gke.300 and later</li>
<li>1.22.7-gke.300 and later</li>
<li>1.22.7-gke.900 and later</li>
<li>1.23.4-gke.300 and later</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_08_2022" data-text="March 08, 2022" tabindex="-1">March 08, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>Setting a minimum CPU platform for node pools created by node auto-provisioning using the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.clusters#autoprovisioningnodepooldefaults"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">autoscaling.autoprovisioning_node_pool_defaults.min_cpu_platform</code></a> field is deprecated. This field will be removed in a future release. In GKE versions 1.23 and later, you can request a minimum CPU platform at the workload level using a node selector or node affinity rule for <code translate="no" dir="ltr">cloud.google.com/requested-min-cpu-platform</code>. For instructions, refer to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-auto-provisioning#custom_min_cpu">Minimum CPU platform</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_07_2022" data-text="March 07, 2022" tabindex="-1">March 07, 2022</h2>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for

information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/oidc">Identity Service for GKE</a> is now generally available. You can authenticate to GKE clusters with external identity providers that use OpenID Connect (OIDC).</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_04_2022" data-text="March 04, 2022" tabindex="-1">March 04, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Public clusters created on GKE versions 1.22 and later, and created between October 28, 2021 and February 17, 2022 use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/private-service-connect">Private Service Connect (PSC)</a>. Therefore, each control plane is assigned to a private IP address from the cluster node subnet.</p>

<p>For public clusters created outside of this time frame or with a different GKE version, the control plane has a public IP address by default.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>Some unexpected paths to access the node VM on GKE Autopilot clusters could have been used to escalate privileges in the cluster. These issues have been fixed and <strong>no further action is required</strong>. The fixes address issues reported through our <a href="https://bughunters.google.com/about">Vulnerability Reward Program</a>.</p>

<p>For instructions and more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-009">GCP-2022-009 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_25_2022" data-text="February 25, 2022" tabindex="-1">February 25, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The Envoy project recently discovered a set of vulnerabilities. All
 issues listed below are fixed in Envoy release 1.21.1.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-008">GCP-2022-008 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

is now available in the Rapid channel.</li>
<li>The following versions are no longer available in the Rapid channel:
<ul>
<li>1.21.6-gke.1500</li>
<li>1.22.3-gke.700</li>
<li>1.22.3-gke.1500</li>
<li>1.23.2-gke.300</li>
</ul></li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel
will be upgraded from version 1.20 to <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v1219" class="external">1.21.9-gke.1001</a> 
with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel
will be upgraded from version 1.21 to <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v1219" class="external">1.21.9-gke.1001</a> 
with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel
will be upgraded from version 1.23 to <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.23.md#v1233" class="external">1.23.3-gke.1100</a> 
with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>GKE nodes that use Container-Optimized OS with Docker (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">cos</code>) may experience random TCP connection resets when two pods on the same node communicate using a Kubernetes ClusterIP Service.</p>

<p>For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/node-images#known_issues">GKE Node images known issues</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_22_2022" data-text="February 22, 2022" tabindex="-1">February 22, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/traffic-management">GKE Gateway traffic management</a> is now in Preview for GKE 1.22 and later version clusters. You can now <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/horizontal-pod-autoscaling#autoscale-traffic">autoscale Pods</a> or <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/deploying-multi-cluster-gateways#capacity-load-balancing">dynamically shift traffic between clusters</a> based on Service traffic capacity.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_17_2022" data-text="February 17, 2022" tabindex="-1">February 17, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Kubernetes Network Policy API allows specifying range of ports (see <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-network/2079-network-policy-port-range" class="external">KEP on port ranges</a>) on which the policy is enforced in GKE 1.22 and later versions. If you specify <code translate="no" dir="ltr">endPort</code> field in a Network Policy, it might not take effect in Dataplane V2 based on the cluster configuration. This API will be supported in Calico Network Policy enabled clusters but not in Dataplane V2 clusters. </p>

<p>For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/dataplane-v2#known_issues">GKE Dataplane V2 known issues</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_15_2022" data-text="February 15, 2022" tabindex="-1">February 15, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A security vulnerability, <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2022-0492">CVE-2022-0492</a>,
        has been discovered in the Linux kernel&#39;s <code translate="no" dir="ltr">cgroup_release_agent_write</code> function.
        The attack uses unprivileged user namespaces, and under certain circumstances, this
        vulnerability can be exploitable for container breakout.</p>

<p>For more information, see the
 <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-006">GCP-2022-006 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_14_2022" data-text="February 14, 2022" tabindex="-1">February 14, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>Kubernetes 1.23 is now available in the Rapid channel. Before upgrading, read the
<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.23.md#urgent-upgrade-notes">Kubernetes 1.23 Release Notes</a>,
especially the action required and deprecation
sections. Also, read the guide for <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/webhookcompatibility">ensuring compatibility of webhook and aggregated API server certificates</a> before the upgrade.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_11_2022" data-text="February 11, 2022" tabindex="-1">February 11, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A security vulnerability, <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-43527">CVE-2021-43527</a>, has been discovered in any binary that links to the vulnerable versions of libnss3 found in NSS (Network Security Services) versions prior to 3.73 or 3.68.1.</p>

<p>Applications using NSS for certificate validation or other TLS, X.509, OCSP or CRL functionality may be impacted, depending on how they configure NSS. </p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-005">GCP-2022-005 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_10_2022" data-text="February 10, 2022" tabindex="-1">February 10, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>Versions 1.21.9-gke.300, 1.22.6-gke.300, and 1.23.2-gke.300 contain a fix for a race condition which could result in erroneously detaching all endpoints from network endpoint groups for a short period.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_04_2022" data-text="February 04, 2022" tabindex="-1">February 04, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A security vulnerability, <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-4034" class="external">CVE-2021-4034</a>, has been discovered in pkexec, a part of the Linux policy kit package (polkit), that allows an authenticated user to perform a privilege escalation attack. PolicyKit is generally used only on Linux desktop systems to allow non-root users to perform actions such as rebooting the system, installing packages, restarting services etc, as governed by a policy. GKE clusters are <strong>not affected</strong>.</p>

<p>For instructions and more details, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-004-gke">GCP-2022-004 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>You will not be able to create new node pools that use a Docker node image starting with GKE v1.23 when: </p>

<ul>
<li>Creating a new cluster, </li>
<li>Adding a node pool to an existing cluster, or</li>
<li>Using Node Auto-provisioning (NAP) with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--autoprovisioning-image-type</code> set to Docker node images. </li>
<li>For existing clusters, you will also not be able to change the value of <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--autoprovisioning-image-type</code> to Docker node images. </li>
</ul>

<p>If you are upgrading your GKE clusters from GKE v1.22 to v1.23, then you will be able to continue using:</p>

<ul>
<li>Docker node pools that were configured before the upgrade.</li>
<li>Cluster Autoscaler on Docker node pools.</li>
<li>Node Auto-provisioning (NAP) with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--autoprovisioning-image-type</code> set to Docker node images if it was configured before upgrading to v1.23. However, we highly recommend you to migrate to GKE node images that use the Containerd container runtime.</li>
</ul>

<p>For your reference, below are the GKE node images for the Containerd and Docker container runtimes:</p>

<ul>
<li>Containerd container runtime (recommended): <code translate="no" dir="ltr">cos_containerd</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ubuntu_containerd</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">windows_ltsc_containerd</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">windows_sac_containerd</code></li>
<li>Docker container runtime (unsupported starting with v1.24): <code translate="no" dir="ltr">cos</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ubuntu</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">windows_ltsc</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">windows_sac</code></li>
</ul>

<p>Containerd is the default runtime on GKE. Most user workloads do not have dependencies on the container runtime. Support for Docker as a container runtime on Kubernetes nodes will be removed from OSS Kubernetes and GKE starting with v1.24. If you use a node image based on Docker container runtime, please migrate your GKE workloads to a Containerd node image as soon as possible. For more details, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/using-containerd#migrating">Containerd node images</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_03_2022" data-text="February 03, 2022" tabindex="-1">February 03, 2022</h2>

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

<h2 id="February_02_2022" data-text="February 02, 2022" tabindex="-1">February 02, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>Three security vulnerabilities, <a href="https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2021-4154" class="external">CVE-2021-4154</a>, <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=2021-22600" class="external">CVE-2021-22600</a>, and <a href="https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2022-0185" class="external">CVE-2022-0185</a> have been discovered in the Linux kernel, each of which can lead to either a container breakout, privilege escalation on the host, or both. These vulnerabilities affect all GKE node operating systems and Anthos clusters on VMware node operating systems (COS and Ubuntu). </p>

<p>Pods using <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/sandbox-pods">GKE Sandbox</a> are not vulnerable to these vulnerabilities. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2022-002">GCP-2022-002 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_31_2022" data-text="January 31, 2022" tabindex="-1">January 31, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE, you can now filter Pub/Sub cluster notifications by notification type.
For more information, see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cluster-notifications#filtering">Receive cluster notifications</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>When creating a maintenance exclusion window, you can restrict the exclusion to
specify types of maintenance. For example, during a specific time period you can
exclude minor upgrades from occurring on your cluster. For more information, see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/maintenance-windows-and-exclusions#exclusions">Maintenance exclusions</a> documentation.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_27_2022" data-text="January 27, 2022" tabindex="-1">January 27, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Starting with GKE version 1.23.0, if a Kubernetes event is created using
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s.io/api/core/v1</code>, the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">LastTimestamp</code> field is used as the timestamp of the
corresponding event log if the field is non-empty. Otherwise, the timestamp
field will be unset and will be determined by Cloud Logging.</p>

<p>If a Kubernetes event is created using <code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s.io/api/events/v1</code>, the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Series.LastObservedTime</code> field is used as the timestamp of the corresponding
event log if the field is non-empty. Otherwise, the timestamp field will be
unset and will be determined by Cloud Logging. An event created with
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s.io/api/events/v1</code> will be converted to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s.io/api/core/v1</code> before exporting to
Cloud Logging.</p>

<p>Log payload of an event log will contain the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">LastTimestamp</code> field from
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s.io/api/core/v1</code> Event API. If an event is created using <code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s.io/api/events/v1</code>,
the value of this field will be <code translate="no" dir="ltr">null</code>. Instead, use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Series.LastObservedTime</code>
field in the log payload.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_21_2022" data-text="January 21, 2022" tabindex="-1">January 21, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="notable_changes_and_bug_fixes" data-text="Notable changes and bug fixes" tabindex="-1">Notable changes and bug fixes</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.23 is built with go1.17, which requires aggregated API servers,
admission webhooks, and custom resource conversion webhooks to use TLS
certificates that include the service DNS name as a subjectAltName.</p>

<ul>
<li>Before upgrading to 1.23, ensure any non-local aggregated API servers,
admission webhooks, and custom resource conversion webhooks in your cluster
are served using valid TLS certificates.</li>
<li><p>At cluster version 1.22.3-gke.700 or higher, GKE provides a Cloud Audit log to
check if your cluster contains an affected service. You can use the following
filter to search for the logs:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded><code translate="no" dir="ltr">logName: &#34;projects/$PROJECT/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity&#34;
resource.type = &#34;k8s_cluster&#34;
operation.producer = &#34;k8s.io&#34;
&#34;invalid-cert.webhook.gke.io&#34;
</code></pre></devsite-code></li>
<li><p>If you are not affected you won&#39;t see any logs. If you do see such an audit
log, it will include the name of the service (whether webhook or aggregated
API).</p></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="123_is_now_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="1.23  is now available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">1.23  is now available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.23 is now available in the Rapid channel. Before upgrading, read
the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.23.md#urgent-upgrade-notes" class="external">Kubernetes 1.23 Release Notes</a>,
especially the action required and deprecation sections.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><h4 id="notable_features" data-text="Notable features" tabindex="-1">Notable features</h4>

<h5 id="beta_podsecurity_admission" data-text="Beta: PodSecurity admission" tabindex="-1">Beta: PodSecurity admission</h5>

<p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">PodSecurity</code> replaces the deprecated <code translate="no" dir="ltr">PodSecurityPolicy</code> admission controller
(which will be removed in 1.25). <code translate="no" dir="ltr">PodSecurity</code> is an admission controller that
enforces <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/">Pod Security Standards</a>
on Pods in a Namespace based on specific namespace labels that set the
enforcement level. In 1.23, the PodSecurity feature is enabled by default, and
applies to namespaces that opt into enforcement. Refer to the
<a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-admission/">PodSecurity documentation</a>
and <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/migrate-from-psp/">PodSecurityPolicy migration guide</a>
for more information.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="new_api_versions" data-text="New API versions" tabindex="-1">New API versions</h4>

<ul>
<li>flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2 FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration</li>
<li>autoscaling/v2 HorizontalPodAutoscaler</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_api_versions" data-text="Deprecated API versions" tabindex="-1">Deprecated API versions</h4>

<p>These APIs are still served in version 1.23 but are in a deprecation period:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/04/06/podsecuritypolicy-deprecation-past-present-and-future/" class="external">PodSecurityPolicy</a> 
<ul>
<li>policy/v1beta1 PodSecurityPolicy</li>
<li>Deprecated in 1.21 with <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#psp-v125" class="external">removal targeted</a> for version 1.25.</li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-25" class="external">removed in 1.25</a> 
in favor of their GA versions:
<ul>
<li>discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 EndpointSlice, deprecated since 1.21</li>
<li>policy/v1beta1 PodDisruptionBudget, deprecated since 1.21</li>
<li>batch/v1beta1 CronJob, deprecated since 1.21</li>
<li>node.k8s.io/v1beta RuntimeClass</li>
<li>autoscaling/v2beta1 HorizontalPodAutoscaler</li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-26" class="external">removed in 1.26</a> 
in favor of newer versions:
<ul>
<li>flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta1 FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration
<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.23</li>
<li>use flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2 instead, available since 1.23</li>
</ul></li>
<li>autoscaling/v2beta2 HorizontalPodAutoscaler
<ul>
<li>deprecated since 1.23</li>
</ul></li>
<li>use autoscaling/v2 instead, available since 1.23 (or autoscaling/v1)</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Clusters running GKE node versions 1.19.16-gke.1500 and 1.19.16-gke.3600 will be
unstable if Container Threat Detection (KTD) is enabled. To use KTD, create the
cluster with the most recent 1.19.15 version or any GKE version 1.20 or later. If you
require GKE version 1.19.16-gke.1500 or 1.19.16-gke.3600, you should disable KTD
on the cluster using the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/how-to-configure-security-command-center#advanced_settings">Cloud Security Command Center Advanced Settings</a>
before creating or upgrading nodes to these versions</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_20_2022" data-text="January 20, 2022" tabindex="-1">January 20, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cloud-dns#vpc_scope_dns">VPC-scoped DNS</a> for GKE using Cloud DNS is now generally available for GKE versions 1.21 and later. This allows for seamless VPC-wide DNS resolution of GKE Services. Note that cluster-scoped DNS using Cloud DNS is still in public preview.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>A new kubernetes metric, <strong>Network policy event count
(kubernetes.io/pod/network/policy_event_count)</strong>, is available (<strong>beta</strong>) for
GKE Dataplane V2 clusters in GKE versions 1.22.3-gke.700 and later.</p>

<p>This metric can be viewed in the Metrics Explorer in Cloud Monitoring for
resource type, Kubernetes Pod.</p>

<p>This metric provides visibility into
<a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/" class="external">network policy</a> 
events and shows the <strong>Change in the number of network policy events seen in
the dataplane</strong>, each event has the following metric labels:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>verdict</strong>: Policy verdict, possible values: [allow, deny].</li>
<li><strong>workload_kind</strong>: Kind of the workload, policy-enforced-pod belongs to, for
example, &quot;Deployment&quot;, &quot;Replicaset&quot;, &quot;StatefulSet&quot;, &quot;DaemonSet&quot;, &quot;Job&quot;, or
&quot;CronJob&quot;.</li>
<li><strong>workload_name</strong>: Name of the workload, policy-enforced-pod belongs to.</li>
<li><strong>direction</strong>: Direction of the traffic from the point of view of
policy-enforced-pod, possible values: [ingress, egress].</li>
</ul>

<p>In addition to these metric labels, customers can also see usual resource labels
for resource type, Kubernetes Pod: <strong>project_id, location, cluster_name,
namespace_name, and pod_name</strong>.</p>

<p>This metric can be used for setting up automated alerts for specific behaviors
(denials higher than a threshold), identifying security issues, gaining better
understanding of traffic flow, and troubleshooting.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_17_2022" data-text="January 17, 2022" tabindex="-1">January 17, 2022</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Now available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>: Use a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/compact-placement">compact placement policy</a> to specify that nodes within the node pool should be placed in closer physical proximity to each other within a zone. Having nodes closer to each other can reduce network latency between nodes, which can be useful for tightly-coupled batch workloads.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_20_2021" data-text="December 20, 2021" tabindex="-1">December 20, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>A bug was found in containerd where container root directories and some plugins had insufficiently restricted permissions, allowing otherwise unprivileged Linux users to traverse directory contents and execute programs.</p>

<p>This issue is fixed in the following GKE versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.22.3-gke.1100 or above</li>
<li>1.21.6-gke.700 or above</li>
<li>1.20.12-gke.700 or above</li>
<li>1.19.16-gke.700 or above</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information about the CVE, refer to <a href="https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-41103" class="external">CVE-2021-41103</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>For GKE versions 1.21 and later, newly created clusters will have the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#denyserviceexternalips" class="external">DenyServiceExternalIPs</a> admission controller enabled by default, disabling the use of ExternalIPs Services.</p>

<p>For existing clusters, when you upgrade the cluster to GKE version 1.21 or later, the DenyServiceExternalIPs admission controller will not be enabled. Since ExternalIPs Services are not widely used, we recommend manually auditing any external IP usage. You can choose to block ExternalIPs by using the following command:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Bash"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>container<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>clusters<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>update<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>--no-enable-service-externalips
</code></pre></devsite-code>
<p>For more information, refer to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/hardening-your-cluster#deny_external_IPs">Hardening your cluster&#39;s security</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_14_2021" data-text="December 14, 2021" tabindex="-1">December 14, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>File capability <code translate="no" dir="ltr">CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE</code> required by <code translate="no" dir="ltr">metrics-server</code> to bind privileged port <code translate="no" dir="ltr">443</code> is dropped in clusters that enable PodSecurityPolicy and use the Ubuntu with Docker container runtime in node pools. As a result, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">metrics-server</code> fails to bootstrap and autoscaling functionality fails to function. All 1.21 and 1.22 node versions are impacted. This issue will be fixed in a future release. Automatic node upgrades from GKE version 1.20 to 1.21 will be halted until this issue is fixed.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_09_2021" data-text="December 09, 2021" tabindex="-1">December 09, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>GKE version 1.22.3-gke.1500 and later support <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authentication/#user-impersonation" class="external">user impersonation</a> for all user-defined users and groups. System users and groups such as the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kube-apiserver</code> user and the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">system:masters</code> group cannot be impersonated.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_06_2021" data-text="December 06, 2021" tabindex="-1">December 06, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>PodSecurityPolicy (beta) was <a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/04/06/podsecuritypolicy-deprecation-past-present-and-future/" class="external">deprecated in Kubernetes 1.21</a> and is scheduled for shutdown in 1.25. For alternatives, refer to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/podsecuritypolicy">PodSecurityPolicy deprecation</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The following GKE versions fix <a href="https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/issues/4710" class="external">Calico issue #4710</a> and <a href="https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/issues/4518" class="external">Calico issue #4518</a>, related to Pod graceful termination, in GKE clusters with Calico Network Policy enabled:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.19.16-gke.100 and later</li>
<li>1.20.11-gke.1300 and later</li>
<li>1.21.4-gke.1500 and later</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information about the resolved issue, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/network-policy#statefulset_calico">known issues page</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_03_2021" data-text="December 03, 2021" tabindex="-1">December 03, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#2021-r32_version_updates">2021-R32</a>
release notes from October 29, 2021 were updated on December 03, 2021 with revisions to the upgrade
versions for control plane and nodes in Rapid, Regular, Stable, and No Channel.</p>

<p>See the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#revisions_for_2021-r32">revision note</a>
for further details.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="December_02_2021" data-text="December 02, 2021" tabindex="-1">December 02, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The following GKE versions contain an issue that might affect workloads that use
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/sandbox-pods">GKE Sandbox</a>:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.19.14-gke.301, 1.19.14-gke.1900, 1.19.14-gke.2300, 1.19.15-gke.500, 1.19.15-gke.1300, 1.19.15-gke.1801</li>
<li>1.20.10-gke.301, 1.20.10-gke.1600, 1.20.10-gke.2100, 1.20.11-gke.1300, 1.20.11-gke.1801</li>
<li>1.21.4-gke.2300, 1.21.4-gke.2302, 1.21.5-gke.1300, 1.21.5-gke.1302, 1.21.5-gke.1802</li>
<li>1.22.2-gke.1901</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>What do I need to know?</strong></p>

<p>Applications that use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">xmm15</code> register and receive a signal or hit a page
fault while the register is in use might have the register corrupted, leading to
unpredictable application behavior. The security of the sandbox is not
compromised.</p>

<p><strong>What do I need to do?</strong></p>

<p>Upgrade to one of the following GKE versions that fix the issue:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.19.16-gke.1500 or later</li>
<li>1.20.12-gke.1500 or later</li>
<li>1.21.6-gke.1500 or later</li>
<li>1.22.3-gke.700 or later</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="November_12_2021" data-text="November 12, 2021" tabindex="-1">November 12, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The release on <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#September_17_2021">September 17, 2021 (2021-R29)</a>
fixed CVEs in the Compute Engine PD CSI driver for the cluster minor version
1.18. The fixes are available in GKE version 1.18.20-gke.5900 and later.</p>

<p>The following CVEs were fixed: CVE-2021-3712, CVE-2021-3580, CVE-2021-33910,
CVE-2020-29361, CVE-2020-29362, CVE-2021-24031, CVE-2021-3711, CVE-2021-20305,
CVE-2020-24659, CVE-2021-24032, CVE-2021-20231, CVE-2021-20232, CVE-2021-33560,
CVE-2020-29363, CVE-2021-3520, and CVE-2020-27350.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Legacy networks that contain GKE clusters can be converted to VPC networks, if the required control plane and node pool upgrades are performed. This feature is available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/legacy#single-region-conversion">Single-region conversion tool</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

Spot Pods let you run fault-tolerant workloads at lower costs.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_04_2021" data-text="November 04, 2021" tabindex="-1">November 04, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">

For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/image-streaming">Use image streaming to pull container images</a>.</p></div>

</div></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_28_2021" data-text="October 28, 2021" tabindex="-1">October 28, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>GKE public clusters versions 1.22 and later created on or after October 28, 2021, will move to using <a href="https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/private-service-connect">Private Service Connect</a> (PSC) for private control plane communication. There is no price increase for using GKE public clusters running on PSC, however, there will be a SKU change. This change does not apply to public clusters using <a href="https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/legacy">legacy networks</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>In clusters running GKE version 1.21.0-gke.1000 and later, the destination IP address and port of the GKE metadata server has changed. If you have a cluster network policy and you use Workload Identity, you should update your network policy to allow access to the following destination IP addresses and ports. To avoid disruptions during auto-upgrades, allow access to all these destination address and destination port combinations in your network policy. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/workload-identity#gke_mds">Understanding the GKE metadata server</a>.</p>

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>GKE version</th>
<th>GKE metadata server address</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Prior to 1.21.0-gke.1000</td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">127.0.0.1:987</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">127.0.0.1:988</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.21.0-gke.1000 and later</td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">169.254.169.252:987</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">169.254.169.252:988</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_27_2021" data-text="October 27, 2021" tabindex="-1">October 27, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.22 and later, GKE cluster autoscaler and node auto-provisioning will support working on empty (zero node) clusters, and will support scaling down nodes with pods requesting local storage.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_21_2021" data-text="October 21, 2021" tabindex="-1">October 21, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>For GKE Autopilot clusters, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/using-cmek">CMEK for boot disks</a>
and CMEK for <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/encrypting-secrets#enabling">application-layer encryption</a>
is now generally available.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A security issue was discovered in the Kubernetes ingress-nginx controller, <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-25742" class="external">CVE-2021-25742</a>. Ingress-nginx custom snippets allows retrieval of ingress-nginx service account tokens and secrets across all namespaces. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2021-024">GCP-2021-024 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>For GKE Autopilot clusters, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/role-based-access-control#google-groups-for-gke">Google Groups for RBAC</a> is now generally available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_15_2021" data-text="October 15, 2021" tabindex="-1">October 15, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2021-r31_version_updates" data-text="(2021-R31) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2021-R31) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="no-channel_174" data-text="No channel" tabindex="-1">No channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#v12010" class="external">1.20.10-gke.1600</a> 
is now the default version.</li>
<li><p>The following control plane and node versions are now available:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v11915" class="external">1.19.15-gke.1300</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#v12011" class="external">1.20.11-gke.1300</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v1215" class="external">1.21.5-gke.1300</a> </li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>Control plane version 1.19.13-gke.701 is no longer available.</p></li>
<li><p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded from
version 1.19 to <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v11913" class="external">1.19.13-gke.1900</a> 
with this release.</p></li>
<li><p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded from
version 1.20 to <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#v12010" class="external">1.20.10-gke.1600</a> 
with this release.</p></li>
</ul></section>

the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>

<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v11913" class="external">1.19.13-gke.1900</a> 
with this release.</p></li>
</ul></section>

all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>

    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>GKE Windows clusters using the persistent disk CSI driver ​might experience volume mount issues with existing <code translate="no" dir="ltr">PersistentVolumeClaim</code> or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">PersistentVolume</code> resources if upgraded to one the following versions. Please do not upgrade your Windows node pools to the following versions in the Rapid channel:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.22.1-gke.1602 or later</li>
</ul>

<p>The fix will be available in a future GKE 1.22 release.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_14_2021" data-text="October 14, 2021" tabindex="-1">October 14, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>StatefulSet Pods in Calico Network Policy enabled GKE clusters might experience connectivity issues in a <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Terminating</code> state in the following GKE versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.18</li>
<li>1.19</li>
<li>1.20 to 1.20.11-gke.1299</li>
<li>1.21 to 1.21.4-gke.1499</li>
</ul>

<p>To mitigate this issue, upgrade your GKE control plane to GKE version
1.21.4-gke.1500 or later.<br>
For more information, see the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/network-policy#statefulset_calico">known issue</a>
and <a href="https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/issues/4710">Calico issue #4710</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_13_2021" data-text="October 13, 2021" tabindex="-1">October 13, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The following GKE versions fix containerd issue <a href="https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/5438">#5438</a>. This issue caused pod IP address leaks which exhaust the IP addresses of containerd based nodes.</p>

<ul>
<li>1.19.14-gke.1500 or later</li>
<li>1.20.10-gke.1500 or later</li>
<li>1.21.4-gke.1600 or later</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see the Containerd node images <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/using-containerd#containerd-pod-ip-leak">known issues</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_12_2021" data-text="October 12, 2021" tabindex="-1">October 12, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/spot-vms">Spot VMs</a> on GKE is now available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>With GKE version 1.19 and later, the CPU and memory usage of gke-metrics-agent have been optimized. With this change, Out Of Memory (OOM) crashes are reduced significantly.</p>

<p>If you are on GKE version 1.18 and earlier, you will need to upgrade your clusters to version 1.19 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_04_2021" data-text="October 04, 2021" tabindex="-1">October 04, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE version 1.20.8-gke.2100 or later offers a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a> of a fully managed metric collection pipeline to scrape Prometheus-style metrics exposed by any GKE workload and send those metrics to Cloud Monitoring for dashboards, alerts, and SLOs. Compared to the Prometheus Stackdriver sidecar, this new pipeline is easy to set up, allows filtering to control cost, supports larger clusters, is fully managed, supports Autopilot and horizontal Pod autoscaling, and offers better pricing. Get started with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/managing-metrics#workload-metrics">GKE workload metrics</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_01_2021" data-text="October 01, 2021" tabindex="-1">October 01, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>1.20 clusters with legacy ABAC authorization enabled should not upgrade to 1.21 until 1.21.4-gke.2500+ is available.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
