all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v1214" class="external">1.21.4-gke.1801</a> 
is now the default version in the Rapid channel.</li>
<li>The following control plane and node versions are now available in the Rapid
channel:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v1214" class="external">1.21.4-gke.2300</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v1221" class="external">1.22.1-gke.1602</a> </li>
</ul></li>
<li>Version 1.21.4-gke.301 is no longer available in the Rapid channel.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from
version 1.21 to <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v1214" class="external">1.21.4-gke.1801</a> 
with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel will be upgraded from
version 1.22 to <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.22.md#v1221" class="external">1.22.1-gke.1602</a> 
with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The following features are introduced in version 1.21:</p>

<h4 id="cronjob_ga" data-text="CronJob (GA)" tabindex="-1">CronJob (GA)</h4>

<p>The CronJob API has graduated to General Availability (GA), bringing performance improvements and allowing scheduled jobs to be run using a stable API.</p>

<ul>
<li>This resource is now available in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">batch/v1</code> group/version. </li>
<li>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">batch/v1beta1</code> group/version is deprecated, and will be removed in
version 1.25. See the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-25" class="external">migration guide</a> 
for details.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="poddisruptionbudget_ga" data-text="PodDisruptionBudget (GA)" tabindex="-1">PodDisruptionBudget (GA)</h4>

<p>The PodDisruptionBudget has graduated to GA, allowing Pod evictions to be
controlled using a stable API.</p>

<ul>
<li>This resource is now available in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">policy/v1</code> group/version.</li>
<li>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">policy/v1beta1</code> group/version is deprecated, and will be removed in
version 1.25. See the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-25" class="external">migration guide</a> 
for details.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="endpointslice_ga" data-text="EndpointSlice (GA)" tabindex="-1">EndpointSlice (GA)</h4>

<p>The EndpointSlice API has graduated to GA, bringing performance improvements
over the v1 Endpoints API.</p>

<ul>
<li>This more scalable API for service discovery is now enabled on all clusters
and is promoted to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">discovery.k8s.io/v1</code>.</li>
<li>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1</code> group/version is deprecated, and will be
removed in version 1.25. See the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-25" class="external">migration guide</a> 
for details.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="default_namespace_label_beta" data-text="Default namespace label (Beta)" tabindex="-1">Default namespace label (Beta)</h4>

<p>Namespace API objects now have a <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/metadata.name</code> label matching
their <code translate="no" dir="ltr">metadata.name</code> field to allow selecting any namespace by its name using a
label selector. This can be used for objects which select namespaces by label,
such as <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/#matching-requests-namespaceselector" class="external">admission webhooks</a> 
and <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/#targeting-a-namespace-by-its-name" class="external">network policies</a>.</p>

<h4 id="bound_service_account_token_volumes_beta" data-text="Bound service account token volumes (Beta)" tabindex="-1">Bound service account token volumes (Beta)</h4>

<ul>
<li>The API credentials injected into containers at <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token</code>
are now time-limited, auto-refreshed, and invalidated when the containing
pod is deleted.</li>
<li>By default, injected tokens are given an extended lifetime so they remain
valid even after a new refreshed token is provided. The metric
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">serviceaccount_stale_tokens_total</code> and the audit annotation
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">authentication.k8s.io/stale-token</code> can be used to monitor for workloads
that depend on the extended lifetime and are continuing to use tokens even
after a refreshed token is provided to the container.</li>
<li>Clients should reload the token from disk periodically (once per minute is
recommended) to ensure they use the refreshed token. <code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s.io/client-go</code>
version 11.0.0+ and 0.15.0+ reload tokens automatically.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><h4 id="notable_features_in_122" data-text="Notable features in 1.22" tabindex="-1">Notable features in 1.22</h4>

<h5 id="ga_server-side_apply" data-text="GA: Server-side Apply" tabindex="-1">GA: Server-side Apply</h5>

<p><em>Server-side Apply</em> is a new object merge algorithm, as well as tracking of field
ownership, running on the Kubernetes API server. Server-side Apply helps users
and controllers create and modify their resources via declarative configurations
by sending their fully specified intent. Refer to <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/server-side-apply/" class="external">server-side apply
documentation</a> 
for more information. Improvements in 1.22 include:</p>

<ul>
<li>scale subresource ownership is tracked correctly (<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/98377" class="external">#98377</a>)</li>
<li>label selector fields are applied atomically (<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/97989" class="external">#97989</a>)</li>
</ul>

<h5 id="beta_daemonset_maxsurge" data-text="Beta: DaemonSet maxSurge" tabindex="-1">Beta: DaemonSet maxSurge</h5>

<p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">DaemonSet</code> objects now support a <code translate="no" dir="ltr">maxSurge</code> rollout parameter, which allows
running updated pods for the DaemonSet on nodes before removing old pods. Refer
to the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#rollingupdatedaemonset-v1-apps" class="external">DaemonSet API documentation</a> 
for more information.</p>

<h5 id="beta_suspended_jobs" data-text="Beta: Suspended jobs" tabindex="-1">Beta: Suspended jobs</h5>

<p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">Job</code> objects can now be created or placed in a suspended state, to allow
higher-level control over ordering and scheduling of batch workloads. Refer to
the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/job/#suspending-a-job" class="external">Job documentation</a> 
for more information.</p>

<h5 id="beta_podaffinity_namespace_selection" data-text="Beta: podAffinity namespace selection" tabindex="-1">Beta: podAffinity namespace selection</h5>

<p>Pod affinity rules can now specify namespaced using a label selector, in
addition to a fixed list of namespace names. Refer to the
<a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#namespace-selector" class="external">pod affinity documentation</a> 
for more information.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="new_api_versions_in_122" data-text="New API versions in 1.22" tabindex="-1">New API versions in 1.22</h4>

<p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">pods/eviction</code> subresource now accepts <code translate="no" dir="ltr">policy/v1</code> eviction requests in
addition to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">policy/v1beta1</code> eviction requests
(<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/100724" class="external">#100724</a>)</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="deprecated_api_versions" data-text="Deprecated API versions" tabindex="-1">Deprecated API versions</h4>

<p>These APIs are still served in version 1.22 but are in a deprecation period, and
will be removed in 1.25:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/04/06/podsecuritypolicy-deprecation-past-present-and-future/" class="external">PodSecurityPolicy</a> 
<ul>
<li>policy/v1beta1 PodSecurityPolicy</li>
<li>Deprecated in 1.21 with <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#psp-v125" class="external">removal targeted</a> for version 1.25.</li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following Beta versions of graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-25" class="external">removed in 1.25</a> 
in favor of their GA versions:
<ul>
<li>discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 EndpointSlice, deprecated since 1.21</li>
<li>policy/v1beta1 PodDisruptionBudget, deprecated since 1.21</li>
<li>batch/v1beta1 CronJob, deprecated since 1.21</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="121_is_now_generally_available" data-text="1.21 is now generally available" tabindex="-1">1.21 is now generally available</h4>

<p>Kubernetes version 1.21 is now generally available. Before upgrading, read the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#changelog-since-v1200" class="external">Kubernetes 1.21 Release Notes</a>, especially the action required and deprecation sections.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="notable_changes_and_bug_fixes_in_122" data-text="Notable changes and bug fixes in 1.22" tabindex="-1">Notable changes and bug fixes in 1.22</h4>

<ul>
<li><p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">terminationGracePeriodSeconds</code> field on pod specs and container probes
should not be negative. Negative values of <code translate="no" dir="ltr">terminationGracePeriodSeconds</code>
will be treated as the value <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1</code> on the delete path. Immutable field
validation will be relaxed in order to update negative values. In a future
release, negative values will not be permitted. (<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/98866" class="external">#98866</a>)</p></li>
<li><p>As a mitigation for <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103675" class="external">CVE-2021-25740</a>,
newly created Kubernetes 1.22 clusters no longer include write access to the
Endpoints API in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">edit</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">admin</code> roles by default. Existing clusters
upgraded to Kubernetes 1.22 retain previous permissions in those roles. For
instructions to re-add Endpoints write access to the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">edit</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">admin</code>
roles in newly created 1.22 clusters, refer to the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/rbac/#write-access-for-endpoints" class="external">RBAC documentation</a>.</p></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_30_2021" data-text="September 30, 2021" tabindex="-1">September 30, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes, CVE-2021-25741, where
a user may be able to create a container with subpath volume mounts to
access files &amp; directories outside of the volume, including on the host
filesystem.
  For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2021-018">GCP-2021-018 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A security vulnerability, <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2020-8561" class="external">CVE-2020-8561</a>,
has been discovered in Kubernetes where certain webhooks can be made to
redirect <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kube-apiserver</code> requests to private networks of that API
server.
For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2021-021">GCP-2021-021 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>There is a known issue where updating a <code translate="no" dir="ltr">BackendConfig</code> resource using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">v1beta1</code> API that removes an active Google Cloud Armor security policy from its service.
  For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2021-019">GCP-2021-019 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Now you can see how effectively your GKE clusters and workloads are utilizing your available compute resources. The new Cost Optimization tab lets you view, filter, and learn more about the CPU and memory usage, requests, allocation, and limit amounts of each of your clusters and workloads. This information can help you identify opportunities to optimize your clusters or workloads for more cost effective resource utilization. This feature is now available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products/#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cost-optimization-metrics">View cost-related optimization metrics</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_24_2021" data-text="September 24, 2021" tabindex="-1">September 24, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>GKE clusters running node pools that use Docker might experience containers restarting every time Docker restarts.</p>

<p>The following versions are affected:</p>

<ul>
<li>GKE 1.20 versions lower than 1.20.9-gke.2100 </li>
<li>GKE 1.21 versions lower than 1.21.3-gke.1600 </li>
</ul>

<p>To fix this issue, either use Containerd or upgrade your nodes to version:</p>

<ul>
<li>For GKE 1.20: 1.20.9-gke.2100 or higher</li>
<li>For GKE 1.21: 1.21.3-gke.1600 or higher</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>GKE versions 1.18.20-gke.5100 and later fix the issue with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">v1beta1</code> of the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Backendconfig</code> API, where a Cloud Armor security policy was inadvertently deleted from the backend Service of an Ingress resource.</p>

<p>For more information, see Kubernetes <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-gce/issues/1508" class="external">issue #1508</a> and the Ingress <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ingress-features#armor_fields_removed">Known issues</a> page.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_17_2021" data-text="September 17, 2021" tabindex="-1">September 17, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2021-r29_version_updates" data-text="(2021-R29) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2021-R29) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="no-channel_176" data-text="No channel" tabindex="-1">No channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#v1209" class="external">1.20.9-gke.1001</a> 
is now the default version.</li>
<li>Control plane version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#v1209" class="external">1.20.9-gke.1000</a> 
is now available.</li>
<li>The following control plane and node versions are now available:
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v11820" class="external">1.18.20-gke.6000</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v11914" class="external">1.19.14-gke.1900</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#v12010" class="external">1.20.10-gke.1600</a> </li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following control plane versions are no longer available:
<ul>
<li>1.17.17-gke.9100</li>
<li>1.18.20-gke.901</li>
<li>1.18.20-gke.2300</li>
</ul></li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded from
version 1.18 to <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v1182" class="external">1.18.20-gke.3001</a> 
with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="stable-channel_176" data-text="Stable channel" tabindex="-1">Stable channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on

is now available in the Stable channel.</li>
<li>The following versions are no longer available in the Stable channel:
<ul>

<li>1.18.20-gke.3001</li>

will be upgraded from version 1.19 to
<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v11913" class="external">1.19.13-gke.701</a>

will be upgraded from version 1.20 to
<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#v1209" class="external">1.20.9-gke.1000</a> 
with this release.</li>
</ul></section>

</div></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_16_2021" data-text="September 16, 2021" tabindex="-1">September 16, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE versions 1.21.0-gke.1500 and later, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/alias-ips">VPC-native</a>
is the default network mode during cluster creation. To create a routes-based cluster, you can use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--no-enable-ip-alias</code> flag:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Bash"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>container<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>clusters<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>create<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>CLUSTER_NAME<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>--no-enable-ip-alias
</code></pre></devsite-code></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>For Autopilot clusters, starting with GKE version <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.21.3-gke.900</code>:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>Users can also create mutating webhooks. However, Autopilot modifies the
mutating webhooks objects to add a namespace selector which excludes the
resources in managed namespaces (currently, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kube-system</code>) from being
intercepted. Additionally, webhooks which specify one or more of following
resources (and any of their sub-resources) in the rules, will be rejected:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="YAML"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-p devsite-syntax-p-Indicator">-</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">group</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">""</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">resource</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">nodes</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-p devsite-syntax-p-Indicator">-</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">group</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">""</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">resource</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">persistentvolumes</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-p devsite-syntax-p-Indicator">-</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">group</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">certificates.k8s.io</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">resource</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">certificatesigningrequests</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-p devsite-syntax-p-Indicator">-</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">group</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">authentication.k8s.io</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">resource</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">tokenreviews</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></li>
<li><p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">SYS_PTRACE</code> capability is allowed in user workloads.</p></li>
<li><p>Gatekeeper is no longer used in Autopilot policy enforcement, letting users
install their own Gatekeeper instances.</p></li>
</ul>

<p>When downgrading Autopilot clusters versions <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1.21</code> to the older minor versions,
the cluster might intermittently become unavailable. Once the downgrade is
complete, the cluster will be available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_14_2021" data-text="September 14, 2021" tabindex="-1">September 14, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>With GKE versions 1.21.4-gke.30 and later, users can create <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balancing#ilb_psc">ServiceAttachment resources</a> to provision <a href="https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/private-service-connect">Private Service Connect (PSC)</a> for internal LoadBalancer Services. This feature is available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Multi-cluster Ingress now supports <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/multi-cluster-ingress#ssl_policies_and_https_redirects">SSL policies and HTTPS redirects</a> using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">FrontendConfig</code> resource. This feature is generally available in GKE versions 1.17.13-gke.2600 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_13_2021" data-text="September 13, 2021" tabindex="-1">September 13, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>GKE versions 1.19.14-gke.301 and later fix the issue with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">v1beta1</code> of the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Backendconfig</code> API, where a Cloud Armor security policy was inadvertently deleted from the backend Service of an Ingress resource.</p>

<p>For more information, see Kubernetes <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-gce/issues/1508" class="external">issue #1508</a> and the Ingress <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ingress-features#armor_fields_removed">Known issues</a> page.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_09_2021" data-text="September 09, 2021" tabindex="-1">September 09, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/filestore-csi-driver">managed Filestore CSI driver for GKE</a> is now available in GKE versions 1.21 and later to provision and manage Filestore instances for GKE workloads.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_08_2021" data-text="September 08, 2021" tabindex="-1">September 08, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>Several <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud</code> flags used to configure which logs and metrics are collected are deprecated and replaced with new flags. See <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/installing#deprecated_configuration_parameters">Deprecated Configuration Parameters</a> for a list of the deprecated logging and monitoring flags as well as the equivalent values for the new <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--logging</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--monitoring</code> flags.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_07_2021" data-text="September 07, 2021" tabindex="-1">September 07, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The R28 release notes were updated on September 24, 2021 with the following additions:</p>

<p><strong>No channel</strong></p>

<p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded from version 1.18 to <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v11912" class="external">1.19.12-gke.2101</a> with this release.</p>

<p><strong>Stable channel</strong></p>

<p>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded from version 1.18 to <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v11912" class="external">1.19.12-gke.2101</a> with this release.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2021-r28_version_updates" data-text="(2021-R28) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2021-R28) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">

all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>

<li>The following control plane and node versions are now available:
<ul>

<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v11820" class="external">1.18.20-gke.4501</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v11912" class="external">1.19.12-gke.2101</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v11913" class="external">1.19.13-gke.701</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v11914" class="external">1.19.14-gke.301</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#v1208" class="external">1.20.8-gke.2101</a> </li>

</ul></li>

<li>1.19.13-gke.700</li>
<li>1.19.14-gke.300</li>
<li>1.20.8-gke.2100</li>
<li>1.20.9-gke.700</li>
<li>1.20.9-gke.1000</li>
</ul></li>

with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded from
version 1.20 to <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#v1208" class="external">1.20.8-gke.2101</a> 
with this release.</li>
</ul></section>

the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across

<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Stable channel will be upgraded from

<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#v1209" class="external">1.20.9-gke.701</a>

<li>The following control plane and node versions are now available in the Regular channel:

<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v1213" class="external">1.21.3-gke.2001</a> 
is now the default version in the Rapid channel.</li>
<li>The following control plane and node versions are now available in the Rapid
channel:
<ul>

</ul></li>

version 1.21 to <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#v1213" class="external">1.21.3-gke.2001</a>

</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>Two security vulnerabilities,
<a href="https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-33909" class="external">CVE-2021-33909</a> and
<a href="https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-33910" class="external">CVE-2021-33910</a>, have been
discovered in the Linux kernel that can lead to an OS crash or an escalation to root by an
unprivileged user. This vulnerability affects all GKE node operating systems (COS and Ubuntu).</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2021-017">GCP-2021-017 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_02_2021" data-text="September 02, 2021" tabindex="-1">September 02, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gpus-multi">Multi-Instance GPU</a> on GKE is is now generally available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_30_2021" data-text="August 30, 2021" tabindex="-1">August 30, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-autoscaler#autoscaling_profiles">GKE Autoscaling profiles</a>
are now generally available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_24_2021" data-text="August 24, 2021" tabindex="-1">August 24, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Identity Service for GKE (<a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>) is available. Identity Service for GKE extends existing identity solutions for authentication into GKE clusters by supporting OpenID Connect (OIDC). For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/oidc">Authenticating with Identity Service for GKE</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now enable Google Virtual NIC in a new GKE cluster on GPU nodes. For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/using-gvnic">Using Google Virtual NIC</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_20_2021" data-text="August 20, 2021" tabindex="-1">August 20, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2021-r27_version_updates" data-text="(2021-R27) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2021-R27) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>

all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>

is now the default version.</li>
<li>The following control plane and node versions are now available:

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>For GKE clusters running Windows Server node pools, you can proactively receive
updates about new GKE versions and the Windows OS versions they use by
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cluster-upgrade-notifications#upgradeavailable">subscribing to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">UpgradeAvailableEvent</code> notifications</a>.
This feature is now available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_19_2021" data-text="August 19, 2021" tabindex="-1">August 19, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>A simplified GKE API for configuring which logs and metrics are collected and sent to Cloud Logging and Cloud Monitoring is now available. The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/container/clusters/create#--logging"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud container clusters create</code></a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/container/clusters/update#--logging"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud container clusters update</code></a> commands now support the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--logging</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">--monitoring</code> flags.</p>

<p>For example, to collect both system and workload logs in an existing cluster, use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud container clusters update --logging=SYSTEM,WORKLOAD</code>. Or, to create a new cluster with no metrics collected, use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud container clusters create --monitoring=NONE</code>.</p>

<p>See a complete list of <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/installing#available-logs">available logs</a> and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/installing#available-metrics">available metrics</a>.</p>

<p>These flags are available in Google Cloud SDK version 352.0.0 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_18_2021" data-text="August 18, 2021" tabindex="-1">August 18, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>GKE clusters running node pools that use containerd might experience IP leak issues and exhaust all Pod IPs on a node. 
A Pod scheduled on an affected node shows an error message similar to the following: </p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-disable-click-to-copy devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded><code translate="no" dir="ltr">failed to allocate for range 0: no IP addresses available in range set: 10.48.131.1-10.48.131.62
</code></pre></devsite-code>
<p>For more information about the issue, see containerd <a href="https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/5438" class="external">issue #5438</a> and <a href="https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/5768" class="external">issue #5768</a>.</p>

<p>For workarounds to mitigate this issue, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/using-containerd#known_issues">Known issues section in containerd node images</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_17_2021" data-text="August 17, 2021" tabindex="-1">August 17, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>An issue was identified with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">v1beta1</code> of the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">BackendConfig</code> API, where a Cloud Armor security policy was inadvertently deleted from the backend Service of an Ingress resource on the following affected GKE versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.18.19-gke.1400 and later</li>
<li>1.19.10-gke.700 and later</li>
<li>1.20.6-gke.700 and later</li>
</ul>

<p>To fix this issue, use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">v1</code> of the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">BackendConfig</code> API, or update your clusters to one of the following GKE versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.20.9-gke.900 and later</li>
<li>1.21.1-gke.2700 and later</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information, see Kubernetes <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-gce/issues/1508" class="external">issue #1508</a> and the Ingress <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ingress-features#armor_fields_removed">Known issues</a> page.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="July_21_2021" data-text="July 21, 2021" tabindex="-1">July 21, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/role-based-access-control#google-groups-for-gke">Google Groups for RBAC</a> is now generally available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_20_2021" data-text="July 20, 2021" tabindex="-1">July 20, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>Legacy Logging and Monitoring was <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/deprecations/legacy">deprecated</a> December 12, 2019 and was decommissioned March 31, 2021. As described in the guide for <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/migration">Migrating to Cloud Operations for GKE</a> all clusters still using Legacy Logging and Monitoring are being automatically and gradually migrated to Cloud Operations for GKE during the coming weeks.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

<h2 id="July_14_2021" data-text="July 14, 2021" tabindex="-1">July 14, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A new security vulnerability, <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-22555" class="external">CVE-2021-22555</a>, has been discovered where a malicious actor with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">CAP_NET_ADMIN</code> privileges can potentially cause a container breakout to root on the host. This vulnerability affects all GKE clusters and Anthos clusters on VMware running Linux version 2.6.19 or later.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2021-015">GCP-2021-015 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_13_2021" data-text="July 13, 2021" tabindex="-1">July 13, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>There is a known issue that prevents the gcloud client from interacting with multi-cluster Ingress that was introduced in gcloud version 346.0.0 and was fixed in version 348.0.0. It is recommended that you do not use gcloud versions 346.0.0 and 347.0.0 when using multi-cluster Ingress.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="July_08_2021" data-text="July 08, 2021" tabindex="-1">July 08, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>Microsoft published a security bulletin on a Remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability, <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-34527">CVE-2021-34527</a>, that affects the print spooler in Windows servers. The CERT Coordination Center (CERT/CC) published an update note on a related vulnerability, dubbed &quot;PrintNightmare&quot; that also affects Windows print spoolers - <a href="https://us-cert.cisa.gov/ncas/current-activity/2021/06/30/printnightmare-critical-windows-print-spooler-vulnerability">PrintNightmare, Critical Windows Print Spooler Vulnerability</a>.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2021-014">GCP-2021-014 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_02_2021" data-text="July 02, 2021" tabindex="-1">July 02, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Config Management is now available on GKE. Config Management provides you with the following benefits:</p>

<ul>
<li>You can now use Policy Controller. Policy Controller enables the enforcement of fully programmable policies for your clusters. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos-config-management/docs/concepts/policy-controller">Policy Controller overview</a>.</li>
<li>You can now install Config Sync using the Cloud Console or the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud</code> command line tool. To learn more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos-config-management/docs/how-to/installing-config-sync">Installing Config Sync</a>.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The Istio project recently <a href="https://istio.io/latest/news/security/istio-security-2021-007/">disclosed</a> a new security vulnerability, <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-34824">CVE-2021-34824</a>, affecting <a href="https://cloud.google.com/learn/what-is-istio">Istio</a>. Istio contains a remotely exploitable vulnerability where credentials specified in the Gateway and DestinationRule credentialName field can be accessed from different namespaces.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2021-012">GCP-2021-012 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_29_2021" data-text="June 29, 2021" tabindex="-1">June 29, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">asia-south2</code> <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones">region</a> in Delhi is now available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_28_2021" data-text="June 28, 2021" tabindex="-1">June 28, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In GKE node version 1.21.1-gke.2200 and later, Containerd is available as a runtime for Windows Server LTSC and SAC node images. Containerd is the recommended container runtime for GKE.  For more information, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/node-images#windows-server">Node images</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_25_2021" data-text="June 25, 2021" tabindex="-1">June 25, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>GKE clusters on some 1.18.18+ and 1.19.10+ versions might fail to create or
apply CustomResourceDefinitions containing integer validation rules using
server-side apply. The following error occurs: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">failed to convert new object to proper version: unable to convert unstructured object to apiextensions.k8s.io/v1, Kind=CustomResourceDefinition: cannot convert int64 to float64.</code></p>

<p>The following versions are affected:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.19.11-gke.1700</li>
<li>1.19.10-gke.1700</li>
<li>1.19.10-gke.1600</li>
<li>1.19.10-gke.1000</li>
<li>1.18.19-gke.1700</li>
<li>1.18.18-gke.1700</li>
<li>1.18.18-gke.1100</li>
</ul>

<p>To resolve this issue, upgrade to a newer version or downgrade to one of the
following versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.19.9-gke.1900</li>
<li>1.18.17-gke.1901</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

<h2 id="June_15_2021" data-text="June 15, 2021" tabindex="-1">June 15, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#April_19_2021">issue</a> affecting the Datadog Agent on Autopilot has been resolved in Datadog version 2.13.1.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_11_2021" data-text="June 11, 2021" tabindex="-1">June 11, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/multi-cluster-services">GKE Multi-cluster Services</a>
support for pod-specific addressing is now generally available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_10_2021" data-text="June 10, 2021" tabindex="-1">June 10, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Committed use discounts are now generally available to purchase for Google Kubernetes
Engine (Autopilot Mode).</p>

<p>Google Kubernetes Engine (Autopilot Mode) committed use discounts apply to all
Autopilot Pod workload vCPU, memory, and ephemeral storage usage in the region
in which you have committed. Google Kubernetes Engine (Autopilot Mode) committed
use discounts <em>do not apply</em> to the cluster management fee or to GKE Standard
mode compute nodes.</p>

<p>See the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/cud">documentation</a> for more
details.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>For GKE clusters running Windows Server node pools, you can see the version
mapping between GKE versions and Windows Server versions for all available GKE
versions by using a <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud</code> command. This feature is now available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">preview</a>.</p>

<p>For more details, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/creating-a-cluster-windows#gcloud_versionmapping">Use gcloud tool to get version mapping</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/volume-snapshots">Volume snapshots</a>
is now generally available. Starting in GKE version 1.21 and later, you can now
use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">v1</code> snapshots; <code translate="no" dir="ltr">v1beta1</code> snapshots will continue to operate as expected
until further notice.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_09_2021" data-text="June 09, 2021" tabindex="-1">June 09, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>If you manually upgrade your cluster from 1.18 to 1.19 and the network tier configuration on an existing external network load balancer does not match the network tier annotation in the service spec (if unspecified, defaults to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Premium</code>), the load balancer will be deleted and recreated, and the network tier configuration will be enforced.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>A domain-scoped project is not supported in GKE version 1.20. The cluster&#39;s <code translate="no" dir="ltr">CertificateSigningRequest</code> will be denied when validating the DNS name and the nodes cannot join the cluster.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Stable channel

with this release.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Stable channel
will be upgraded from version 1.19 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v11910" class="external">1.19.10-gke.1000</a> 
with this release.</li>

with this release.</li>

    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>As of version 1.20, the kubelet no longer creates the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">target_path</code> for
NodePublishVolume in accordance with the CSI spec. If you have self-managed CSI
drivers deployed in your cluster, ensure that they are idempotent and do any
necessary mount creation or verification. For more information, see Kubernetes
issue <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88759" class="external">#88759</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><h4 id="reminder_future_beta_api_removals_in_versions_122_and_125" data-text="Reminder: Future beta API removals in versions 1.22 and 1.25" tabindex="-1">Reminder: Future beta API removals in versions 1.22 and 1.25</h4>

<p>Kubernetes versions 1.22 and 1.25 will stop serving several deprecated beta
APIs. It is recommended to begin migrating your clients and manifests to the
stable replacement APIs now. More information is available in the
<a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#removed-apis-by-release" class="external">OSS Kubernetes documentation</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="120_is_now_generally_available" data-text="1.20 is now generally available" tabindex="-1">1.20 is now generally available</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.20 is now generally available (GA). Before upgrading, read the
<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#changelog-since-v1190" class="external">Kubernetes 1.20 Release Notes</a> 
especially the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#urgent-upgrade-notes" class="external">Urgent upgrade notes</a> 
and <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.20.md#deprecation" class="external">Deprecations</a> 
sections.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">metadata.selfLink</code> field, <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.16.md#deprecations-and-removals" class="external">deprecated since version 1.16</a>,
  is no longer populated in version 1.20. See Kubernetes <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/1164" class="external">issue #1164</a> 
for details. A related bug in the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go" class="external"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s.io/client-go</code>library</a> 
in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">GetReference</code> function was fixed in versions 0.15.9 or later, 0.16.4 or
later, and 0.17.0 or later. Clients using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">GetReference</code> function should
upgrade to one of those versions of <code translate="no" dir="ltr">client-go</code> or newer in order to work
correctly against an API Server running version 1.20 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/65200" class="external">Non-deterministic treatment of objects with invalid <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ownerReferences</code></a> 
was <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/92743" class="external">fixed in version 1.20</a>.
Run the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubectl-check-ownerreferences" class="external"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl-check-ownerreferences</code></a> 
tool prior to upgrade to locate existing objects with invalid <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ownerReferences</code>.</p>

<ul>
<li><p>A namespaced object with an <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ownerReference</code> to another namespaced object
which does not exist in the same namespace is now consistently treated as
having a missing owner and is deleted.</p></li>
<li><p>A cluster-scoped object with an <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ownerReference</code> to a namespaced object is
now consistently treated as having an unresolvable owner, and is ignored
by the garbage collector.</p></li>
<li><p>Starting in version 1.20, when a namespace mismatch between a child and owner
object is detected, an event with a reason code of
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">OwnerRefInvalidNamespace</code> is recorded.</p></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">node.k8s.io/v1beta1</code> RuntimeClass API has graduated to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">node.k8s.io/v1</code>
with no changes. API clients and manifests should switch to using the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">node.k8s.io/v1</code> API after version 1.20. The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">node.k8s.io/v1beta1</code> API is
deprecated and will no longer be served starting in version 1.25.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Starting in version 1.20, timeouts on exec probes are honored, and
default to 1 second if unspecified. If you have Pods using exec probes, ensure
that they can easily complete in 1 second or explicitly set an appropriate
timeout. For more information, see
<a href="https://docs.k8s.io/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes/#configure-probes" class="external">ConfigureProbes</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_07_2021" data-text="June 07, 2021" tabindex="-1">June 07, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>You can now specify the default image type to use for new auto-provisioning node pools. See <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-auto-provisioning#default-image-type">Using node auto-provisioning</a> for more details.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="June_04_2021" data-text="June 04, 2021" tabindex="-1">June 04, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The security community recently disclosed a new security vulnerability  <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-30465" class="external">CVE-2021-30465</a>  found in <code translate="no" dir="ltr">runc</code> that has the potential to allow full access to a node filesystem.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2021-011">GCP-2021-011 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_28_2021" data-text="May 28, 2021" tabindex="-1">May 28, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2021-r18_version_updates" data-text="(2021-R18) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2021-R18) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on versioning and upgrades, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">GKE versioning and support</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/upgrades">Upgrades</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">

the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v1199" class="external">1.19.9-gke.1900</a> 
is now the default version.</li>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v11818" class="external">1.18.18-gke.1700</a> 
is now available.</li>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v11910" class="external">1.19.10-gke.1700</a> 
is now available.</li>

all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v11817" class="external">1.18.17-gke.1200</a>

<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v11817" class="external">1.18.17-gke.1900</a> 
is now available in the Stable channel.</li>

<li>Version 1.17.17-gke.5400 is no longer available in the Stable channel.</li>
<li>Version 1.18.17-gke.700 is no longer available in the Stable channel.</li>
<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Stable channel
will be upgraded from version 1.18 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v11817" class="external">1.18.17-gke.1200</a> 
with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="regular-channel_187" data-text="Regular channel" tabindex="-1">Regular channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v1199" class="external">1.19.9-gke.1900</a>

</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="rapid-channel_187" data-text="Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Rapid channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on

<li>Control planes and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled in the Rapid channel

    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="121_new_beta_and_stable_apis" data-text="1.21 New Beta and Stable APIs" tabindex="-1">1.21 New Beta and Stable APIs</h4>

<p>The following Stable APIs are new in 1.21:</p>

<ul>
<li>batch/v1 CronJob</li>
<li>policy/v1 PodDisruptionBudget</li>
<li>discovery.k8s.io/v1 EndpointSlice</li>
</ul>

<p>The following Beta APIs are new in 1.21:</p>

<ul>
<li>storage.k8s.io/v1beta1 CSIStorageCapacity</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>GKE clusters running version 1.18 or later now support <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cloud-dns">container native Cloud DNS</a> (available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>). Cloud DNS can be used as the in-cluster DNS provider instead of kube-dns.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><h4 id="121_features" data-text="1.21 Features" tabindex="-1">1.21 Features</h4>

<p>The following features are introduced in version 1.21:</p>

<h4 id="cronjob_ga" data-text="CronJob (GA)" tabindex="-1">CronJob (GA)</h4>

<p>The CronJob API has graduated to General Availability (GA), bringing performance
improvements and allowing scheduled jobs to be run using a stable API.</p>

<ul>
<li>This resource is now available in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">batch/v1</code> group/version.</li>
<li>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">batch/v1beta1</code> group/version is deprecated, and will be removed in
version 1.25. See the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-25" class="external">migration guide</a> 
for details.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="poddisruptionbudget_ga" data-text="PodDisruptionBudget (GA)" tabindex="-1">PodDisruptionBudget (GA)</h4>

<p>The PodDisruptionBudget has graduated to GA, allowing pod evictions to be
controlled using a stable API.</p>

<ul>
<li>This resource is now available in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">policy/v1</code> group/version.</li>
<li>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">policy/v1beta1</code> group/version is deprecated, and will be removed in
version 1.25. See the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-25" class="external">migration guide</a> 
for details.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="endpointslice_ga" data-text="EndpointSlice (GA)" tabindex="-1">EndpointSlice (GA)</h4>

<p>The EndpointSlice API has graduated to GA, bringing performance improvements
over the v1 Endpoints API.</p>

<ul>
<li>This more scalable API for service discovery is now enabled on all clusters
and is promoted to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">discovery.k8s.io/v1</code>.</li>
<li>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1</code> group/version is deprecated, and will be
removed in version 1.25. See the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-25" class="external">migration guide</a> 
for details.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="default_namespace_label_beta" data-text="Default namespace label (Beta)" tabindex="-1">Default namespace label (Beta)</h4>

<p>Namespace API objects now have a <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/metadata.name</code> label matching
their <code translate="no" dir="ltr">metadata.name</code> field to allow selecting any namespace by its name using a
label selector. This can be used for objects which select namespaces by label,
such as <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/#matching-requests-namespaceselector" class="external">admission webhooks</a> 
and <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/#targeting-a-namespace-by-its-name" class="external">network policies</a>.</p>

<h4 id="bound_service_account_token_volumes_beta" data-text="Bound service account token volumes (Beta)" tabindex="-1">Bound service account token volumes (Beta)</h4>

<ul>
<li>The API credentials injected into containers at <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token</code>
are now time-limited, auto-refreshed, and invalidated when the containing
pod is deleted.</li>
<li>By default, injected tokens are given an extended lifetime so they remain
valid even after a new refreshed token is provided. The metric
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">serviceaccount_stale_tokens_total</code> and the audit annotation
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">authentication.k8s.io/stale-token</code> can be used to monitor for workloads
that depend on the extended lifetime and are continuing to use tokens even
after a refreshed token is provided to the container.</li>
<li>Clients should reload the token from disk periodically (once per minute is
recommended) to ensure they use the refreshed token. <code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s.io/client-go</code>
version 11.0.0+ and 0.15.0+ reload tokens automatically.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="121_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="1.21 available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">1.21 available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes version 1.21 is now available in the Rapid channel. Before upgrading,
read the <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.21.md#changelog-since-v1200" class="external">Kubernetes 1.21 Release Notes</a>,
especially the action required and deprecation sections.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><h4 id="121_deprecated_apis" data-text="1.21 Deprecated APIs" tabindex="-1">1.21 Deprecated APIs</h4>

<p>The following APIs are deprecated in the 1.21 release:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/04/06/podsecuritypolicy-deprecation-past-present-and-future/" class="external">PodSecurityPolicy</a> 
<ul>
<li>policy/v1beta1 PodSecurityPolicy</li>
<li>Deprecated in 1.21 with <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#psp-v125" class="external">removal targeted</a> for version 1.25.</li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following Beta versions of newly graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-25" class="external">removed in 1.25</a> in favor of GA versions:
<ul>
<li>discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 EndpointSlice</li>
<li>policy/v1beta1 PodDisruptionBudget</li>
<li>batch/v1beta1 CronJob</li>
</ul></li>
<li>The following Beta versions of previously graduated APIs will be <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-22" class="external">removed in 1.22</a> in favor of GA versions:
<ul>
<li>admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1, MutatingWebhookConfiguration</li>
<li>admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1, ValidatingWebhookConfiguration</li>
<li>apiextensions.k8s.io/v1beta1, CustomResourceDefinition</li>
<li>apiregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1, APIService</li>
<li>authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1, TokenReview</li>
<li>authorization.k8s.io/v1beta1, LocalSubjectAccessReview</li>
<li>authorization.k8s.io/v1beta1, SelfSubjectAccessReview</li>
<li>authorization.k8s.io/v1beta1, SubjectAccessReview</li>
<li>certificates.k8s.io/v1beta1, CertificateSigningRequest</li>
<li>coordination.k8s.io/v1beta1, Lease</li>
<li>extensions/v1beta1, Ingress</li>
<li>networking.k8s.io/v1beta1, Ingress</li>
<li>networking.k8s.io/v1beta1, IngressClass</li>
<li>rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1beta1, ClusterRole</li>
<li>rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1beta1, ClusterRoleBinding</li>
<li>rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1beta1, Role</li>
<li>rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1beta1, RoleBinding</li>
<li>scheduling.k8s.io/v1beta1, PriorityClass</li>
<li>storage.k8s.io/v1beta1, CSIDriver</li>
<li>storage.k8s.io/v1beta1, CSINode</li>
<li>storage.k8s.io/v1beta1, StorageClass</li>
<li>storage.k8s.io/v1beta1, VolumeAttachment</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>In Kubernetes 1.21, newly provisioned PersistentVolumes by gce-pd will use the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">topology.kubernetes.io/zone</code> GA label instead of the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone</code>
beta label.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_21_2021" data-text="May 21, 2021" tabindex="-1">May 21, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/network-policy-logging">Network Policy Logging</a> is generally available (GA).
Note that Network Policy Logging requires <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/dataplane-v2">Dataplane V2</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_20_2021" data-text="May 20, 2021" tabindex="-1">May 20, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.20 and later, audit logging does not occur for
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs/viewing-audit-logs#fail_open_events_in">Binary Authorization fail open events</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_19_2021" data-text="May 19, 2021" tabindex="-1">May 19, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2021-r17_version_updates" data-text="(2021-R17) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2021-R17) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p><strong>New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</strong></p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on the Kubernetes versioning scheme, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">Versioning</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">

the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>

<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.17.md#v11717" class="external">1.17.17-gke.8200</a> 
is now available.</li>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v11818" class="external">1.18.18-gke.1100</a> 
is now available.</li>

is now available.</li>

version 1.17 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v11817" class="external">1.18.17-gke.700</a> 
with this release.</li>

version 1.18 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v11817" class="external">1.18.17-gke.700</a> 
with this release.</li>
</ul></section>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>For GKE clusters running 1.18.18-gke.1200 or later, Ingress Controller only syncs NEGs that were created by the controller. Custom named NEGs that were created outside of the controller will no longer be synced.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_17_2021" data-text="May 17, 2021" tabindex="-1">May 17, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cluster-upgrade-notifications#upgradeavailable">UpgradeAvailableEvent</a>
notification is now generally available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="May_12_2021" data-text="May 12, 2021" tabindex="-1">May 12, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The Istio project recently <a href="https://istio.io/latest/news/security/" class="external">disclosed</a> a new security vulnerability (<a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-31920" class="external">CVE-2021-31920</a>) affecting <a href="https://cloud.google.com/learn/what-is-istio">Istio</a>.  For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2021-006">GCP-2021-006 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>In GKE version 1.20 and later, the GKE Gateway controller introduces the new <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gateway.networking.x-k8s.io</code> resource.
 This is similar but different from the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gateway.networking.istio.io</code> resource. This may cause the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl get 
gateway</code> command to return the incorrect Gateway resource unless the fully qualified resource name is used. To avoid
 seeing unexpected results when using kubectl, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/deploying-gateways#istio-gateways">Kubernetes Gateways and Istio Gateways</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/gateway-api">GKE Gateway controller</a>, Google Cloud&#39;s 
implementation of the <a href="https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/" class="external">Gateway API</a>, is available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a> in GKE version 1.20 and later. See <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/deploying-gateways">Deploying Gateways</a> for how to expose applications using Gateway.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/dataplane-v2">Dataplane V2</a> is generally available in newly created clusters using GKE versions 1.20.6-gke.700 and later.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="May_06_2021" data-text="May 06, 2021" tabindex="-1">May 06, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>The Envoy and Istio projects recently <a href="https://istio.io/latest/news/security/istio-security-2021-003" class="external">announced</a> several new security vulnerabilities ( <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-28683" class="external">CVE-2021-28683</a>, <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-28682" class="external">CVE-2021-28682</a>, and <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2021-29258" class="external">CVE-2021-29258</a>)  that could allow an attacker to crash Envoy.</p>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/anthos/clusters/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2021-004">GCP-2021-004 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now enable and configure <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/enable-oslogin">OS Login for private GKE clusters and nodes</a>.
This feature is enabled for private GKE clusters running node pool versions 1.20.5 or later.</p></div>
    </div>

    </div>
<h2 id="May_03_2021" data-text="May 03, 2021" tabindex="-1">May 03, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/nodes/#graceful-node-shutdown" class="external">kubelet graceful node shutdown feature</a> is now enabled on preemptible and GPU accelerator nodes running versions 1.20.5-gke.500 or later.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_29_2021" data-text="April 29, 2021" tabindex="-1">April 29, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>Fixes for the following GKE Autopilot clusters issues are rolling out to the Rapid release channel:</p>

<ul>
<li>Pods with a priority lower than -10 would not trigger scale up.</li>
<li>Pod anti-affinity might cause overscaling.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>For GKE clusters with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/creating-a-cluster-windows">Windows Server nodes</a>,
node names will now be limited to 15-characters to allow for Active Directory joining.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_27_2021" data-text="April 27, 2021" tabindex="-1">April 27, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gpus-multi">Multi-Instance GPU </a> on GKE is available in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages">Preview</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
