<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v11812" class="external">1.18.12-gke.1206</a> 
is now available in the Rapid channel.</li>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v1197" class="external">1.19.7-gke.800</a> 
is now available in the Rapid channel.</li>
<li>Version 1.19.6-gke.600 is no longer available in the Rapid channel.</li>
<li>Auto-upgrading nodes in the Rapid channel automatically upgrade from
version 1.19 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v1196" class="external">1.19.6-gke.1700</a> 
with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_28_2021" data-text="January 28, 2021" tabindex="-1">January 28, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p><em>2021-04-07 update:</em> Added a previously reported security bulletin to this releases note.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A vulnerability was recently discovered in the Linux utility <code translate="no" dir="ltr">sudo</code>, described in <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=2021-3156" class="external">CVE-2021-3156</a>, that may allow an attacker with unprivileged local shell access on a system with with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">sudo</code>installed to escalate their privileges to root on the system. GKE clusters are not affected by this vulnerability. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2021-001">GCP-2021-001 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>For clusters using a 1.19 version, with the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/node-images#cos-containerd">Container-Optimized OS with Containerd (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">cos_containerd</code>)</a>
node image,
<a href="https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/dockerd/" class="external"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">dockerd</code></a> 
(the Docker Daemon) is not running at boot. It needs to be started manually.
This issue will be fixed in a future release.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_25_2021" data-text="January 25, 2021" tabindex="-1">January 25, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2021-r3_version_updates" data-text="(2021-R3) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2021-R3) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<h5 id="new_versions_available_for_upgrades_and_new_clusters_7" data-text="New versions available for upgrades and new clusters" tabindex="-1">New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</h5>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on the Kubernetes versioning scheme, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">Versioning</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="no-channel_202" data-text="No channel" tabindex="-1">No channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.17.md#v11716" class="external">1.17.16-gke.1600</a> 
is now available.</li>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v11814" class="external">1.18.14-gke.1600</a> 
is now available.</li>
<li>Version 1.17.13-gke.2600 is no longer available.</li>
<li>Auto-upgrading nodes in the no channel automatically upgrade from version
1.17 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.17.md#v11714" class="external">1.17.14-gke.1600</a> 
with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="stable-channel_202" data-text="Stable channel" tabindex="-1">Stable channel</h3><p>There are no new releases in the Stable release channel.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="regular-channel_202" data-text="Regular channel" tabindex="-1">Regular channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.17.md#v11714" class="external">1.17.14-gke.1600</a> 
is now available in the Regular channel. This version is now the default.</li>
<li>Version 1.17.14-gke.400 is no longer available in the Regular channel.</li>
<li>Auto-upgrading nodes in the Regular channel automatically upgrade from
version 1.17 to version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.17.md#v11714" class="external">1.17.14-gke.1600</a> 
with this release.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="rapid-channel_202" data-text="Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Rapid channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#v1196" class="external">1.19.6-gke.1700</a> 
is now available in the Rapid channel.</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_22_2021" data-text="January 22, 2021" tabindex="-1">January 22, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The Ubuntu image for GKE 1.16 clusters is
now <a href="https://storage.googleapis.com/ubuntu-os-gke-cloud/ubuntu-gke-1804-1-16-v20201116.manifest">ubuntu-gke-1804-1-16-v20201116</a>.</p>

<p>This version includes the following improvements:</p>

<ul>
<li>USN-4627-1 CVEs is fixed</li>
<li>A patch for the GPU driver installer for Ubuntu with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">containerd</code></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Multidimensional Pod autoscaling is now available in beta in the Rapid release
channel. With this feature, you can use horizontal scaling based on CPU and
vertical scaling based on memory at the same time. To learn more, see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/multidimensional-pod-autoscaling">Configuring multidimensional Pod autoscaling</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>GKE will gradually begin using the
<a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/control-plane-node-communication/#konnectivity-service" class="external">Konnectivity service</a> for versions 1.19.4-gke.200 and later. Konnectivity replaces SSH
tunnels between the control plane and nodes with a more secure TCP proxy. The
change will first be introduced for non-private clusters.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Support for
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/legacy-stackdriver/logging">Legacy Logging</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/legacy-stackdriver/monitoring">Legacy Monitoring</a>
for GKE is extended to GKE versions 1.16 and 1.17.
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke">Cloud Operations for GKE</a>
remains the default configuration for GKE 1.16 and 1.17. Both
existing and new 1.16 and 1.17 clusters can use either of the two logging options.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_19_2021" data-text="January 19, 2021" tabindex="-1">January 19, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The widely used
<a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/" class="external">Ingress API</a> 
has graduated to general availability in Kubernetes 1.19. The v1beta1 Ingress
API is deprecated, and will no longer be served in 1.22+. Before 1.21,
identify and transition clients and manifests using the v1beta1 Ingress API to
use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">networking.k8s.io/v1</code>.</p>

<p>Clusters with Google Cloud&#39;s operations suite enabled can use the following
query to identify clients that access the Ingress v1beta1 APIs:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Objective-C" syntax-guessed><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-n">resource</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">type</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"k8s_cluster"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-n">resource</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">labels</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">cluster_name</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"$CLUSTER_NAME"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-n">protoPayload</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">authenticationInfo</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">principalEmail</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"system:serviceaccount"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">OR</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"@"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-n">protoPayload</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">request</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">apiVersion</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"extensions/v1beta1"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">OR</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"networking.k8s.io/v1beta1"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-n">protoPayload</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">request</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">kind</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"Ingress"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-n">NOT</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"kube-system"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
<p>Identify and transition clients and manifests using the v1beta1 Ingress APIs to
use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">networking.k8s.io/v1</code> before 1.21 is released on GKE
(approximately in June 2021), then verify no clients are using the v1beta1 API
during the 1.21 timeframe. Workloads using the v1beta1 APIs need to be upgraded
before your cluster is upgraded to GKE 1.22.</p>

<p>To migrate manifests to networking.k8s.io/v1:</p>

<ol>
<li>Rename the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">spec.backend</code> field (if specified) to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">spec.defaultBackend</code></li>
<li>Rename each <code translate="no" dir="ltr">backend.serviceName</code> field to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">backend.service.name</code></li>
<li>Rename each numeric <code translate="no" dir="ltr">backend.servicePort</code> field to
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">backend.service.port.number</code></li>
<li>Rename each string <code translate="no" dir="ltr">backend.servicePort</code> field to
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">backend.service.port.name</code></li>
<li>Specify a <code translate="no" dir="ltr">pathType</code> field for each defined path. Options are <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Prefix</code>,
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Exact</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ImplementationSpecific</code>. To match the undefined v1beta1
behavior, use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ImplementationSpecific</code>.</li>
</ol>

<p>As an example, to migrate this v1beta1 manifest to v1:</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="v1beta1-manifest" data-text="v1beta1 manifest" tabindex="-1">v1beta1 manifest</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="YAML"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">apiVersion</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">networking.k8s.io/v1beta1</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-nt">kind</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">Ingress</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-nt">metadata</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">name</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">example</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-nt">spec</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">backend</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">serviceName</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">default-backend</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">servicePort</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">80</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">rules</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p devsite-syntax-p-Indicator">-</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">http</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">paths</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p devsite-syntax-p-Indicator">-</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">path</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">/testpath</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">        </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">backend</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">          </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">serviceName</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">test</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">          </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">servicePort</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">80</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></section>
<section><h3 id="v1-manifest" data-text="v1 manifest" tabindex="-1">v1 manifest</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="YAML"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">apiVersion</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">networking.k8s.io/v1</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-nt">kind</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">Ingress</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-nt">metadata</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">name</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">example</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-nt">spec</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">defaultBackend</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">service</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">name</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">default-backend</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">port</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">        </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">number</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">80</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">rules</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p devsite-syntax-p-Indicator">-</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">http</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">paths</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">      </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p devsite-syntax-p-Indicator">-</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">path</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">/testpath</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">        </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">pathType</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">ImplementationSpecific</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">        </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">backend</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">          </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">service</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">            </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">name</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">test</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">            </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">port</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">              </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">number</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">80</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> This release note has been updated since it was originally published. The
update adds an authentication change with 1.19.</span></aside></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Seccomp (secure computing mode) support for Kubernetes has graduated to General
Availability (GA). This feature can be used to increase the workload security by
restricting the system calls for a Pod (applies to all containers) or individual
containers.</p>

<p>A new <code translate="no" dir="ltr">seccompProfile</code> field is added to Pod and Container securityContext
objects, starting in Kubernetes 1.19.</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="YAML"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">securityContext</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">seccompProfile</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-c1"># "Unconfined", "RuntimeDefault", or "Localhost"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">type</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">Localhost</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-c1"># only necessary if type == Localhost</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nt">localhostProfile</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-l devsite-syntax-l-Scalar devsite-syntax-l-Scalar-Plain">my-profiles/profile-allow.json</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
<p>The alpha seccomp annotations <code translate="no" dir="ltr">seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod</code> and
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/…</code>are deprecated in favor of the
GA API field. The alpha annotations will not be honored in Kubernetes 1.22+.</p>

<p>If you are currently using Seccomp annotations on Pods or Containers, you should
identify and transition workloads using the annotations to set the API fields
before 1.21 is released on GKE (approximately in June 2021). No
change on PodSecurityPolicy is required, as it supports
<a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/pod-security-policy/#seccomp" class="external">both annotation and field seccomp profiles</a>.
You can follow the recommended steps below:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Locate Seccomp annotation usages. In your Kubernetes manifest files, search
for &quot;seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod&quot; and
&quot;container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/&quot;&quot;.</p></li>
<li><p>Add or update securityContext fields. Based on your annotation usage, add or
update (if securityContext already exists) the securityContext field in Pod or
Container spec. The annotations can be left in place, but must match the
securityContext API field.</p>

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Current annotation usage</th>
<th>Add or update securityContext</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod</code></td>
<td>In Pod&#39;s securityContext, add seccompProfile field.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/<var translate="no">CONTAINER_NAME</var></code></td>
<td>In <var translate="no">CONTAINER_NAME</var>&#39;s securityContext, add seccompProfile field.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></li>
<li><p>Set values for seccompProfile. The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">type</code> field of seccompProfile corresponds
to the annotation value, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">localhostProfile</code> field corresponds to the path
following <code translate="no" dir="ltr">localhost</code> annotation value.</p>

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Current annotation value</th>
<th>seccompProfile value</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">unconfined</code></td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">seccompProfile:<br>
type: Unconfined</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">runtime/default</code><br>
or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">docker/default</code></td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">seccompProfile:<br>
type: RuntimeDefault</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">localhost/path/to/profile.json</code></td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">seccompProfile:<br>
type: Localhost<br>
localhostProfile: path/to/profile.json</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></li>
</ol>

<p>For more details, see the following pages:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tutorials/clusters/seccomp/" class="external">Restrict a Container&#39;s Syscalls with Seccomp</a> </li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/135-seccomp" class="external">Seccomp to GA</a> </li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/api-server-authentication#legacy-auth">Basic authentication with a password</a>
has been removed in Kubernetes 1.19. Clusters upgraded to 1.19 can no longer use
basic authentication to authenticate users to the control plane.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="2021-r2_version_updates" data-text="(2021-R2) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(2021-R2) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<h5 id="new_versions_available_for_upgrades_and_new_clusters_8" data-text="New versions available for upgrades and new clusters" tabindex="-1">New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</h5>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The CertificateSigningRequest API has graduated to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">certificates.k8s.io/v1</code> in
Kubernetes 1.19. The v1beta1 CertificateSigningRequest API is deprecated and
will no longer be served in 1.22+.</p>

<p>Clusters with Google Cloud&#39;s operations suite enabled can use the following
query to identify clients that access the CertificateSigningRequest v1beta1
APIs:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Objective-C" syntax-guessed><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-n">resource</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">type</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"k8s_cluster"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-n">resource</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">labels</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">cluster_name</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"$CLUSTER_NAME"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-n">protoPayload</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">authenticationInfo</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">principalEmail</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"system:serviceaccount"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">OR</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"@"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-n">protoPayload</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">request</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">apiVersion</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"certificates.k8s.io/v1beta1"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-n">NOT</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s">"kube-system"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code>
<p>Identify and transition clients and manifests using the v1beta1
CertificateSigningRequest API to use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">certificates.k8s.io/v1</code> before 1.21 is
released on GKE (approximately in June 2021), then verifying no
clients are using the v1beta1 API during the 1.21 timeframe. Workloads using
the v1beta1 API need to be upgraded before your cluster is upgraded to
GKE 1.22.</p>

<p>Differences between the v1beta1 and v1 API are as follows:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>For API clients requesting certificates:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/certificate-signing-requests/#kubernetes-signers" class="external">spec.signerName</a> 
is now required, and requests for <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io/legacy-unknown</code> are not
allowed to be created using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">certificates.k8s.io/v1</code> API</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">spec.usages</code> is now required, cannot contain duplicate values,
and must only contain known usages</li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>For API clients approving or signing certificates:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">status.conditions</code> cannot contain duplicate types</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">status.conditions[*].status</code> is now required</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">status.certificate</code> must be PEM-encoded, and must contain only
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">CERTIFICATE</code> blocks</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="119_available_in_the_rapid_channel" data-text="1.19 available in the Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">1.19 available in the Rapid channel</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.19 is now available in Rapid channel. Before upgrading to
1.19.6-gke.600, read
<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md" class="external">Kubernetes 1.19 Release Notes</a> 
especially the
<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.19.md#urgent-upgrade-notes" class="external">Urgent upgrade notes</a> 
section.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_11_2021" data-text="January 11, 2021" tabindex="-1">January 11, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/gce-pd-csi-driver">Compute Engine persistent disk Container Storage Interface (CSI)
Driver</a>
is now generally available in GKE. It allows you to take advantage of the latest
persistent disk features without having to manually manage the CSI driver
lifecycle.</p>

<p>For newly created clusters, the Compute Engine persistent disk CSI Driver is
installed by default for the following cluster versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.18.10-gke.2101 and later</li>
<li>1.19.3-gke.2100 and later</li>
</ul>

<p>For all clusters, PersistentVolumeClaims created without specifying a
StorageClass will continue to trigger volume provisioning using the in-tree
gcePersistentDisk volume plugin. Only StorageClasses that reference the
provisioner name <code translate="no" dir="ltr">pd.csi.storage.gke.io</code> will provision using the CSI driver. For
details, refer to
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/gce-pd-csi-driver">Using the Compute Engine persistent disk CSI Driver</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>In all GKE versions 1.14 or later, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke">Google Cloud&#39;s operations suite for GKE</a>
adds two new options for configuring which logs and metrics are collected:</p>

<ol>
<li>System and workload logging only (Monitoring disabled).</li>
<li>System monitoring only (Logging disabled).</li>
</ol></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_08_2021" data-text="January 08, 2021" tabindex="-1">January 08, 2021</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> This release note has been updated since it was originally published. The
update removes 1.18 from the Regular channel and no channel.</span></aside></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p><span id="known-20210108">W</span>e have discovered an issue with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/ingress-ilb">Internal Ingress</a>
on GKE that may require your action <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balance-ingress#https_between_client_and_load_balancer">if you have HTTPS enabled</a> (either through pre-shared
certificates or Kubernetes Secrets). This issue does not affect
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/ingress-xlb">External Ingress</a>
resources or <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/ingress-for-anthos">MultiClusterIngress</a>
resources.</p>

<p><strong>What do I need to know?</strong></p>

<p>For internal Ingress on GKE versions 1.17.x and earlier, there is a known issue
concerning SSL Certificate Updates on internal Ingress resources. Updating the
certificate is not possible for pre-shared or Secrets-based certificates (which
includes Kubernetes certificate managers). Updates to existing certificates on
internal Ingress resources will not complete if attempting to update the Ingress
resource.</p>

<p>In order to replace the certificate on an existing Ingress, the Ingress must be
deleted and re-deployed. Manual updates using the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud compute target-https-proxies update</code> allow a certificate to be updated
on an existing Ingress without recreation, but any manual updates are
overwritten by the Ingress controller if the Ingress is updated again.</p>

<p><strong>What do I need to do?</strong></p>

<p>If you intend to update your TLS Spec or Pre-shared Cert Spec on your
Internal Ingress, you must do so by <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balance-ingress#delete">deleting your Ingress</a>
and recreating it as soon as possible, until you are able to upgrade to a
patched version. Versions 1.16 are expected to be patched this month.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

<h2 id="December_17_2020" data-text="December 17, 2020" tabindex="-1">December 17, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balance-ingress">Internal Ingress</a>
for Internal HTTP(S) Load Balancing is now GA for
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ingress-features">1.17.13-gke.2600+ and 1.18.10-gke.800+</a>.
Note that the <a href="#November_13_2020">certificate update issue</a> is now patched
in these GA versions. Internal Ingress for GKE 1.16 will be patched in an
upcoming release.</p></div>

      <div><p>When using <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/local-ssd#creating_a_node_pool_using_ephemeral_storage_on_local_ssds">ephemeral storage on local SSDs</a>, reserved space is now calculated from the number of SSDs, instead of the size of

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>With the release of GKE node version 1.19, the Container-Optimized OS with
Docker (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">cos</code>) variant is deprecated. Please migrate to the Container-Optimized
OS with Containerd (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">cos_containerd</code>) variant, which is now the default GKE node
image. For instructions, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/using-containerd">Containerd images</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>You can now use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks#disk-types">balanced persistent disks</a>
(<code translate="no" dir="ltr">pd-balanced</code>) as a GKE node boot disk type. You create node pools with
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">pd-balanced</code> boot disks using the Cloud SDK and Google Cloud API.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="#September_28_2020">issue</a> from September 28, 2020 with Container Threat
Detection on GKE 1.18 is resolved in GKE versions 1.18.9-gke.1300 and
later and 1.19.2-gke.2000 and later.</p></div>
    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">

<h2 id="November_13_2020" data-text="November 13, 2020" tabindex="-1">November 13, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ingress-features#ssl">SSL policies</a>
for GKE external Ingress for 1.17.6-gke.11+ are now generally available. SSL
policies allow you to specify a set of TLS versions and ciphers that the load
balancer uses to terminate HTTPS traffic from clients.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ingress-features#direct_health">Custom health checks</a>
across all Ingress types for 1.17.12-gke.500+ are now generally available. With
custom health checks, you specify parameters in a Kubernetes BackendConfig.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balance-ingress#static_ip_addressing">Static IP addressing for internal Ingress</a>
is now in beta.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ingress-features#https_redirect">HTTPS redirects for Ingress</a>
are now in beta. An external HTTP load balancer can redirect unencrypted HTTP
requests to an HTTPS load balancer that uses the same IP address.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>For internal Ingress on GKE versions earlier than 1.18.10-gke.600 there is a
known issue concerning SSL Certificate Updates on internal Ingress resources.
Updating the certificate is not possible for pre-shared or Secrets-based
certificates (which includes Kubernetes certificate managers). In order to
replace the certificate on an existing Ingress, the Ingress must be deleted and
re-deployed. Manual updates using the gcloud compute target-https-proxies update
allow a certificate to be updated, but any manual updates are overwritten by the
Ingress controller if the Ingress is updated again.</p>

<p>The GKE release notes will be updated when the patch is available.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now specify <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/standalone-neg#naming_negs">custom network endpoint group (NEG) names</a>.
This feature is in beta.</p></div>
    </div>

      <div><p>New clusters created with the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">v1alpha1</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">v1beta1</code> APIs install the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gce-pd-csi-driver">Compute Engine persistent disk Container Storage Interface</a>

<h2 id="November_06_2020" data-text="November 06, 2020" tabindex="-1">November 06, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Node pools running GKE 1.18 and higher can now be configured to use local SSD
for ephemeral storage with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">emptyDir</code> volumes. For more information, see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes/local-ssd">Using local SSDs</a>.
This feature is in beta.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="November_04_2020" data-text="November 04, 2020" tabindex="-1">November 04, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Support for Legacy <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/legacy-stackdriver/logging">Logging</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/gke/legacy-stackdriver/monitoring">Monitoring</a>
for Google Kubernetes Engine is extended to GKE 1.15. Google Cloud&#39;s operations
suite remains the default configuration for GKE 1.15. Both existing and new GKE
1.15 clusters can use either of the two logging options.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="October_19_2020" data-text="October 19, 2020" tabindex="-1">October 19, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>A fix for the issue reported on <a href="#September_16_2020">September 16, 2020</a> where
custom resources in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">istio-system</code> namespace were deleted when upgrading
from GKE 1.16 to 1.17 and 1.18 is now available.</p>

<p>Upgrade to one of the following unaffected versions to avoid having to manually
recreate these resources:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.17.12-gke.1501 and higher</li>
<li>1.18.9-gke.1501 and higher</li>
</ul>

<p>The issue only occurs during upgrades, so new clusters created in earlier
versions are unaffected.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_16_2020" data-text="October 16, 2020" tabindex="-1">October 16, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p><span id="known-20201016">T</span>here is a known issue impacting both LTSC and SAC Windows Server images on GKE
versions 1.17.x and 1.18.x. New Windows nodes take longer to join the cluster
which may cause node pool creation, auto-scaling, and auto-repair operations to
time out.</p>

<p>We recommend not upgrading clusters with Windows Server nodes pools to the
following versions:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.17.12-gke.1501</li>
<li>1.18.9-gke.1501</li>
</ul>

<p>GKE versions beyond the affected versions will not have the startup time
regression. Upgrade to versions greater than 1.17.12-gke.1501 and 1.18.9-
gke.1501 when they become available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="October_12_2020" data-text="October 12, 2020" tabindex="-1">October 12, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>A new <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/creating-a-cluster-windows#version_mapping">Windows node image version</a>
that fixes <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2020-1472" class="external">CVE-2020-1472</a> 
is now available. For more information, see the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/support/bulletins#gcp-2020-013-impact">GCP-2020-013 security bulletin.</a></p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="October_06_2020" data-text="October 06, 2020" tabindex="-1">October 06, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p><span id="known-20201006">T</span>here is a known issue with the upgrade from GKE 1.16 to 1.17. Any custom
resources you created in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">istio-system</code> namespace are deleted during an
upgrade to 1.17. These resources must be manually recreated. We recommend not
upgrading clusters with the Istio addon to 1.17 until the fix is rolled out. The
issue only occurs during upgrades, so new clusters are not affected.</p>

<p>The fix was not included in release R31 as <a href="#September_16_2020">previously reported</a>.</p></div>
    </div>

the scheduler name in the Pod spec is set to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gke.io/optimize-utilization-scheduler</code>.</p></div>

      <div><p>For clusters not using Legacy Logging and Monitoring, upgrades from 1.14 to 1.15

announced in <a href="#september_3_2020">R29</a>.</p></div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> This release note has been updated since it was originally published. The
update adds additional information about a known issue with Istio on GKE.</span></aside></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-auto-provisioning">Node Auto-Provisioning</a>
now lets you set default values for the following features:</p>

<ul>
<li>Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK)</li>
<li>Secure Boot and Integrity Monitoring</li>
<li>Boot disk type and size</li>
</ul>

<p>The default value will be used by all newly created node pools.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p><span id="known-20200925">If</span> you have the Istio on GKE add-on enabled on a cluster, there is a known issue
with the upgrade from GKE 1.16 to 1.17 versions lower than 1.17.9-gke.6300 (R30
or earlier). Any custom resources you created in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">istio-system</code> namespace
are deleted during an upgrade to 1.17 (R30 or earlier). These resources must be
manually recreated. We recommend that Istio on GKE users upgrade only to R31 or
a later version that doesn&#39;t have the issue. The issue only occurs during
upgrades, so new clusters are not affected.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><p>We expect the following changes in the coming weeks. This information is not a
guarantee, but is provided to help you plan for upcoming changes.</p>

<p>GKE will gradually upgrade clusters&#39; control planes only to Kubernetes 1.16,
<strong>beginning on or after October 6, 2020</strong>.</p>

<p>Node pools <strong>will not be auto-upgraded to 1.16 at this time</strong>, but can be
manually upgraded completing the following instructions.</p>

<p>Once rolled out, 1.16 will become the most mature control plane version in the
Kubernetes fleet, with newer versions available on the Rapid and Regular
channels. In turn, older control plane versions will be deprecated and
eventually removed from the fleet. Periodically deprecating and eventually
removing beta APIs is part of a standard process to ensure that all Kubernetes
fleets evolve and all APIs continue to be up-to-date.</p>

<p>More information is available in the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/apis-1-16">GKE documentation</a>
and <a href="https://kubernetes.io/blog/2019/07/18/api-deprecations-in-1-16/" class="external">from the Kubernetes project</a>.</p>

<h4 id="what_do_i_need_to_do" data-text="What do I need to do?" tabindex="-1">What do I need to do?</h4>

<ol>
<li><strong>Test and qualify 1.16 in a pre-production environment.</strong> We highly
recommend testing upgrades in a staging or testing environment before
rolling them out to production.</li>
<li><strong>Migrate to use the current API versions before your clusters are upgraded
to Kubernetes 1.16</strong> to ensure your API clients and resource manifests can
access and update API resources without interruption.</li>
</ol>

<p><strong>You can manually upgrade node pools to 1.16:</strong></p>

<ul>
<li>The same method is available for <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-auto-upgrades">auto-upgrade enabled clusters</a>
as GKE will not automatically upgrade node pools to 1.16 at this time.</li>
</ul>

<p>If you are concerned about disruption, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-upgrades#maintenance-window">use maintenance windows and exclusions to control when the upgrade will occur</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_16_2020" data-text="September 16, 2020" tabindex="-1">September 16, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>If you have the Istio on GKE add-on enabled on a cluster, there is a known issue
with the upgrade from GKE 1.16 to 1.17. Any custom resources you created in the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">istio-system</code> namespace are deleted during an upgrade to 1.17 (R30 or earlier).
These resources must be manually recreated. We recommend that Istio on GKE users
do not upgrade to GKE 1.17 until a patch release fixes the issue. The fix will
be rolled out in GKE release R31.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="September_14_2020" data-text="September 14, 2020" tabindex="-1">September 14, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A vulnerability was recently discovered in the Linux kernel, described in
<a href="https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2020/09/03/3" class="external">CVE-2020-14386</a>,
that may allow container escape to obtain root privileges on the host node. All
GKE nodes are affected. For more information, see the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2020-012">GCP-2020-012 security bulletin</a>.</p>

<p>A fix is available in all versions included in this release.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="r291_version_updates" data-text="(R29.1) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(R29.1) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<h5 id="new_versions_available_for_upgrades_and_new_clusters_3" data-text="New versions available for upgrades and new clusters" tabindex="-1">New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</h5>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on the Kubernetes versioning scheme, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">Versioning</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="no-channel_217" data-text="No channel" tabindex="-1">No channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li><p>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.14.md#v11410" class="external">1.14.10-gke.50</a> 
is now available.</p></li>
<li><p>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.15.md#v11512" class="external">1.15.12-gke.20</a> 
is now available.</p></li>
<li><p>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.16.md#v11613" class="external">1.16.13-gke.401</a> 
is now available.</p></li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="stable-channel_217" data-text="Stable channel" tabindex="-1">Stable channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.16.md#v11613" class="external">1.16.13-gke.401</a> 
is now available in the Stable channel.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="regular-channel_217" data-text="Regular channel" tabindex="-1">Regular channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.16.md#v11613" class="external">1.16.13-gke.401</a> 
is now available in the Regular channel.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="rapid-channel_217" data-text="Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Rapid channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.17.md#v1179" class="external">1.17.9-gke.1504</a> 
is now available in the Rapid channel. This version is now the default.</li>
</ul>

<p><div class="release-issue"> There is a known issue that prevents creating
Rapid channel clusters on 1.18. To create a cluster on the Rapid channel,
create a Rapid channel cluster on 1.17, and then manually upgrade to 1.18.</p></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_08_2020" data-text="September 08, 2020" tabindex="-1">September 08, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>GKE clusters in the ERROR state will be automatically deleted.</p>

<p>This change applies to all GKE versions.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p><span id="known-20200908">W</span>hile the Kubernetes API does support the use of the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ingressClassName</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">ingressClass</code> resources, the Compute Engine ingress controller does not.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>GKE now allows clusters of up to 15,000 nodes when using GKE 1.18. To scale a
cluster beyond 5,000 nodes, you must contact support to raise your quota.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p>Cluster Autoscaler for GKE 1.18 could have problems with very large clusters or
scale ups where there are over 5,000 nodes in the cluster or over 1,000 nodes
being added at the same time. A fix is coming soon.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Consumers of the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">certificatesigningrequests/approval</code> API must now have
permission to approve certificate signing requests (CSRs) for the specific
signer requested by the CSR. More information on the new <code translate="no" dir="ltr">signerName</code> field and
the required authorization can be found in the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/certificate-signing-requests/#authorization">CSR documentation</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> This release note has been updated since it was originally published. The
update adds additional information about changes to Shielded Nodes.</span></aside></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="kubernetes_118_available_on_gke" data-text="Kubernetes 1.18 available on GKE" tabindex="-1">Kubernetes 1.18 available on GKE</h4>

<p>Kubernetes 1.18 is now available in the Rapid channel. See the
<a href="https://v1-18.docs.kubernetes.io/docs/setup/release/notes/#what-s-new-major-themes" class="external">Kubernetes 1.18 release notes</a>.
In particular, see the
<a href="https://v1-18.docs.kubernetes.io/docs/setup/release/notes/#urgent-upgrade-notes" class="external">Urgent Upgrade Notes</a> 
before upgrading to 1.18.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>In GKE 1.18, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/shielded-gke-nodes">Shielded Nodes</a>
are enabled by default for newly created clusters. Clusters upgrading to 1.18
are unaffected by this change.</p>

<p>Shielded Nodes are only compatible with Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu
images. If you are using a custom image or Windows images you should disable
Shielded Nodes.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/taint-and-toleration/#taint-based-evictions">TaintBasedEvictions</a>
are generally available in GKE in 1.18 clusters.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="September_03_2020" data-text="September 03, 2020" tabindex="-1">September 03, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="r29_version_updates" data-text="(R29) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(R29) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on the Kubernetes versioning scheme, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">Versioning</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">

the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.15.md#v11512" class="external">1.15.12-gke.17</a> 
is now available.</li>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.16.md#v11613" class="external">1.16.13-gke.400</a> 
is now available.</li>
<li>Auto-upgrading nodes upgrade from version 1.14 to version 1.15.12-gke.2
during this release if they have not already done so.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="stable-channel_218" data-text="Stable channel" tabindex="-1">Stable channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across

<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.16.md#v11613" class="external">1.16.13-gke.1</a> 
is now available in the Stable channel.</li>
<li>Version 1.15.12-gke.9 is no longer available in the Stable channel.</li>
</ul>

<h6 id="coming_soon" data-text="Coming soon" tabindex="-1">Coming soon</h6>

<p>Google Kubernetes Engine will begin gradually upgrading clusters in the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/release-channels">Stable channel</a>
to GKE 1.16 in an upcoming release. To read about API deprecations in 1.16,
see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/apis-1-16">Kubernetes 1.16 deprecated APIs</a>.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="regular-channel_218" data-text="Regular channel" tabindex="-1">Regular channel</h3><p>There are no version changes in the Regular channel in this release.</p></section>

the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.18.md#v1186" class="external">1.18.6-gke.3503</a> 
is now available in the Rapid channel.</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_28_2020" data-text="August 28, 2020" tabindex="-1">August 28, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/private-clusters#master-global-access">Master global access for private clusters</a>
is now generally available. With master global access, you can access the
master&#39;s private endpoint from any Google Cloud region or on-premises
environment no matter what the private cluster&#39;s region is.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><p>We expect the following changes in the coming weeks. This information is not a
guarantee, but is provided to help you plan for upcoming changes.</p>

<p>Google Kubernetes Engine will begin gradually upgrading clusters in the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/release-channels">Stable channel</a>
to GKE 1.16 in an upcoming release. To read about API deprecations in 1.16, see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/apis-1-16">Kubernetes 1.16 deprecated APIs</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_27_2020" data-text="August 27, 2020" tabindex="-1">August 27, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="r28_version_updates" data-text="(R28) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(R28) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<h5 id="new_versions_available_for_upgrades_and_new_clusters_5" data-text="New versions available for upgrades and new clusters" tabindex="-1">New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</h5>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on the Kubernetes versioning scheme, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">Versioning</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">

the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Auto-upgrading nodes begin upgrading from version 1.14 to version
1.15.12-gke.2 in this release. The auto-upgrades will continue gradually
over the course of several releases.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="stable-channel_219" data-text="Stable channel" tabindex="-1">Stable channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Auto-upgrading nodes in the Stable channel continue upgrading from version
1.14 to 1.15.12-gke.2 during this release. All auto-upgrading nodes that
have not yet upgraded to 1.15.12-gke.2 will upgrade during the R28 rollout.</li>
</ul></section>
<section><h3 id="regular-channel_219" data-text="Regular channel" tabindex="-1">Regular channel</h3><p>There are no version changes in the Regular channel in this release.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="rapid-channel_219" data-text="Rapid channel" tabindex="-1">Rapid channel</h3><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li>Version 1.17.9-gke.1703 is no longer available.</li>
</ul></section>
</div>
<h5 id="versions_no_longer_available" data-text="Versions no longer available" tabindex="-1">Versions no longer available</h5>

<p>The following versions are no longer available for new clusters or cluster
upgrades:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.14</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_21_2020" data-text="August 21, 2020" tabindex="-1">August 21, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>In some cases, certain networking kernel sysctls which were previously set to
static defaults are now calculated dynamically based upon machine size. The
networking sysctls affected include:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">net.ipv4.tcp_mem</code></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">net.ipv4.tcp_max_tw_buckets</code></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">net.ipv4.udp_mem</code></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">net.ipv4.tcp_max_orphans</code></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog</code></li>
</ul>

<p>The issue has been fixed in GKE 1.17 in versions 1.17.6-gke.7 and later and in
1.16 in 1.16.13-gke.1 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The use of <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/alias-ips#enable_reserved_ip_ranges">private IP address ranges outside of the RFC 1918 ranges</a> is now generally
available. These addresses can be used for master nodes, nodes, Pods, and
Services.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors#error_codes">Google canonical error codes</a>
are now available in beta. GKE operations now use the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors#error_model">canonical error model</a>
to report errors.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>OpenID Connect Discovery Documents are now published for all clusters, which
allows you to configure other software to understand the service account tokens
issued by GKE clusters. For more information, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/reference/rest/v1beta1/projects.locations.clusters.well-known/getOpenid-configuration">getOpenid-configuration</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/reference/rest/v1beta1/projects.locations.clusters/getJwks">getJwks</a>
in the API reference documentation.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/network-policy-logging">Network policy logging</a>
is now available in beta. Network policy logging requires a cluster with
Dataplane V2.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balancing#global_access">Global access</a>
and <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balancing#lb_subnet">configurable subnets</a>
for the internal load balancer Service are now generally available for
GKE 1.17.9-gke.600 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balancing">internal load balancer Service</a>
type is now generally available for GKE 1.17.9-gke.600 and later.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/dataplane-v2">Dataplane V2</a>
is now available in beta in newly created clusters using GKE versions
1.17.9-gke.600 and later or 1.18 and later. See
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/containers-kubernetes/bringing-ebpf-and-cilium-to-google-kubernetes-engine">New GKE Dataplane V2 increases security and visibility for containers</a>
on the Google Cloud Blog for more details.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_20_2020" data-text="August 20, 2020" tabindex="-1">August 20, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

is now available in the Rapid channel.</li>
<li>Version <a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.17.md#v1179" class="external">1.17.9-gke.1503</a> 
is now available in the Rapid channel. This version is now the default.</li>
<li>Version 1.17.9-gke.600 is no longer available.</li>
</ul></section>
</div></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="August_06_2020" data-text="August 06, 2020" tabindex="-1">August 06, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="r26_version_updates" data-text="(R26) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(R26) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

<h5 id="scheduled_automatic_upgrades" data-text="Scheduled automatic upgrades" tabindex="-1">Scheduled automatic upgrades</h5>

<p>Masters and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded:</p>

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Current version</th>
<th>Upgrade version</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td>1.14</td>
<td>1.15.12-gke.2</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.15.12-gke.3</td>
<td>1.15.12-gke.9</td>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="change_default_machine_type_to_e2" data-text="Change default machine type to E2" tabindex="-1">Change default machine type to E2</h4>

<p>GKE is changing the default machine type for new clusters and node pools from
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">n1-standard-1</code> to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-medium</code>. This change impacts new node pools created using
versions 1.17.6 and higher. If you do not specify a machine type during your
cluster or node pool creation workflow from node pool version 1.17.6 onwards,
the newly provisioned clusters and node pools will default to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-medium</code> VMs.
Note that this change does not impact your existing node pools that are
auto-upgraded or manually upgraded to version 1.17.6 or higher.</p>

<p>E2 machine types do not support GPUs, local SSDs or sole tenancy. As such,
you will receive an error message advising you to specify a compatible machine
type for your workloads if you:</p>

<ul>
<li>Use node pool version 1.17.6+ to provision new worker nodes using the
default machine type with either GPUs, local SSDs or Sole tenancy enabled
(for example, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud container clusters create mycluster --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-v100, count=2)</code>,
or</li>
<li>Use scripts that provision GPUs or local SSDs and do not specify a specific
machine type. Furthermore, these scripts will not work until you specify
your desired compatible machine type.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>What do I need to do?</strong></p>

<p>Use the following interface(s) of your choice to explicitly configure your
machine type setting for newly provisioned machines to be anything other than
the new <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-medium</code> default:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gcloud</code>
<ul>
<li>Specify <a href="https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/container/clusters/create#--machine-type"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">--machine-type</code></a></li>
</ul></li>
<li>API
<ul>
<li>Specify <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/reference/rest/v1/NodeConfig"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">machineType</code> in NodeConfig</a></li>
</ul></li>
<li>Cloud Console
<ul>
<li>Specify <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-pools">machine type in for node pools</a></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>Terraform</p>

<ul>
<li>Specify <a href="https://www.terraform.io/docs/providers/google/r/container_cluster.html#machine_type" class="external"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">machine_type</code> in <code translate="no" dir="ltr">node_config</code></a> </li>
<li><p>Specify <a href="https://registry.terraform.io/modules/terraform-google-modules/kubernetes-engine/google/9.2.0#node_pools-variable"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">machine_type</code> for <code translate="no" dir="ltr">node_pools</code></a>
in the <a href="https://registry.terraform.io/modules/terraform-google-modules/kubernetes-engine/google/9.2.0#node_pools-variable" class="external"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">module &quot;gke&quot;</code> section of your Terraform configuration code</a>.</p>

<p>We strongly recommend explicitly setting the machine type to
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">n1-standard-1</code> or any other suitable VM type if one or more of these
situations apply to you: You are concerned about your single threaded
application&#39;s performance on the new shared-core <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-medium</code> default
machine type. You use GPUs or local SSDs or sole tenancy, all of which
are unsupported by the new default machine type <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-medium</code>.</p></li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>GKE nodes now have the label <code translate="no" dir="ltr">cloud.google.com/machine-family</code> applied. The
value of this label is the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/machine-types#general_purpose">Compute Engine instance family</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_22_2020" data-text="July 22, 2020" tabindex="-1">July 22, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-breaking">Breaking</span>
      <div><p>Starting September 1, 2020, we will automatically delete Google Kubernetes
Engine (GKE) clusters that have ERROR status.</p>

<h4 id="what_do_i_need_to_know" data-text="What do I need to know?" tabindex="-1">What do I need to know?</h4>

<p>GKE clusters might end up with ERROR status (red exclamation mark in the cluster
status page) in rare cases when cluster creation or deletion operation
encounters an unexpected error. Previously, such clusters remained in your
accounts and could have been partially usable. ERROR status clusters are
excluded from the GKE cluster management fee.</p>

<p>Starting September 1, 2020, we will begin blocking access to such ERROR status
clusters and deleting them automatically.</p>

<h4 id="what_do_i_need_to_do_2" data-text="What do I need to do?" tabindex="-1">What do I need to do?</h4>

<p>If you are relying on any of the clusters with ERROR status in your projects,
stop using them by September 1, 2020.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><p>We expect the following changes in the coming weeks. This information is not a
guarantee, but is provided to help you plan for upcoming changes.</p>

<ul>
<li>In the next release (R25), GKE will begin to upgrade nodes in clusters on
the <strong>Stable channel</strong> to 1.15.12-gke.2. Upgrades will proceed gradually
over several GKE releases.</li>
<li>In the next release (R25), GKE will begin to upgrade nodes in clusters on
the <strong>Regular channel</strong> to 1.16.11-gke.5. Upgrades will proceed gradually
over several GKE releases.</li>
<li>In the next release (R25), GKE will begin to upgrade nodes in 1.16 clusters
not on a release channel to 1.16.9-gke.5. Upgrades will proceed gradually
over several GKE releases.</li>
<li>GKE version 1.14 will be deprecated in R26.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-security">Security</span>
      <div><p>A privilege escalation vulnerability was recently discovered in Kubernetes. This
vulnerability allows an attacker that has already compromised a node to execute
a command in any Pod in the cluster. For more information, see the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/security-bulletins#gcp-2020-009">GCP-2020-009 security bulletin</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
