<h2 id="July_17_2020" data-text="July 17, 2020" tabindex="-1">July 17, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>The Kubernetes Engine Monitoring feature has been renamed in the Google Cloud
Console and documentation to Cloud Operations for GKE. No functional changes
were made with this change. Enabling Cloud Operations for GKE continues to
collect logs and metrics for your cluster and workloads as it did before.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The BackendConfig CRD is now GA in GKE 1.16-gke.3+ clusters which promotes most
BackendConfig features (IAP, timeouts, affinity, user-defined request headers,
and so on) to GA across internal, external, and multi-cluster Ingress. See
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ingress-features">Ingress Features</a>
for detail on explicit version support.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Container-native Ingress using Network Endpoint Groups (NEGs) is now default
(with some exceptions) for new Services deployed in GKE 1.17.6-gke.7+ clusters.
The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">cloud.google.com/neg: &#39;{&quot;ingress&quot;: true}&#39;</code> annotation will be automatically
applied to any Services deployed in these clusters without any explicit action
from users to enable container-native Ingress.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Up to 50 TCP/UDP ports are supported per internal TCP/UDP load balancer IP when
deploying through <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balancing#shared_VIP">GKE Services with shared IP addresses</a>.
This also permits multi-protocol TCP and UDP support for the same Service IP.
Shared IP is now available in Beta for all existing GKE versions.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>Customer Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) are now generally available for GKE.
CMEK for GKE lets you secure your node boot disks as well as attached persistent
storage by encrypting the data encryption keys that encrypt your data. To learn
more, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/using-cmek">Using customer-managed encryption keys</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>SSL Policies which allow policy-enforced TLS and cipher settings are available
in Beta for external Ingress and multi-cluster Ingress. Custom health checks,
which allow users to declaratively customize parameters of the load balancer
health check, are also now available for external, internal, and multi-cluster
Ingress. For feature support status and version compatibility see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/ingress-features">Ingress Features</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p><span id="known-202010717">If</span> you have node pools with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubernetes.io</code> or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">k8s.io</code> labels and want to
upgrade to 1.16, you must remove the labels before upgrading.</p>

<p>For more information on this change, see the Kubernetes
<a href="https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/279-limit-node-access#bounding-self-labeling-kubelets" class="external">Node Restriction</a> 
enhancement.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_13_2020" data-text="July 13, 2020" tabindex="-1">July 13, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>A bug in gVisor has been fixed. Default gVisor node labels are now applied when
user-specified labels.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="r23_version_updates" data-text="(R23) Version updates" tabindex="-1">(R23) Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>

opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more

all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>

is now available in the Rapid channel.</li>

    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Beginning with this release, GKE releases also include a release number to
reference changes. This release is R23 for 2020.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> The format of release numbers may change in the future.</span></aside></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><p>We expect the following changes in the coming weeks. This information is not a
guarantee, but is provided to help you plan for upcoming changes.</p>

<ul>
<li>In the next release (R24), GKE will begin to upgrade control planes in
clusters on the <strong>Stable channel</strong> to 1.15.12-gke.2. Upgrades will proceed
gradually over several GKE releases.</li>
<li>In an upcoming release, GKE will begin to upgrade nodes in clusters on the
<strong>Stable channel</strong> to 1.15.12-gke.2. Upgrades will proceed gradually over
several GKE releases.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="July_02_2020" data-text="July 02, 2020" tabindex="-1">July 02, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/beta/container/node-pools/create#--system-config-from-file">GKE Node System Configuration</a>
is now beta. With this feature you can specify custom configurations for Kubelet
and Kernel settings on your node pools.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/nodelocal-dns-cache">NodeLocal DNSCache</a>
is now generally available.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>Starting with GKE 1.17.6, <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/verticalpodautoscaler">Vertical Pod Autoscaler</a> recommendations are more fine-grained, starting from 1 mCPU and 1 MiB.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="June_24_2020" data-text="June 24, 2020" tabindex="-1">June 24, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p><span id="known-2020624">T</span>here is a known that may cause multiple Pods on the same node to be allocated
with the same IPv4 address leading to possible service disruption. We will
automatically upgrade your cluster master to the next available patch version
which will include a fix to the issue.</p>

<h4 id="what_do_i_need_to_know" data-text="What do I need to know?" tabindex="-1">What do I need to know?</h4>

<ul>
<li>Ensure your cluster(s) are subscribed to a <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/release-channels">release channel</a>,
or you have <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-auto-upgrades">node auto-upgrade</a>
enabled. If so, your cluster(s) will be automatically upgraded as described
below.</li>
<li>If you are experiencing any issues or do not want to use auto-upgrade you
can manually initiate an upgrade at your earliest convenience.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="what_do_i_need_to_do" data-text="What do I need to do?" tabindex="-1">What do I need to do?</h4>

<p><strong>If you are experiencing issues and wish to update proactively:</strong></p>

<ul>
<li>Follow the steps in the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/upgrading-a-cluster">Manually upgrading a cluster</a>
page to upgrade the cluster master.</li>
<li>Upgrade your node pool by applying the latest patch available for your node
version.</li>
<li>Consider using <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-upgrades#surge">surge upgrade</a>
for your nodepool upgrade. Surge upgrade allows you to set the number of
additional nodes to be created temporarily for the upgrade process which the
disruption to running workloads.</li>
<li>Use the following table to determine which patch version is applicable for
your cluster(s):</li>
</ul>

<table>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>Channel</th>
<th>Action required</th>
<th>Upgrade target</th>
<th>Date available</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2">No channel</td>
<td rowspan="2">Upgrade to the recommended patch version available</td>
<td>1.15: Node pool <br>1.15.12-gke.3 or higher</td>
<td>June 23, 2020</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.16: Node pool <br>1.16.9-gke.6 or higher</td>
<td>June 30, 2020</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Rapid</td>
<td>Patch will be applied automatically</td>
<td>Master and node pool 1.17.6.gke-4 or higher</td>
<td>June 16, 2020</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Regular</td>
<td>Patch will be applied automatically</td>
<td>Node pool 1.16.9-gke.6 or higher</td>
<td>June 30, 2020</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Stable</td>
<td>No action is required</td>
<td>Patch is not required</td>
<td>N/A</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="June_02_2020" data-text="June 02, 2020" tabindex="-1">June 02, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p><span id="known-2020602">A</span>s part of ensuring better representation of available resources on the node for
e2 burstable node types, GKE has decided to <strong>reduce the allocatable CPU
resources available to schedule user workloads (known as the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-architecture#memory_cpu">node allocatable resources</a>)
on <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-micro</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-small</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-medium</code> machine types.</strong></p>

<h4 id="what_do_i_need_to_know_2" data-text="What do I need to know?" tabindex="-1">What do I need to know?</h4>

<p>Today, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-micro</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-small</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-medium</code> have 1930 mCPU of allocatable
resources for Kubernetes to schedule Pods on per node, and following this change
it will be 940m CPU. Kubernetes uses the node allocatable resources during
scheduling to decide how many Pods it should place on the node. <strong>If your
workloads are currently requesting more CPU resources than what will be
available after upgrading, they may become unscheduled after upgrade.</strong></p>

<p>We are making this change in order to more accurately represent the resources
available in these machine types. These machine types can temporarily burst to 2
vCPUs, but this is not sustained. <strong>The underlying compute capabilities and
resources are not changing</strong>, the machines retain the ability to temporarily
burst to 2 vCPU, this change only affects how many resources the Kubernetes
scheduler considers when allocating Pods to nodes.</p>

<p>When your cluster is <strong>upgraded to 1.14.10-gke.42, 1.15.11-gke.18, 1.16.8-
gke.17, or 1.17.5-gke.5</strong> (whether you perform this
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/upgrading-a-cluster">manually</a>
or you are automatically upgraded), your workloads may become
unscheduled if there are not enough allocatable resources in the cluster.</p>

<h4 id="what_do_i_need_to_do_2" data-text="What do I need to do?" tabindex="-1">What do I need to do?</h4>

<p><strong>Prior to upgrading your nodes to version 1.16.8-gke.17 and 1.17.5-gke.5 or later</strong></p>

<p>Take a moment to review your Pod resource requests. To see the allocated
resources on your node, you can open Kubernetes Engine in the
<a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/list">Google Cloud Console</a> and
select your cluster. On the <strong>Nodes</strong> tab for your cluster, the column
<strong>CPU requested</strong> shows the total CPU requests on the node.</p>

<p>Alternatively, from the command line:</p>

<ol>
<li>Run <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl get nodes</code> to get a list of node names.</li>
<li>Run <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl describe node <var translate="no">node-name</var></code> and look at the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Allocated resources</code> section. Under the column <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Requests</code>, find the row for
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">cpu</code>.</li>
</ol>

<p>If you have nodes of type <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-micro</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-small</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">e2-medium</code> where <strong>more
than 940mCPU is requested</strong>, Pods will be rescheduled onto other nodes after
upgrade. You must have enough <strong>allocatable capacity</strong> on other nodes.</p>

<p>To ensure you have enough allocatable capacity, you can:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Enable auto-scaling</strong> on your node pool. Auto-scaling will automatically
provision the right number of nodes automatically, provided the Pod requests
do not exceed that of the entire node</li>
<li><strong>Increase</strong> the number of nodes in the cluster, or add larger node types if
you have Pods that make CPU requests which exceed the capacity of existing nodes</li>
<li><strong>Decrease</strong> the <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/#resource-requests-and-limits-of-pod-and-container" class="external">resource requests</a> 
made by your workloads on these nodes so that they will still fit after the
upgrade, by modifying the CPU resource requests of the PodSpec. Pods will be
able to burst to the original CPU capacity for short periods as long as
resource limits are not changed.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>After you have upgraded your nodes to versions 1.14.10-gke.42, 1.15.11-gke.18,
1.16.8-gke.17, or 1.17.5-gke.5 or later:</strong></p>

<p>Review the status of your Pods by running <code translate="no" dir="ltr">kubectl get pods</code>.</p>

<p>If any are indicated as <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Pending</code>, it may indicate that there were not enough
resources available to schedule them. <strong>Follow the steps above to either add
more nodes, or reduce the CPU resource requests in the PodSpec.</strong></p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> This release note has been updated since it was originally published. The
update adds affected versions of 1.14 and 1.15.</span></aside></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="May_15_2020" data-text="May 15, 2020" tabindex="-1">May 15, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/concepts-container-threat-detection-overview">Container Threat Detection</a>
is now available in Beta. Container Threat Detection can detect the most common
container runtime attacks and alert you in Security Command Center and
optionally in Cloud Logging. Container Threat Detection includes several
detection capabilities, an analysis tool, and an API.</p>

<p>Container Threat Detection currently supports the following versions on the
Regular and Rapid <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/release-channels">channels</a>:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.15.9-gke.12 and higher</li>
<li>1.16.5-gke.2 and higher</li>
<li>1.17 and higher</li>
</ul>

<p>In a future update, Container Threat Detection will support version 1.14 and the
Stable channel.</p></div>
    </div>

deprecations in 1.16, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/apis-1-16">Kubernetes 1.16 deprecated APIs</a>.</p></div>

      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balancing#lb_subnet">Specifying a VPC subnet</a>
for internal Load Balancer Service IPs is now supported as a per-Service
annotation in GKE clusters 1.16.8-gke.10+ and 1.17+.</p></div>
    </div>

opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more

is now available.</li>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><p>We expect the following changes in the coming weeks. This information is not a
guarantee, but is provided to help you plan for upcoming changes.</p>

<p>Google Kubernetes Engine will gradually upgrade clusters in the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/release-channels">regular channel</a>
to GKE 1.16 beginning in an upcoming release. Read more about API deprecations
in 1.16, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/deprecations/apis-1-16">Kubernetes 1.16 deprecated APIs</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="etcd_default_version_changes" data-text="etcd default version changes" tabindex="-1">etcd default version changes</h4>

<ul>
<li>The default etcd version for new GKE 1.13 and 1.14 clusters is etcd 3.2.27-0-gke.6</li>
<li>The default etcd version for new GKE 1.15 and 1.16 clusters is etcd 3.3.18-0-gke.4</li>
<li>The default etcd version for new GKE 1.17 and higher clusters is etcd 3.4.7-0-gke.1</li>
</ul>

<p>Autoupgrades in existing clusters will occur at a later date.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="node_image_changes_7" data-text="Node image changes" tabindex="-1">Node image changes</h4>

<p><strong>GKE 1.16</strong></p>

<ul>
<li>The Ubuntu image for GKE 1.16 clusters is now <a href="https://storage.googleapis.com/ubuntu-os-gke-cloud/ubuntu-gke-1804-1-16-v20200330.manifest" class="external">ubuntu-gke-1804-1-16-v20200330</a> </li>
<li>The COS image for GKE 1.16 clusters is now <a href="https://cloud.google.com/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m77#cos-77-12371-227-0">cos-77-12371-227-0</a>.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>GKE 1.17</strong></p>

<p>The COS image for GKE 1.17 clusters is now <a href="https://cloud.google.com/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes#cos-stable-81-12871-69-0">cos-81-12871-69-0</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_29_2020" data-text="April 29, 2020" tabindex="-1">April 29, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/ingress-for-anthos">Multi-cluster Ingress</a>
is now Generally Available (GA) for all GKE versions 1.14 and up. Multi-cluster
Ingress provides a Kubernetes-native interface to deploy Ingress resources for
internet traffic across multiple clusters and multiple regions.</p>

<p>Ingress is helpful for use cases including:</p>

<ul>
<li>A global and stable anycast VIP, independent of cluster backends.</li>
<li>Multi-regional and multi-cluster high availability.</li>
<li>Low latency serving of traffic to the closest cluster.</li>
<li>Intelligent and safe traffic management across many clusters.</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_27_2020" data-text="April 27, 2020" tabindex="-1">April 27, 2020</h2>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> This release note has been updated since it was originally published. The
<a href="#issues-20200427">Issues</a> section below was added.</span></aside></div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-runasusername/#set-the-username-for-a-pod">RunAsUsername</a>
feature in 1.17 is now beta and allows specifying the username when running a
Windows container.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><h4 id="issues-20200427" data-text="Known issues with 1.15 and higher" tabindex="-1">Known issues with 1.15 and higher</h4>

<p>A known kernel bug in Linux kernel 4.18, 4.19, 4.20 and 5.0 may cause softlockup
when running eBPF workloads. This may affect nodes with GKE version 1.15 or
higher using cos-77-*, and GKE version 1.15 using Ubuntu. Before the fix is
released, please avoid upgrading nodes to these affected versions if you run
eBPF workloads.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="117_changes" data-text="1.17 Changes" tabindex="-1">1.17 Changes</h4>

<p>The following notable changes are coming in 1.17:</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>The following node labels are deprecated in 1.17:</p>

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Cluster Versions</th>
<th>Deprecated Label</th>
<th>New Label</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td>1.14+</td>
<td>beta.kubernetes.io/os</td>
<td>kubernetes.io/os</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.14+</td>
<td>beta.kubernetes.io/arch</td>
<td>kubernetes.io/arch</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.17+</td>
<td>beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type</td>
<td>node.kubernetes.io/instance-type</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.17+</td>
<td>failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone</td>
<td>topology.kubernetes.io/zone</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.17+</td>
<td>failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region</td>
<td>topology.kubernetes.io/region</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<p>You must identify any node selectors using beta labels and modify them to use GA labels.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><p>Google Kubernetes Engine will gradually upgrade clusters in the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/release-channels">regular channel</a>
to GKE 1.16.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The RuntimeClass scheduler in 1.17 simplifies
<a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/runtime-class/#scheduling">scheduling Windows Pods to appropriate nodes</a></p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>To improve the safety of upgrades and reduce disruption, all new node pools have
surge upgrades turned on by default with the configuration: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">maxSurge=1
maxUnavailable=0</code>. For more information, see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-upgrades#optimizing-surge">Determining your optimal surge configuration</a>.</p>

<p>GKE is also gradually reconfiguring existing node pools to use surge upgrades
with the same configuration. Node pools that already have <code translate="no" dir="ltr">upgrade_settings</code>
defined remain unaffected.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>RBAC in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1alpha1</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta1</code> API versions are deprecated in
1.17 and will no longer be served in 1.20. Update your manifests and API clients
to use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1</code> APIs before 1.20 to avoid any issues.</p></div>
    </div>

      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>

</ul></div>

pools running <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/windows-server-gke">Windows Server</a>

<h2 id="April_10_2020" data-text="April 10, 2020" tabindex="-1">April 10, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><p>Google Kubernetes Engine will gradually upgrade clusters in the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/release-channels">regular channel</a>
to GKE 1.16 beginning on or after April 13, 2020.</p></div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>HTTP access logging for newly created Ingress resources is being deprecated
across various GKE versions on May 12th, 2020. Any new Ingress resources created
with the following versions after May 12th will have access logging disabled for
that Ingress resource and will not record Ingress HTTP requests in Cloud
Logging. Note that existing Ingress resources will continue to log HTTP requests
unless the Ingress resource is redeployed. The following GKE versions are
affected:</p>

<ul>
<li>1.12</li>
<li>1.13</li>
<li>1.14 clusters less than 1.14.10-gke.30</li>
<li>1.15 clusters less than 1.15.9-gke.22</li>
<li>1.16 clusters less than 1.16.6-gke.12</li>
</ul>

<p>Clusters whose masters are on 1.14.10-gke.30, 1.15.9-gke.22, 1.16.6-gke.12 or
later versions are not impacted and HTTP access logging remains defaulted to
&quot;on&quot; for all new and existing Ingress resources. If you&#39;re currently using
access logging for GKE Ingress, we highly recommend upgrading to these versions
or higher before May 12th to avoid loss of HTTP access logs for new Ingress
resources.</p>

<p>In GKE 1.18, access logging will be changed to default to &quot;off&quot; for the GKE
Ingress. <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/backendconfig#logconfig">Enabling access logging</a>
through the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">logging</code> parameter is required to enable it for Ingress resources.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-backend-service#logconfig">Ingress access logging</a>
is now a configurable feature called <code translate="no" dir="ltr">logging</code> in versions 1.16.8-gke.10 and
later. This allows Ingress access logging to be toggled on or off through the
BackendConfig resource.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> This release note has been updated since it was originally published. The
<a href="#coming-soon-20200410">Coming soon</a> section below was added.</span></aside></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="April_07_2020" data-text="April 07, 2020" tabindex="-1">April 07, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p><span id="known-20200407">D</span>ue to the recent Windows Server <a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/virtualization/windowscontainers/deploy-containers/update-containers#host-and-container-version-compatibility" class="external">security update</a> provided by Microsoft in February 2020, a
<a href="https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/help/4542617/you-might-encounter-issues-when-using-windows-server-containers-with-t" class="external">container incompatibility issue</a> 
was introduced. To avoid disruption to your workloads, we have turned off
Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) auto-upgrade for the impacted clusters.</p>

<h4 id="what_do_i_need_to_know_3" data-text="What do I need to know?" tabindex="-1">What do I need to know?</h4>

<p>As a consequence of Microsoft&#39;s security update, your workloads may end up in a
failed state due to broken compatibility if the host Windows Server image has
the security update and the container base image does not have the update.</p>

<p><strong>We have turned off auto-upgrade on the impacted GKE clusters to prevent this
compatibility issue from affecting your workloads.</strong></p>

<p>The security update will be available in the rapid channel in GKE starting April
6, 2020. Beginning April 20, 2020, Windows Server container support in GKE,
along with the security update will be available on the regular channel.</p>

<h4 id="what_do_i_need_to_do_3" data-text="What do I need to do?" tabindex="-1">What do I need to do?</h4>

<p>We strongly recommend you to <strong>rebuild your container images with the
<a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/virtualization/windowscontainers/manage-containers/container-base-images" class="external">base Windows images</a> 
that include Windows Updates from March 2020, then manually upgrade your node
pool to the latest GKE version.</strong> Please follow the following steps:</p>

<ol>
<li><strong><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-auto-upgrades#disable">Disable auto-upgrade</a>
on the Windows node pool(s).</strong></li>
<li>When the first step is complete, <strong>Google will restart the cluster
auto-upgrade. Please note that this could take a few days.</strong> The cluster&#39;s
master and the Linux node pool(s) will be upgraded. The Windows node pool
will not get upgraded as auto-upgrade is disabled in step number one.</li>
<li>After the cluster master upgrade is complete and you have rebuilt your
container images, <strong><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/upgrading-a-cluster">manually upgrade your Windows node pool</a></strong>.</li>
<li><strong>After completing step number three, you can turn back on the auto-upgrade
option.</strong> If you choose to turn the auto-upgrade option back on, please use
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/creating-a-cluster-windows#building_multi-arch_images">multi-arch</a>
(or multi-platform) images to take advantage of the auto-upgrade feature.</li>
</ol>

<p>Incompatibility issues such as this one are a rare occurrence as it is against
Microsoft&#39;s typical guidance for the security updates. Rest assured that if such
issues occur again, we will keep you posted. Please stay up to date with
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes">GKE&#39;s release notes</a>
for the latest info.</p>

<p>If you have any questions or require assistance, <strong>please <a href="mailto:GKE-Windows@google.com">email us</a>
or contact <a href="https://support.google.com/cloud/contactflow">Google Cloud Support</a>.</strong></p></div>

      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/enable-tpus">Enabling TPUs on existing clusters</a>
is now in Beta. With this feature you can toggle Cloud TPU support instead of
creating new clusters and migrating your workloads.</p></div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/workload-identity">Workload Identity</a>
is now generally available in versions 1.14.10-gke.27 and
above, 1.15.9-gke.22 and above, and 1.16.6-gke.12 and above. Workload Identity
is the recommended way to access Google Cloud services from within GKE clusters.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes#february_14_2020">issue reported February 14</a>
with private clusters with <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/private-cluster-concept#network_peering_reuse">VPC peering reuse</a>
enabled has been resolved.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="March_06_2020" data-text="March 06, 2020" tabindex="-1">March 06, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-announcement">Announcement</span>
      <div><p>1.16 will be moving to the Regular channel.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now configure automated deployment for your <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/automated-deployment">existing GKE workloads</a>
with Cloud Build.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>The 1.16 release stops serving the following API versions in favor of newer and
more stable API versions:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">NetworkPolicy</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">extensions/v1beta1</code> API version, deprecated since
1.9, is no longer served. Migrate to the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">networking.k8s.io/v1</code> API version,
available since 1.8.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">PodSecurityPolicy</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">extensions/v1beta1</code> API version, deprecated
 since 1.10, is no longer served. Migrate to the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">policy/v1beta1</code> API
 version, available since 1.10.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">DaemonSet</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">extensions/v1beta1</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta1</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta2</code>
API versions, deprecated since 1.9, is no longer served. Migrate to the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1</code> API version, available since 1.9. Notable changes:
<ul>
<li>spec.templateGeneration is removed.</li>
<li>spec.selector is now required and immutable after creation; use the
existing template labels as the selector for seamless upgrades.</li>
<li>spec.updateStrategy.type now defaults to RollingUpdate.</li>
</ul></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">Deployment</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">extensions/v1beta1</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta1</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta2</code>
API versions, deprecated since 1.9, is no longer served. Migrate to the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1</code> API version, available since 1.9. Notable changes:
<ul>
<li>spec.rollbackTo is removed.</li>
<li>spec.selector is now required and immutable after creation; use the
existing template labels as the selector for seamless upgrades.</li>
<li>spec.progressDeadlineSeconds now defaults to 600 seconds.</li>
<li>spec.revisionHistoryLimit now defaults to 10.</li>
<li>maxSurge and maxUnavailable now default to 25%.</li>
</ul></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">StatefulSet</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta1</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta2</code> API versions,
deprecated since 1.9, is no longer served. Migrate to the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1 API version</code>,
available since 1.9. Notable changes:
<ul>
<li>spec.selector is now required and immutable after creation; use the
existing template labels as the selector for seamless upgrades.</li>
<li>spec.updateStrategy.type now defaults to RollingUpdate.</li>
</ul></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">ReplicaSet</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">extensions/v1beta1</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta1</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta2</code>
API versions, deprecated since 1.9, is no longer served. Migrate to the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1</code>
API version, available since 1.9. Notable changes:
<ul>

existing template labels as the selector for seamless upgrades.</li>

<h2 id="February_27_2020" data-text="February 27, 2020" tabindex="-1">February 27, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/standalone-neg">Container-native load balancing with standalone network endpoint groups (NEGs)</a>
is generally available. You can use Standalone NEGs to create load balancers for
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/standalone-neg#use_cases_of_standalone_negs">several use cases</a>
including backends composed of Kubernetes and non-Kubernetes workloads.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/ingress-for-anthos">Ingress for Anthos</a>
is now Beta for GKE versions 1.14.x+ and in the Rapid and Regular release
channels. Ingress for Anthos supports Internet-facing Ingress shared across
multiple backend GKE clusters and multiple Google Cloud regions. Ingress can now
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/multi-cluster-ingress">support</a>
use cases such as multi-regional and multi-cluster availability, low backend to
user latency, and seamless cluster migrations.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_25_2020" data-text="February 25, 2020" tabindex="-1">February 25, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-deprecated">Deprecated</span>
      <div><p>The v1.16 release stops serving the following API versions in favor of newer and
more stable API versions:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">NetworkPolicy</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">extensions/v1beta1</code> API version, deprecated since
1.9, is no longer served. Migrate to the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">networking.k8s.io/v1</code> API version,
available since 1.8.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">PodSecurityPolicy</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">extensions/v1beta1</code> API version, deprecated
since 1.10, is no longer served. Migrate to the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">policy/v1beta1</code> API version,
available since 1.10.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">DaemonSet</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">extensions/v1beta1</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta1</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta2</code>
API versions, deprecated since 1.9, is no longer served. Migrate to the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1</code> API version, available since 1.9. Notable changes:
<ul>
<li>spec.templateGeneration is removed.</li>
<li>spec.selector is now required and immutable after creation; use the
existing template labels as the selector for seamless upgrades.</li>
<li>spec.updateStrategy.type now defaults to RollingUpdate.</li>
</ul></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">Deployment</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">extensions/v1beta1</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta1</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta2</code>
API versions, deprecated since 1.9, is no longer served. Migrate to the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1</code> API version, available since 1.9. Notable changes:
<ul>
<li>spec.rollbackTo is removed.</li>
<li>spec.selector is now required and immutable after creation; use the
existing template labels as the selector for seamless upgrades.</li>
<li>spec.progressDeadlineSeconds now defaults to 600 seconds.</li>
<li>spec.revisionHistoryLimit now defaults to 10.</li>
<li>maxSurge and maxUnavailable now default to 25%.</li>
</ul></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">StatefulSet</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta1</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta2</code> API versions,
deprecated since 1.9, is no longer served. Migrate to the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1 API version</code>,
available since 1.9. Notable changes:
<ul>
<li>spec.selector is now required and immutable after creation; use the
existing template labels as the selector for seamless upgrades.</li>
<li>spec.updateStrategy.type now defaults to RollingUpdate.</li>
</ul></li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">ReplicaSet</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">extensions/v1beta1</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta1</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">apps/v1beta2</code>

<ul>
<li>spec.selector is now required and immutable after creation; use the
existing template labels as the selector for seamless upgrades.</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></div>

      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones">region</a> us-west3 in
Salt Lake City is now available.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The ability to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gce-pd-csi-driver">use the Google Cloud Compute Engine Persistent Disk CSI driver in GKE</a>
is now in Beta. This feature provides a simple mechanism for users to enable the
driver in GKE.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/ingress-ilb">Ingress for Internal HTTP(S) Load Balancing</a>
is now available in Beta in the Rapid release channel. This enables private L7
load balancing inside the VPC that can be deployed with Ingress resources.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="February_21_2020" data-text="February 21, 2020" tabindex="-1">February 21, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-breaking">Breaking</span>
      <div><p>Starting February 24, 2020, GKE will gradually enable
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/node-auto-upgrades">Node Auto Upgrade</a>
on all nodepools running on version 1.10.x and older to ensure
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes-archive#important_information_about_v110x_nodes">reliability and supportability</a>
of these clusters.</p></div>
    </div>

<h2 id="February_14_2020" data-text="February 14, 2020" tabindex="-1">February 14, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p><span id="known-20200214">P</span>rivate clusters created on and after January 15, 2020 that use
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/private-cluster-concept#network_peering_reuse">VPC peering reuse</a> might experience an issue where VPC peering is removed after attempting to reschedule a cluster for deletion after the first attempt fails.</p>

<p>To mitigate this issue, create a private cluster in the same location as your
existing private clusters. Creating a new cluster recreates the required VPC
peering. You can delete the new cluster after VPC peering is recreated.</p></div>
    </div>

    </div>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/cluster-autoscaler#autoscaling_profiles">Autoscaling profiles</a>
for GKE are now available in Beta. Autoscaling profiles let you choose whether
the cluster autoscaler should optimize for resource utilization or resource
availability when deciding to remove nodes from a cluster.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>All GKE clusters running 1.15 and up will have etcd upgraded to
<strong>etcd 3.3.18-0-gke.1</strong>, and all new GKE clusters with 1.15 and up will be
created with <strong>etcd 3.3.18-0-gke.1</strong>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_29_2020" data-text="January 29, 2020" tabindex="-1">January 29, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="version_updates_9" data-text="Version updates" tabindex="-1">Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<h5 id="scheduled_automatic_upgrades_8" data-text="Scheduled automatic upgrades" tabindex="-1">Scheduled automatic upgrades</h5>

<p>Masters and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded:</p>

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Current version</th>
<th>Upgrade version</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td>1.12.x</td>
<td>1.13.12-gke.13</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.14.0.x to 1.14.8-gke.32</td>
<td>1.14.8-gke.33</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.14.9.x to 1.14.9-gke.22</td>
<td>1.14.9-gke.23</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.14.10.x to 1.14.10-gke.16</td>
<td>1.14.10-gke.17</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<p>Rollouts are phased across multiple weeks, to ensure cluster and fleet stability.</p>

<h6 id="new_versions_available_for_upgrades_and_new_clusters_9" data-text="New versions available for upgrades and new clusters" tabindex="-1">New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</h6>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on the Kubernetes versioning scheme, see <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">Versioning</a>.</p>
<div class="ds-selector-tabs" data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="no-channel_244" data-text="No channel" tabindex="-1">No channel</h3><h5 id="v113x_6" data-text="v.1.13.x" tabindex="-1">v.1.13.x</h5>

<ul>
<li>1.15.8-gke.2</li>
</ul></section>

<ul>
<li>1.14.7-gke.40</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/config-connector/docs/overview">Config Connector</a> is
now generally available. Config Connector is a GKE addon that allows you to
manage your Google Cloud resources through Kubernetes configuration.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/sandbox-pods">GKE Sandbox</a>
is now generally available. GKE Sandbox protects the host kernel on your nodes
when containers in the Pod execute unknown or untrusted code.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/config-sync/overview">Config Sync</a>
is now generally available. Config Sync allows you to manage Kubernetes
deployments using files stored in a Git repository.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_27_2020" data-text="January 27, 2020" tabindex="-1">January 27, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The ability to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/creating-a-cluster-windows">create clusters with node pools running Microsoft Windows Server</a>
is now in Beta. This feature is currently only available in the Rapid release
channel.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_24_2020" data-text="January 24, 2020" tabindex="-1">January 24, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-fixed">Fixed</span>
      <div><p><strong>This issue was resolved January 27, 2020.</strong></p>

<p><del><strong>Do not create a cluster with versions 1.15.7-gke.23, 1.14.10-gke.17, or
1.14.9-gke.23 if you depend on Workload Identity.</strong> Workload Identity is not
working for newly created clusters in these versions due to a
recently-discovered issue. Clusters upgraded to one of these versions are not
affected. A fix will be released in the next GKE release. As workaround, you can
create a cluster at a lower version, then upgrade.</del></p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>The <a href="https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones">region</a> asia-northeast3
in Seoul is now available.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_22_2020" data-text="January 22, 2020" tabindex="-1">January 22, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> This release note has been updated since it was originally published.
The <a href="#node-changes-20200122">Node image changes</a> section below was added.</span></aside></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="node_image_changes" data-text="Node image changes" tabindex="-1">Node image changes</h4>

<p>The COS kernel previously reported on November 22nd, 2019, was discovered to
cause kernel panics in certain workloads. The 1.13 and 1.14 versions available
in this release were rolled back to a known stable version of COS. GKE 1.13 and
1.14 will continue to use cos-u-73-11647-293-0 while our team works to develop a
permanent fix.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>All private clusters you create now <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/private-cluster-concept#network_peering_reuse">reuse VPC Network Peering connections</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="version_updates_10" data-text="Version updates" tabindex="-1">Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<h5 id="new_default_version_4" data-text="New default version" tabindex="-1">New default version</h5>

<p>The default version for new clusters is now 1.13.11-gke.23.</p>

<h5 id="scheduled_automatic_upgrades_9" data-text="Scheduled automatic upgrades" tabindex="-1">Scheduled automatic upgrades</h5>

<p>Masters and nodes with auto-upgrade enabled will be upgraded:</p>

<th>Upgrade version</th>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.15.x</td>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<p>Rollouts are phased across multiple weeks, to ensure cluster and fleet stability.</p>

    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/nodelocal-dns-cache">NodeLocal DNSCache</a>
is now in Beta for GKE clusters 1.15 and above. NodeLocal DNS is an optional
feature for local DNS resolution to every GKE node for enhanced DNS scale and capacity.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/object/browser">Object Browser</a> is
now available to inspect resources on GKE clusters in Google Cloud Console. For
more information, go to <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/dashboards#object_browser">Dashboards</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/add-on/application-delivery">Application Delivery</a>
is now in Beta. This feature manages configurations for your GKE workloads
declaratively with Git. For more information, see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/add-on/application-delivery">Application Delivery</a>.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_08_2020" data-text="January 08, 2020" tabindex="-1">January 08, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-issue">Issue</span>
      <div><p><strong>Do not update to version 1.16.0-gke.20 if you depend on HPA.</strong>
Horizontal Pod Autoscaling is not working in this version due to a recently
discovered issue. A fix will be released with GKE 1.16.3+.</p></div>
    </div>
<h2 id="January_07_2020" data-text="January 07, 2020" tabindex="-1">January 07, 2020</h2>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p>You can now use <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/using-cmek">Customer-managed encryption keys (beta)</a> to control the encryption used for node boot disks as well as attached persistent disks in your clusters.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-feature">Feature</span>
      <div><p><a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/consuming-reservations">Consuming reservations in GKE</a> is now generally available. Reservations allow you to reserve resources in a specific zone to ensure sufficient capacity is available for your workloads.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><h4 id="version_updates_11" data-text="Version updates" tabindex="-1">Version updates</h4>

<p>GKE cluster versions have been updated.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Your clusters might not have these versions available. Rollouts begin on
the day of the note and take four or more business days to be completed across
all Google Cloud zones.</span></aside>
<h5 id="new_default_version_5" data-text="New default version" tabindex="-1">New default version</h5>

<p>The default version for new clusters is now 1.14.8-gke.12 (previously 1.13.11-gke.14).</p>

<h5 id="new_versions_available_for_upgrades_and_new_clusters_11" data-text="New versions available for upgrades and new clusters" tabindex="-1">New versions available for upgrades and new clusters</h5>

<p>The following Kubernetes versions are now available for new clusters and for
opt-in control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more
information on the Kubernetes versioning scheme, see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/versioning">Versioning</a>.</p>

<ul>
<li>1.12.10-gke.17</li>
<li>1.12.10-gke.20</li>
<li>1.12.10-gke.22</li>
</ul></div>
    </div>
    <div class="devsite-release-note">
      <span class="devsite-label devsite-label-release-changed">Change</span>
      <div><p>New clusters and node-pools created with the GKE API will have node auto-upgrade
enabled by default. This change ensures that your clusters have the most recent
default Kubernetes version, bug fixes, and security patches. Existing scripts
running against the gcloud CLI or integrating with the GKE API will follow this
new default behavior.</p>

<p>Node autoupgrades keep the nodes in your cluster up to date with the cluster
master version when your master is updated on your behalf. To disable it
explicitly, set <code translate="no" dir="ltr">autoUpgrade</code> to false in the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/reference/rest/v1/NodeManagement">NodeManagement</a>
object.</p></div>
    </div>



      
    </section>
